Thanks for playing. Roll well.

apps.name: Hotline Navigator
apps.subtitle: Official Website
apps.localizedDescription:
Hotline Navigator:

Official Website.

What the hell is Hotline?:

Hotline in concept, was to replicate a BBS but for the internet age. Modern users would recongize more as a proto peer-to-peer or a Discord like application.

Hotline's Navigator's website has a deeper drive the history of Hotline.

Platform Support:

Right now the iOS, iPadOS, and Android versions are not in their respective app stores and must be built manually or sideloaded.

This is a Tauri-based Hotline client that provides a modern, cross-platform experience for the classic Hotline protocol. Built with React and Rust, it offers:

• Cross-Platform: Single codebase for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, iPadOS, and Android.
• Modern Stack: React + TypeScript frontend, Rust backend.

• Native Performance: Tauri's lightweight architecture for fast, efficient apps.

versions.localizedDescription:
v0.2.8:

There's been a lot of rapid changes in Navigator's capabilities so this release UX quality-of-life series of fixes since the Discord style chat introduced a new UX paradigm which inevitable had some loose ends.

Disconnects are detected in seconds instead of minutes, chat icons no longer fall back to gray letter placeholders for emotes or for users who chatted before their info loaded, and! / / commands now appear above the bot's response instead of below it. News browsing also works on multi-tier servers like VesperNet, where top-level entries are folders of folders.

Next release will be new feature bound.

Bugfixes and Improvements:

• Faster disconnect detection — When a server vanishes silently (peer crash, network drop, NAT timeout), the client now notices in ~60s on macOS/Linux and ~130s on Windows, down from the OS TCP retransmit default of 15+ minutes. Auto-reconnect kicks in correspondingly faster.

• News browsing on nested servers — On servers like VesperNet where the top-level news entries are folders containing more folders, navigation no longer dead-ends with an empty article pane. The client now dispatches based on the clicked item's actual type (bundle vs. category) rather than assuming any non-root path holds articles.

Technical:

• TCP SO_KEEPALIVE configured on the control channel via socket2: idle=30s, interval=10s, retries=3 on macOS/Linux. Windows uses the OS default retry count.
• App-level keepalive failure now emits StatusChanged(Disconnected) and clears the transport, instead of silently breaking.

• Optimistic insert tagged with pending: true and optimisticKey; echo dedup matches by userName + message text within a 10s window. /me and /em are preformatted as *** name action to match the server echo. 30s safety timeout clears the pending flag if no echo arrives.
• News load effect dispatches on a tracked newsLeafType (2 = bundle → get_news_categories; 3 = category → get_news_articles). Going back always sets leaf type to bundle, since non-leaf path segments are bundles by invariant.

Download the installer for your platform from the release assets.

.dmg = macOS, .msi/.exe = Windows, .apk = Android, .ipa = iOS/iPadOS, Linux hippies can figure it out.

apps.subtitle: Ported scrcpy for mobile platforms, to remotely control Android devices on your iPhone or Android phone

versions.localizedDescription:
Built on scrcpy v4.0 (SDL3 + FFmpeg 8.1.1).

Fixes:

Mirrored picture geometry.

• Fix the picture overflowing the window and not being draggable back. The porting layer applied SDL_SetRenderScale(nativeScale) on top of the density conversion scrcpy v4 already performs, magnifying the geometry by density × nativeScale (4× on @2x, 9× on @3x).
• Fix the picture being offset to one side from the moment a session connects. The Stage Manager resize path compared the view size in pixels against SDL_GetWindowSize(), which SDL3 reports in points, so the sizes never matched and every layout pass pushed a resize event carrying a pixel-sized geometry.

Black screen on high-contrast scene changes.

• A full display-layer queue is normal back-pressure; it no longer escalates to flushing the queue and restarting the server-side encoder after 5 dropped frames. Recovery now requires a sustained stall, and the reset cooldown was raised so a second reset cannot land before the previous restart has produced a keyframe.

Disk filling with logs.

• The active log file is now bounded at runtime (previously only older files were cleaned, and only at cold start — one user reported a single 76 GB log).
• Decoder and render error logs are rate-limited; they previously wrote one line per packet or per frame for as long as the error persisted.

Crashes and background behaviour.

• Fix SIGTRAP/SIGABRT during teardown (sc_server_destroy, sc_main_thread_destroy, sc_screen_destroy/sc_fps_counter_destroy) when a session is re-entered in the same process.
• Fix the background timeout ignoring the configured duration, and a background-task handle leak that could disconnect an already-disconnected session.
• Fix a VNC connect crash and a blank screen after ADB disconnect.

The attached IPA is Ad Hoc signed and installs only on devices registered to the developer account. For general use, install via TestFlight or the App Store.

versions.localizedDescription:
Theft4 0.3.2 — potential BC texture preparation fix:

Version 0.3.2 · build 144 · iPhone and iPad · 2026-10-14.

I don't have an older phone, so I cannot test these changes on one. Your mileage may vary (YMMV).

Getting “No BC textures found”? Check this first:

The first thing to check is a missing or misplaced aes_key.bin. This has now been confirmed in a 0.3.2 user log. Your game files can be present, but Theft4 needs this small file to read the texture archives. If the log says “Archive AES key is unavailable,” the app did not load the required key; this does not establish a phone/GPU problem.

Copy aes_key.bin from your validated, prepared game folder into the same folder as default.xex and default.xexp on your device. It should be named exactly aes_key.bin and be 32 bytes. Do not put it inside an extra nested folder.

If you use LiveContainer, make sure the file is in the game folder used by the copy of Theft4 inside LiveContainer.

Then close and reopen Theft4 and retry texture preparation. Version 0.3.2 will rescan after the key is restored. If it still fails, export a new log using System → Download Latest Log Capture and include your device model, iOS/app version and exact error.

What changed:

• A scan that finds zero textures is scanned again on retry instead of repeatedly reusing a failed result.
• Restoring or replacing aes_key.bin invalidates the saved source scan. Older scan identities are refreshed once; existing converted textures can still be reused by their content keys.
• Empty-scan errors now show the source-file count, resources decoded, warning count and first underlying archive/resource warning.

Update and retry:

• Update the existing app in place. Do not delete it: deletion removes its private saves and caches.
• Open Theft4, check the game files, and retry texture preparation if your GPU requires it. Allow a fresh source scan; completed conversion files remain reusable.
• Keep Theft4 open during preparation, preferably on power. Allow roughly 2.4 GB for prepared textures plus additional free working space. Pause/resume retains completed conversions.

Bug reports need logs and information:

• Exact device model, iOS/iPadOS version, and Theft4 version/build.
• Exact error text or a screenshot, the failing setup step, and whether retry changes it.
• Game platform/region/media ID, base version, exact TU8 source/patch hash, and how the game folder was staged and transferred. Do not upload game files or the AES key.
• Free device storage and steps needed to reproduce the problem.

Validation and limitations:

IPA SHA-256: 8f7d3a2865a10f34af0cdd736ee66677ac2614207651d60267d61a47cced9f57.

No physical iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 13 Pro, or other older-phone test was performed for this release. Host tests and compilation do not confirm the initial cause on an affected phone. Please provide diagnostics if the issue persists.

apps.subtitle: A roguelike built on the real Mega Man Battle Network 6, from your own ROM: every run jacks MegaMan into a newly generated net of battles, loot and guardian Navis
apps.localizedDescription:
· Player's guide · Project page · Discussions.

You need your own ROM: Mega Man Battle Network 6: Cybeast Gregar (USA), unmodified. Battle Network 5: Team Colonel (USA) beside it is optional. No download and no page contains Capcom data; without the ROM there is no game. What the game checks.

·.

· For developers · Buy me a coffee.

versions.localizedDescription:
BN5's net, fought in BN6's engine:

In 0.11, a battle in one of BN5's areas handed the screen to a second emulator running BN5 itself, with its own rules, its own HUD and no Crosses. Now every battle is BN6's. BN5's 25 virus families that BN6 lacks are moved from your BN5 ROM into BN6's battle engine by their own code, and each was checked frame by frame against BN5's own battles before it shipped. They fight beside BN6's HUD and Custom screen, and everything MegaMan carries works against them.

BN5's guardians:

ToadMan, KnightMan, ShadowMan, NumberMan, TomahawkMan and Colonel guard acts in BN5's areas, fought in BN6's engine at BN6's guardians' strength, no longer three quarters of it. So does the Dark Soul.

Souls, in every battle:

A BN5 guardian deleted gives his Soul for the run. UNITE on the Custom screen, giving up a chip of the Soul's kind, makes MegaMan that Soul for three turns, in any battle, BN6's areas too: its look, its charged shot and its passive, as BN5 has them. One form at a time: UNITE and Beast Out share the emblem's slot. Chaos Unison goes as BN5's does: a DarkChip comes while MegaMan worries, and UNITE stays dark while he does, so keep it, calm him with a chip that lands, and give it up on the next Custom screen. A DarkChip given up for Chaos Unison costs no max HP.

DarkChips from the flames:

BN5's flames of darkness stand on its areas' layers, and their DarkChips come by BN5's rule: dealt while MegaMan is worried, at a quarter of his HP or hit again and again. Every battle a DarkChip runs in costs 20 max HP for the rest of the dive, and MegaMan says so before you take one. DarkInvs hands MegaMan to the game for ten seconds, grey and untouchable, as BN5's does. DarkPlus adds 50 to the next chip.

Lava and sea:

BN5's lava and sea panels work in BN6's battles as they do in BN5: lava burns what stands on it unless it is Fire, and the sea holds back whatever is not Aqua.

Where the nets meet:

From act 2, a battle in four may bring a visitor from the other net: BN5's viruses in BN6's areas, BN6's in BN5's. The deep acts draw from both nets, and BN5's chips are chips of the run, one chip per name, in shops, traders, rewards and Mystery Data.

On the New 3DS too:

The New 3DS reads BN5's ROM where its heap has room for it. Put Team Colonel beside BN6's ROM and BN5's net joins your runs there as everywhere else. A 3DS without BN5 gets 16 MB of its heap back.

🎮 A smoother New 3DS:

• No freeze at a save. A checkpoint wrote its ten files on the frame that saved, and on the 3DS's SD card that held the game still for up to a second at every layer. A thread of its own writes them now. In a six-minute run on a New 3DS, the stalls of 0.6 to 1.5 seconds went from 20 to none.
• The act's card at full speed. Its text went through the software renderer one letter at a time, and the card dropped the game to about 40 frames a second as it showed. A line of text is drawn once and blended whole now: the seconds with the card on screen ran at 56.6 frames a second, up from 40.8.

🌐 The site in Japanese:

The home page, the downloads, the FAQ and the browser player have Japanese pages, written for Japan's players, who know the game as ロックマンエグゼ6, with BN6's names as Capcom's Japanese releases write them.

Under the hood:

BN5's battles in BN6's engine are held to BN5's own by a differential: each of 366 specs fights the same battle in BN5's engine and in BN6's and compares them frame by frame. 363 pass, and the three others stop where they are recorded to. Each of 167 deliberate breaks in the moved code fails its spec. The repository holds numbers only (addresses, ids, checksums); everything BN5's comes from your ROM as the game starts.

You'll need to provide your own Halo: CE XISO, which the app imports right on your device.

versions.localizedDescription:
Halo: CE 0.1.2 (build 6) renders at native display resolution by default and keeps iPhone/iPad gameplay and importing in landscape.

• Retina drawable and matching internal color/depth render targets. The HUD and touch controls retain their original logical size.

• screen_width = 0 fits the display; 640 selects original 4:3 framing. See display settings.
• Landscape-only orientation masks and a full-screen orientation-lock request on recent iPadOS versions.
• In-app importing of your own original Xbox Halo XISO, the Halo: CE icon, touch controls, and hidden debug overlays remain included.

Download Halo-CE-iOS-unsigned.ipa, sign it with your own Apple account/profile, and install it. The IPA is unsigned and cannot be installed directly. Keep your existing bundle identifier when updating to retain app data. Back up the save folder before uninstalling.

Halo-CE-simulator.zip is an ARM64 simulator app for Apple Silicon Macs. The .sha256 file verifies the IPA download. See the build and installation guide.

Validation and limitations:

A signed build 6 was installed on a physical iPad Pro 13-inch (M5). Its renderer reported 2752 × 2064; the complete landscape menu was visible, and the player confirmed turning the iPad upright keeps Halo horizontal with all controls visible. All three persistent save files matched their pre-update SHA-256 hashes. The preceding build imported a real NTSC-US XISO on this iPad and reached the opening campaign scene.

Build 6 was also installed and launched on a physical iPhone 17 Pro Max. Its renderer reported 2868 × 1320, a screenshot showed the complete landscape profile menu and controls, and all three persistent save files matched their pre-update SHA-256 hashes. The earlier runtime was played with audible sound on this phone. Native-resolution campaign performance, prolonged play, older devices/OS versions, physical controllers, and multiplayer remain unverified. Anti-aliasing and an in-app graphics settings menu are not implemented yet. Bink intro videos are unsupported.

An iPadOS 27 beta simulator cold-started with a portrait canvas that cropped landscape content despite a landscape scene. This did not occur in the physical iPad session. See the validation record for coverage and remaining limitations.

Thanks to cybersecurity/halo-ce-universal, bnunu/halo-1, punpckhdq/halo, and their contributors. This product includes software developed by in. This is an unofficial community port, unaffiliated with the Halo rights holders.

It runs the game's own code, so it plays, sounds and feels like the PAL PlayStation 2 game. There are extras, such as a sharper picture, widescreen and smoother motion. The sharper picture, widescreen and the other picture extras stay off until you turn them on, and the frame rate is not held to the PS2's unless you choose Original. The mouse camera starts on.

versions.localizedDescription:
Please note: this release changes how the game draws nearly everything, and it has had only limited testing: one phone and automated checks. It may run slower, or look wrong, on a computer, phone or Mac it has not been tried on. If it does, keep the previous version and send the game's log file with a short description of what you saw. The log says what the game chose for your device.

New:

• The log now lists, every 10 seconds, how many drawing steps the game takes for each picture, which steps take the graphics card longest, and what kind of graphics card the game found (named in the first lines). If the game is slow, send the log with your report.
• On Android phones and handhelds and on Apple Silicon Macs, the fog, some see-through effects and the glow blur are drawn in fewer steps, with the same picture.
• The 3D scenery, the shadows and the glow are drawn in fewer steps that give the same picture; the game's log says which steps each device takes.

Fixed:

• Blending between see-through things and what is behind them now uses the graphics card's own mixing on every computer, phone and Mac, as the game did up to v0.5.2. A few mixed colours can come out one shade lighter than on the PlayStation 2, which the eye cannot tell apart. The more exact mixing of v0.6.0 to v0.7.9 took many more drawing steps on some cards and is now a developer switch. On cards that used it, the game also has fewer graphics programs to prepare at the first start.
• With the Original picture, textures that have several detail levels are now filtered by the graphics card instead of by a hand-written filter. The picture is the same to the eye; at the edges of cut-out textures such as leaves and grilles a single pixel can differ from the PlayStation 2.
• On computers, the 3D scenery is drawn by a leaner method that gives the same picture; a driver that cannot handle it is noticed at start and the old way is taken. Phones and handhelds draw it as before.
• On the AYN Thor and the AYN Odin 2 Portal the game prepares its graphics at the first start again, in small steps.
• On Android, the start after the graphics driver stopped responding now runs with extra checks.
• The game has fewer graphics programs to prepare at the first start.
• The settings vu_plain_only and vu_extended in config.toml are no longer used. You can delete them.

apps.localizedDescription:
Just Volleyball - iOS build:

Godot 4.7.2 project plus a GitHub Actions pipeline that produces an unsigned .ipa on GitHub's macOS runners. You do not need a Mac and you do not need an Apple Developer account to get the file; you only need an Apple ID on the device to sign it at install time.

• Fallback: the same file is attached to every run under Actions -> iOS -> Artifacts (just-volleyball-unsigned-ipa), for 90 days.
• Target: iOS 15+, iPhone and iPad, landscape only.
• Device requirement: A12 or newer (iPhone XS/XR and later, any current iPad). Godot's Metal renderer declares the iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12 capability, so older devices will refuse to install it.

versions.localizedDescription:
All six complaints were real, and each one is fixed at the cause:

• Replays: tap to skip. The skip was read from the accept key, which a phone has no way to press, so the vote could not be cast there at all. Any tap during a replay now casts it, and the banner names the gesture the device actually has ("tap to skip" on a phone, "space to skip" on a desktop). A tap also pauses and resumes inside the replay viewer.
• Round movement wheel. The wheel's base was built with its corner radius at the default of 0, which draws square corners, so the circular stick sat on a flat card. It is now the same disc as its rim and knob, and the "move" label is gone.
• No more frozen yellow. The yellow slab is the transition cover, and the next scene used to be loaded synchronously underneath it: the loading thread is the main thread, so the cover could not animate and a big venue read as a hang. Scenes now load on a worker thread while the cover runs a progress bar, the sweeps are shorter (about 0.33 s in, 0.2 s out), and the cover holds until the incoming scene has actually drawn - the first look at a new screen is a finished one, not a half-built court. The boot intro is about half as long and no longer waits out the full audio sting after its animation has finished.
• Exit really exits. SceneTree.quit() only stops the main loop, and iOS answers it by leaving the app alive on its last frame - that is exactly what an exit button that "freezes for a second instead of closing" is. Saving happens first, then the process is ended, on every exit path (menu confirm, pause menu, launch gate).
• Real saving. Settings, profile and career are flushed when the app is backgrounded (NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED is the only leaving notice a phone gives, and a suspended app can be killed without another word) and before quitting. Progress no longer depends on the 2-minute autosave.
• Easier to start. A touch device that has never been asked starts on the easy CPU preset with aim assist on - a phone has no keyboard and no mouse, so the desktop defaults were the wrong starting point. It happens exactly once, never overrides a deliberate choice (the choice flag is persisted), and both stay ordinary settings you can change.

Not verified by me:

Nothing here was checked on a phone - I have no iOS device. What was verified on the exact released file: the sha256 matches the published .sha256, the headless gate below ran green in CI before the export, and the pack audit passes inside the IPA.

Harmless notes:

• The difficulty/aim-assist preset applies once and never again: if you set a difficulty yourself, that wins forever.
• The gate (tools/verify_transitions.gd) is a headless regression test that CI runs before every export; it caught two real bugs while being written. It runs without a device, so on-device times (how long a venue actually takes now) are still yours to confirm.
• A12 or newer, unsigned, same install method: Sideloadly / AltStore as before.

apps.name: Robrix
apps.subtitle: Robrix: a powerful multi-platform Matrix chat client written in Rust, using the Makepad UI toolkit and Robius platform abstractions
apps.localizedDescription:
Robrix: a Rust Matrix client built atop Robius:

Robrix is a fast, powerful Matrix chat client written from scratch in Rust.

It brings some cool new features to the world of Matrix, like our signature "dockable tabs" layout that lets you view and interact with multiple rooms or threads simultaneously. This works just like your favorite multi-tab IDE or web browser, letting you keep tabs on as many conversations as you want.

versions.localizedDescription:
Cool new features: full navigation history that lets you go back and forward through rooms just like a web browser, swipe gestures to go back (on mobile), support for animated stickers/images, in-app link handling, and more!

We also polished the UI all over the place, from the image viewer and welcome screen to the layout and HTML formatting of messages. Many features were further stabilized in preparation for our full 1.0 release.

Highlights from this release:

• Full navigation history: go back and forward through all the rooms, threads, spaces, etc you've visited, just like a web browser.

• You can use the new back/forward buttons in the window's title bar, your mouse's back/forward buttons, the back gesture on Android, or the back button in mobile view mode.
• Long-press (or click & hold) a back/forward button to show all history and jump to any point.

• New gesture: swipe right to go back, just like most mobile apps.
• Animated images (GIFs, stickers) now play properly in the timeline.
• Robrix properly opens all links in app now: links to rooms, messages in rooms, threads, spaces, etc.
• Brand new image viewer design with modern, sleek overlays for metadata and buttons.
• A new prettier welcome screen with tips for getting started.
• Better, cleaner formatting for messages that wastes less space.

• The left column with avatars and timestamps is narrower, which gives messages about 20 more pixels of width. This is nicer on narrower screens like smaller mobile devices.
• Timestamps always line up perfectly with the first line of each message.
• Paragraphs, lists, and quotes are now spaced better with redundant whitespace getting combined nicely.
• Reactions can now take up all the horizontal space in the timeline instead of wrapping prematurely.
• Hover highlights in lists, menus, and the timeline now use one consistent color, with a hint of blue for better contrast.
• Loading spinners now animate properly on Android, Linux, and Windows, where they used to freeze whenever nothing else on screen was changing.

• The window title bar properly scales with Robrix's UI zoom level.
• Jumping to a message consistently highlights it, and for a longer duration so it's more noticeable.

macOS:

Download and open the .dmg, then drag Robrix to your Applications folder as normal.

iOS and iPadOS:

Join the TestFlight beta at https://testflight.apple.com/join/cQPRgdVY.

Linux:

Ubuntu or Debian (and similar) distros.

Download and open that file in the Software Center (or App Center), or run this in your terminal:

Arch Linux.

Note that the robrix_1.0.0-beta.3_x86_64.tar.gz and robrix_1.0.0-beta.3_aarch64.tar.gz files are just published for use with community-maintained AUR packages (see robrix-bin and robrix-git in that package manager). We can't guarantee they are correct or up-to-date.

AppImage (for any Linux).

What changed in Robrix since the last release:

• Fix regression in makepad that prevents mention popup from showing.
• Open links to rooms, aliases, spaces, and specific events within Robrix.
• Redesign ImageViewer overlay layout to be more modern/sleek.
• Allow reactions to take the full horizontal width of the timeline.
• more visual improvements to the ImageViewer floating overlays.
• Play animated images in the timeline, decode images at their drawn size.
• use sleeker icons with thinner strokes for the imageviewer.
• Shrink/condense the layout of the left column in the timeline.
• Use one consistent hover highlight color everywhere.
• Tweak message layout for alignment perfection!
• Full navigational history: go back/forward through rooms.
• Makepad fix to properly center and layout title/caption bar.
• Enable the bounce effect for SpacesBar and the main timeline.
• keep macOS linker plist in the Cargo output.
• Fix title bar nav buttons disappearing in a narrow window.
• redesign the welcome screen with a nice responsive layout.
• makepad: properly scale the macOS title bar with the UI.
• Show a popup menu for nav history when long pressing a nav button.
• Allow dragging and releasing to select an item in the nav history menu.
• makepad: fix LoadingSpinner not properly animating on android, linux, windows.
• Swipe right to go back on mobile.
• adjust spacing and ordering of content in the settings screen.
• Bump version to 1.0.0-beta.3.

Changes we made to Makepad since the last release:

As always, a significant amount of our effort is spent upstreaming improvements & fixes into Makepad, such that Robrix and everyone else benefits from them.

• On phones, you can now swipe right anywhere on a screen to go back. The screen follows your finger and reveals the one beneath it, and when you let go, it either finishes going back or springs back into place, depending on how far you dragged it and how fast you flicked it, like on iOS. Android's predictive back gesture drives the same animation. A drag that already means something else, like selecting text in the message box or resizing a pane, stays with that widget instead of turning into a swipe. ().
• Animated GIF, WebP, and APNG images now play at their proper speed, with each frame shown for its own delay, instead of at a fixed 25 frames per second that played each animation forward and then backward. Animations also only wake Robrix up when their next frame is due rather than on every display frame, they all step on one shared clock so frames that are due together share a single repaint, and they pause while they're off screen, like in a hidden tab. The image viewer no longer stretches animated images either, since it was sizing them by the sprite sheet that holds all of their frames, and animated WebP and APNG frames are now drawn correctly. ().

• Messages written in HTML are now spaced like they are on the web: no stray space at the top or bottom of a message, a single gap between neighboring paragraphs, lists, and quotes instead of both of their margins stacked together, and a list item's text sits right next to its bullet instead of below it. Makepad's HTML widget now collapses the margins between blocks the same way CSS does. ().
• Loading spinners now spin on their own on Android, Linux, and Windows. Makepad only noticed that a shader animates over time when it was compiled for Metal (Apple platforms), so everywhere else, a spinner froze whenever nothing else on screen was changing. Makepad also now repaints only the window or cached view that a spinner is drawn in, rather than all of them, so on macOS and iOS, a spinner can't make Robrix's cached reply previews re-render on every frame anymore. ().
• Once you've scrolled all the way back to the start of a room's history, the timeline now bounces at the top like any other list, so you can tell there's nothing left to load. It couldn't bounce there before, since scrolling up to the top is how older messages get loaded, so Makepad now lets Robrix turn on that bounce once the whole history is loaded. ().
• The new back and forward buttons in the title bar work like normal buttons: clicking or dragging one never moves the window, they keep their hand cursor, and they stay clear of the window's minimize, maximize, and close buttons at any zoom level. In a narrow window, the window title moves out of their way or gets cut off with "…" instead of overlapping them. You can also press and hold one, then drag onto a place in its history menu and let go to jump there. (,,, ).
• macOS: the title bar now grows when you zoom in on Robrix's UI, and the traffic lights move down to stay vertically centered in it, like in VS Code. Before, the title bar stayed the same height at every zoom level, since it was sized around the traffic lights, which don't zoom. ().
• Windows: clicking on Robrix's window to bring it to the front no longer breaks Escape or the @mention popup. Makepad mistook that click for the window losing focus, so until you switched to Robrix some other way, like with Alt-Tab, Escape did nothing and the mention popup never showed up. ().
• iOS: long-pressing a message opens its context menu again. A long press on iOS always came with a touch ID of 0 instead of the ID of the finger that made it, so Robrix couldn't match it up with the finger pressing on the message. ().

apps.localizedDescription:
Decantra:

A bottle-sorting puzzle game with procedurally generated levels that never run out. Available on Android, iOS, and Web.

How to Play:

Sort the colored liquids by pouring from one bottle to another until each bottle holds a single color.

• Pour by dragging one bottle onto another.
• You can only pour onto the same color or into an empty bottle.
• Black bottles (sinks) accept liquid but can't be picked up - plan around them.
• A level is solved when every non-empty bottle contains exactly one color.

Early levels ease you in. Later levels introduce more colors, varying bottle sizes, and multiple sinks that demand careful sequencing. Every level is procedurally generated, so there's always a fresh puzzle waiting.

You need your own copy of the game. The app on the.

versions.localizedDescription:
0.3.0:

• Fixes for freezes. The freeze after leaving the safehouse (and in some tollbooth races): the picture stopped while music and controls went on. And a rare black-screen hang at boot.

• HDMI and AirPlay. An external display shows the game by itself, full size, while the phone keeps the touch controls.
• MetalFX (native renderer): temporal upscaling with the game's motion, to the screen, lighter, or anti-aliasing only. FXAA, MSAA where the game draws without it, and the game's own mip levels.
• Battery and heat. Battery mode (lower resolution, half-size shadows, car reflections updated less often), 30 fps in menus and pause, 30 fps when warm or on Low Power, 0.75x when hot, each also on its own. Less CPU spent waiting, no idle 120 Hz screen refresh, steadier frame pacing.

apps.name: Skate 3
apps.subtitle: Build the Skate 3 recompilation for iOS from your own disc image. Or ipa Ships no game code
apps.localizedDescription:
skate3-ios-setup:

Build the Skate 3 recompilation for iOS from your own disc image, on your own Mac, signed with your own Apple ID, installed on your own iPhone.

Runs at a locked 60fps on an iPhone 13 mini (A15): median frame 16.7ms against a 16.67ms budget, 95th percentile 16.8-17.8ms. Anything newer has more headroom than that.

Step 3 is the whole thing: it checks your tools, extracts your disc image, recompiles it, builds the app, signs it with your Apple ID, and installs it on your phone.

--recurse-submodules matters - the runtime lives in a submodule and the build will not configure without it. If you already cloned without it, run git submodule update --init --recursive inside skate3recomp-dev.

versions.localizedDescription:
Skate 3 Recompiled v2.7.1 — iOS:

iOS skipped a release. Everything Android got in v0.2.0 is here, plus two iOS-specific defaults. 24 engine commits and 17 SDK commits since v2.6.3.

Put any button anywhere:

Full controller remapping, on the Controls page under Button Mapping. Sixteen inputs — the four face buttons, both bumpers, both triggers, both stick clicks, Back, Start and the four D-pad directions — can each be moved to any of the others. Your mapping is saved and survives an update.

The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that.

Three bugs that were costing you frames:

Touching the frame-rate row uncapped the game. One setting's name was a prefix of another's (._fps_cap inside ._fps_cap_auto), so changing the Framerate Cap row erased the shipped cap entirely, on every launch after you touched that row. The game then ran the guest loop uncapped. On Android that also meant rendering roughly twice the frames the panel could show and dumping the rest as heat, which is what "runs at 60, drops after a few minutes" was there; iOS presents through FIFO, so the cost here is wasted work rather than heat.

"The frame rate is fine but it feels like slow motion." Skate 3 advances exactly one refresh period of simulation per rendered frame, however long that frame took, so a 33 ms frame runs the game at half speed. The ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one period (skate3_frame_advance_cap) had been compiled for Switch only — iOS and Android, the two platforms whose frames overrun the period most, never got it. It is compiled in on iOS now.

Being straight about this one: the clamp is in and reachable, but raising it was measured as changing nothing on hardware, so treat it as a lever that now exists rather than a fix you are guaranteed to feel.

A profiler was running in every build. A per-packet GPU timer took two clock reads and two atomic increments on every command packet — around 1.7 million clock reads a second on the busiest thread — whether or not anyone was profiling. It is off unless you ask for it.

First launch could come up blank:

Roughly one clean install in ten reached the setup screen with an empty options list and no way forward. Parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back — and the difficulty prompt is drawn exactly once. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so nothing can draw before it is ready.

Eleven new rows, most of them aimed at buying frames back on a phone:

• 3D Scene Resolution — Full / 75% / 67% / 50% / 40%, separate from UI sharpness.
• Draw Distance — now goes down to Quarter and Eighth.
• NPC Update Rate and World Update Rate.
• Pedestrians & Traffic, Movable Props, Other Skaters — stop the world spawning crowds you are not looking at (all three need a restart).
• Vegetation, Hair Detail, Water Effects, Draw Batching.
• Framerate Cap — 40, 45 and 50 added (40 divides 120 Hz, 45 divides 90 Hz).
• FPS Percentiles — the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average (darchap's, see Credit).

Known limitation on the three population cuts: they remove the bodies, not the gameplay objects behind them, so you may still hear pedestrians, traffic and other skaters you cannot see. Being worked on. The average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter: a steady 60 and a 60 that drops four frames a second read the same.

Two changed defaults on iOS:

• Draw distance now ships at Half. The static world is roughly 750 of the 765 things drawn in a frame, so it is the only content lever with real weight behind it. The trade is real: props, street furniture and foliage pop in closer than they did in 2.6.3. Settings > Video > Draw Distance > Original puts it back.This applies to new installs only. If you are updating, your existing draw distance is kept exactly as it is — the game records your video settings the first time it runs, and a new default never overwrites settings that are already on your device. To get the new one, set the row to Half yourself.
• FPS Percentiles ships on, so the 1% low is there as soon as you turn the FPS counter on. The counter itself is still off by default.

Under the hood:

• The render pass stays open when the target has not changed.
• The tonemap and HUD passes can be merged into one (off by default).
• The guest is parked while the app is in the background, instead of running on against a surface that is gone.
• The texture budget is enforced between rescans.
• Shader compilation stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so the first-run setup screen cannot draw before its shaders exist.

Bring your own copy of the game — no game content ships in this IPA. See the README for the ISO and title-update steps.

Credit:

This is a packaging of other people's work as much as my own.

• Alex McHugh — skate3recomp. The Skate 3 recompilation itself. None of this exists without it.
• portingpete — skate3-recomp. Early bring-up on ReXGlue.

• Buku313 — Skate3-Mobile. A parallel ARM64 port; the 16 KB page-alignment fix came from there.
• ReXGlue SDK and Xenia (Ben Vanik and contributors) underneath it all.

Licences: this repo's scripts are MIT; the code in the binary is under its own authors' terms. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

apps.name: Photos Backup
apps.subtitle: PhotosBackup iOS app
apps.localizedDescription:
Photos Backup for iOS:

An experimental, fully on-device iPhone app for backing up selected photos, videos, and albums to Google Photos. It is a single SwiftUI app that completes Google account setup in an in-app web view, so everything happens on the phone without a desktop companion or hosted service.

This project uses Google's private, undocumented Photos endpoints and an Android-style authentication flow. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google, and the integration may stop working without notice. Treat it as experimental software and use it at your own risk.

What it can do:

• Connect a Google account through Google's EmbeddedSetup flow, in an in-app web view.
• Capture the single-use oauth_token in-process from the web view's cookie store.
• Exchange the token for a Google Photos credential entirely on the device.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

• The Google Photos app now counts what this app backs up. (, thanks @saileshbro) Uploads showed as "not backed up" in the Google Photos app, and its own Free up space never offered them. It now recognises them, and its Free up space and Delete from device remove the photos from your iPhone. On one library of about 8,500 items, "Not backed up" went from 8,145 to 0 and Free up space from 2 items to 461.The reason was the version being uploaded. The Google Photos app only counts a photo it can match to the one on your iPhone, so an edited photo or video now backs up as it looks, not as its unedited original. A photo you edited in the Google Photos app also needs the version that edit was applied on, which is uploaded in an extra step.
• Back Up Live Photo Motion. Off by default. With it on, a Live Photo's motion is attached to the still already in your account, so it plays as a Live Photo and Free up space will offer it. Live Photos backed up earlier get their motion added as a backlog — this can be tens of GB, which is why it is a setting you turn on.
• Backup keeps going after you leave the app (iOS 26). While the app is open with work to do, iOS is asked to keep it running; progress then shows in a Live Activity, where you can also stop it. Up to 2 uploads run at once in the background. On earlier iOS versions nothing changes.

Fixed:

• Google's rate limit no longer fails a row. When Google asked the app to slow down (HTTP 429), rows retried a second apart, met the same refusal, and failed. The whole queue now waits it out — a minute, doubling up to ten while Google keeps refusing — and carries on.
• Photos deleted while still queued. Freeing space on your iPhone deletes photos that may still be waiting to upload. Those rows are dropped quietly instead of failing with "no longer in your photo library" — about 2,000 rows had failed that way on one library.
• Hand-picked photos are re-checked even when the app already remembers them as backed up.

Verifying this release:

• Every pull request and every push now runs the test suite before it can land.

Worth knowing:

• An edited photo now backs up its edit, not its original. Originals already uploaded stay in your account, but a newly edited photo no longer uploads its unedited version. Google's own backup behaves the same way.
• After updating, the app queues a one-time re-check of edited photos already backed up. Most settle without uploading anything.
• A photo saved to your iPhone from Google Photos is never counted as backed up, even though it is in your library. Editing it in Apple Photos works around this.

Notes:

• 191 tests, 189 passing (2 opt-in live tests skipped).
• Tested on an iPhone 16 Pro Max (iOS 26.6.1, Google Photos 7.92.0) across a full library, and on a SideStore-signed install where the background tasks now register and run.

apps.subtitle: Logging in may break at random due to Apple's constant server-side changes
apps.localizedDescription:
Logging in may break at random due to Apple's constant server-side changes. If login fails, make sure that you're on the latest version of PancakeStore. Do NOT open any issues or ask for support regading logins. It will not speed up the process of fixing authentication.

Before you continue...:

• Not only is authentication unstable, but there is no guarantee that user data will be retained when downgrading! Use this tool at your own risk.

The target app must meet the following requirements:

• This app has been purchased from the App Store with the same Apple ID you're using to log in.
• The app isn't installed on your device (offloading works).
• The app actually has vaild versions to downgrade to (some don't, so keep this in mind).

versions.localizedDescription:
EoL Notice:

PancakeStore is officially EoL (End-of-Life) as of 8/22/2026.

Apple has implemented server-side changes to the iTunes API that's used in PancakeStore, as well as other popular tools such as ipatool, which primarily include SEP-based device attestation. What this means, in short, is that PancakeStore will not work ever again unless someone figures out an alternative route for downgrading apps, or successfully re-implements the attestation logic (both of which are very difficult).

In the event that this occurs, or a new method for downgrading apps is discovered and made, we will update PancakeStore. Until then, consider the project EoL.

Thank you all for all of your support of this tool, and we apologize that things have to halt like this.

❤️.

SteamPhone (steamphone-v2):

SteamOS-style gaming on iPhone — v2 of the DroidDeck iOS port, adding the SteamPhone GPU Bridge (SPGB): a real QEMU→Metal translation layer for the local virtual machine, with an on-device harness proving the Metal side executes the protocol.

Unofficial, GPL-3.0, not affiliated with Valve or Droid-Deck. v1 lineage: this repo carries the full v1 history (custom launcher, guest image builder, Moonlight streaming skeleton, CI) and rebrands the user-facing app to SteamPhone (com.steamphone.*), version 0.2.0.

iOS apps may only touch the GPU through Metal. v1's local VM was software-rendered for that reason. v2 introduces the translation pipeline with explicit gates (full audit in gpu-rd/G0-audit.md):

Because UTM's engine runs QEMU inside the app process, the boundary is a plain C call — no IPC, no shared memory, no kernel interfaces.

CyPort contains no game files. You need your own legally bought copy of Cyberpunk 2077 for Mac (GOG, version 2.3.1). The app is built on your Mac from that copy. CyPort is an independent fan project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CD PROJEKT RED. Cyberpunk 2077 is a trademark of CD PROJEKT S.A.

Status:

Tested on: iPhone 16 Pro Max (A18 Pro, 8 GB), iOS 27.0.1, built with Xcode 27.

versions.localizedDescription:
CyPort v1.2:

Run your own copy of Cyberpunk 2077 for Mac natively on iPhone and iPad – no emulation, no streaming.

Not affiliated with CD PROJEKT RED.

This release is about heat and frame times. On an iPhone the limit isn't raw speed, it's heat: the phone used to throttle within a minute or two of open-world play, and then the frame rate jumped around.

❄️ Cool mode (always on):

• The engine's 5 job worker threads ask for the highest thread priority, which kept them all on the A18 Pro's 2 performance cores next to the game and render threads – that is what made the phone hot so fast.
• CyPort now runs 3 of them on the 4 efficiency cores, which do the same work for far less power. 2 stay on the performance cores, so the game thread doesn't wait on slow cores every frame (all 5 on the efficiency cores felt stuttery).
• Tunable in macshim.plist: CoolFastWorkers (default 2), CoolMode = NO turns it off.

🏙️ Steadier frame rate in the open world:

• The engine streams the city in on the game thread, by default up to 12 ms and 300 objects per frame – desktop values. At 30 FPS a frame only has 33 ms, so on a phone that showed up as frame drops while driving.
• CyPort now writes engine/config/platform/mac/user.ini at every start with 6 ms / 200 objects per frame: the work is spread over more frames. Things may appear a moment later.
• StreamingTweaks = NO restores the engine defaults; StreamingMsPerFrame / StreamingNodesPerFrame set your own values. If you edit user.ini yourself, remove its first line and CyPort leaves it alone.

🧹 Fewer hitches from CyPort itself:

• The worker-thread profiler from v1.1 paused all job workers for 2 s every minute – a regular hitch. Now off by default (WorkerSampler = YES to turn on).
• The log no longer forces a disk flush after every line (that blocked game threads). Crash reports are still written in full.
• Periodic statistics lines are only logged with Diagnostics = YES.
• With the performance overlay set to Off, its window is now removed completely, so iOS no longer has to composite it over the game.

🛠️ Other:

• The start screen marks the resolutions that make the phone hot quickly.
• The log now shows how busy the GPU is (1 s sample every 30 s), to tell GPU heat from CPU heat. GPUSampler = NO turns it off.
• Optional frame pacing for testing: FrameRate = 30 / 40 / 60 in macshim.plist. By default the frame rate is the game's own setting (Settings → Graphics → VSync / Maximum FPS).
• CPUCount now also reports a matching number of performance cores.

Performance tips:

• Resolution 1434 × 660 on the start screen – at 1912 × 880 an iPhone 16 Pro Max still throttles within about 1.5 minutes of driving.
• Maximum FPS 30 in the game's graphics settings: a steady 30 looks smoother than a rate that jumps between 25 and 50, and the phone stays cool much longer.
• Leave frame generation off.
• A clip-on phone cooler helps more than any setting.

Upgrading:

Rebuild the IPA with this version (./build.sh, see the README), then reinstall. Your game data, saves and settings stay in place.

Known issues:

• The phone still throttles in long open-world sessions; expect ~20–30 FPS while driving once it's hot.
• The streaming change and the 2-fast/3-efficient worker split are new and have only had short tests – please report pop-in or stutter.
• The free Apple ID route (SideStore + GetMoreRam, compact memory layout) is still untested on a device.

Every download is one file. sha256sums.txt covers all of them.

ByeTunes 🎵:

Say goodbye to iTunes sync!

ByeTunes is a native iOS app that lets you inject music (MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV) and ringtones directly into your device's media library—without needing a computer connection for every sync. It communicates directly with the iOS media database, giving you the power to manage your music on your terms.

• No Computer Needed (after setup): Once paired, you're free!

Prerequisites:

• Xcode: Version 15+ recommended.
• iOS Device: Running iOS 16.0 or later.

versions.localizedDescription:
ByeTunes v2.6 – Favorites, Playlist Pinning & Background Downloads Reworked:

Hi guys, here is the 2.6 update for ByeTunes. A good amount of things got added, fixed and improved in this one. You can now properly favorite injected songs, pin playlists from inside ByeTunes, and keep downloads going in the background with a new Picture in Picture window. There were also a bunch of fixes around metadata, library management and database safety.

Favorites.

There are three new options inside Library Repair:

• Create Favorites Playlist creates the Favorites playlist using the right name for your device region.
• Fix Missing Favorites repairs songs injected with an older version that you already favorited but that never actually appeared in Favorites.
• Delete Favorites Playlist lets you delete that playlist from Library Repair.

Songs injected from 2.6 onwards now get their store IDs during injection, so you can favorite them right away. If the metadata fetcher finds a match, ByeTunes uses the IDs from that match. Songs without a match get generated IDs instead.

Quick recommendation: if you have older injected songs that you favorited but cannot find in Favorites, run Fix Missing Favorites inside Library Repair.

Playlist Pinning.

You can now pin and unpin playlists from the On-Device Library. Long-press a playlist or use the Pin button from inside it.

Keep in mind: pinning and unpinning these playlists needs to be done through ByeTunes. The Pin option inside the Apple Music app does not work for them.

Background Downloads.

Background downloads got a big rework. ByeTunes now uses silent audio to keep downloads going in the background, with an optional Picture in Picture window so you can see what is happening after leaving the app.

The window shows the current song's progress, what is next in the queue, and when metadata is being fetched. You can also customize it with themes, your own colors or a background picture. There is a live preview in Settings so you can see how it looks before using it.

This replaces the old background download behavior and Live Activity support. Download progress now shows in the Picture in Picture window.

If the app closes while songs are still downloading, those songs go back to the front of the queue the next time you open ByeTunes.

Pause and Cancel were fixed too. They now properly stop background transfers instead of accidentally starting a fallback download after you already paused or cancelled the song.

Download Queue & Saving Files.

Downloaded songs now get their metadata as part of the download process. You will see a "fetching metadata" state before the song is marked as done, instead of that work being left to a separate background metadata manager.

A few other things got added or improved:

• Clear All for completed items in the queue sheet.
• Preview buttons in the album sheet and artist profile.

• A new Save With Fetched Metadata toggle that writes the fetched tags and cover artwork into the MP3 and FLAC copies you save.

Metadata Fixes.

Metadata matching got a lot of attention in this update. There were cases where a remix could get the original song's information, or a song could get renamed to a different track from the same album. Those issues should now be fixed.

• Apple Music track matching now checks the title, so songs should no longer get relabeled as another track from that album.
• Apple Music search pages are requested in English so ByeTunes can find the Songs and Albums sections even when using a non-English storefront.
• A Deezer result with missing artwork or an unreadable item no longer causes the entire search to come back empty.

FLAC handling was improved too. Some changes in the downloaded files were causing every song to take the album name as its title when an ALBUMTITLE tag was present. That is fixed now.

Album artist is also read correctly from files using the ALBUM ARTIST or album_artist tags.

Library Management.

Added sorting, a genre filter and multi-delete to the Library management tab.

Fixed an issue where the library would only show some of your songs, for example just 50 tracks. ByeTunes was only scanning one folder. It now scans all folders so the rest of your songs show up too.

Injected songs now use the file's creation date for a more accurate date.

Deleting songs also cleans up any albums, artists and artwork entries left empty after the deletion.

Stability, Backups & Database Safety.

There were also several fixes to make injection, transfers and backups more reliable:

• One unreadable local file no longer stops the whole injection batch.
• The export folder is checked before transferring files. If it cannot be used, ByeTunes falls back to its own Exports folder.
• Snapshot backups keep the previous snapshot until the new one finishes successfully, and only replace snapshots of the same kind.
• The heartbeat timeout handles stale connection attempts more reliably.

Overall stability and database safety were improved too.

Cleanup.

The old background metadata manager and its pending import pipeline were removed, since downloaded songs now get their metadata directly during the download process.

The Live Activity extension and download tracking were also removed as part of the move to Picture in Picture, along with the old background download behavior and unused code.

Official Backend & Building Your Own.

I also added BACKEND_TERMS.md, which explains how the official hosted backend may be used. Modified builds need to use their own backend.

If you are building ByeTunes yourself, Config.example.plist is now included as a template for the backend address. The README explains how to set it up.

I also reorganized the project structure. Files are now grouped into proper folders so everything is easier to find and work on. This should help anyone working on their own fork of ByeTunes understand where things are and make changes more easily. I am also considering a bigger rewrite of the app down the road, so this cleanup is a step towards that, but nothing is confirmed yet.

Thanks as always to everyone testing ByeTunes, sending logs and reporting what breaks. Hope you guys enjoy this update.

apps.localizedDescription:
YouTube Downloader:

A cross-platform video downloader. On Windows and Linux it's a desktop GUI (and CLI) wrapping yt-dlp and FFmpeg. On Android and iPhone/iPad it's a native app that does YouTube extraction in pure C# (mobile OSes can't run yt-dlp/ffmpeg as subprocesses). Every version can search YouTube, so you don't need a link.

Features:

• YouTube-themed dark UI built with Avalonia.

• Paste a URL and fetch video info (title, channel, duration, thumbnail), with Copy link and Copy player link buttons.
• Player page: a web page that plays just the video in any browser, remembers your place and follows re-uploads.

• Custom filename and save location.
• Live progress bar showing size, speed, and ETA.
• Auto-updates yt-dlp on startup.
• Supports cookies.txt for age-restricted videos.

versions.localizedDescription:
Every app can now give you a player link for the video in the box:

• iPhone and Android: the ▶ Copy player link button under the video info.

The player page:

• Just the picture. YouTube's title, channel, logo, controls, captions and end screen are hidden, and the page's own link bar fades away while the video plays. Click or tap to pause, double-click for full screen; space, the arrow keys, f and m work too.
• It remembers where you were. Open the same video again and it carries on from the second you left (saved in your browser only).
• It follows re-uploads. If the video is deleted or made private, the page looks on the same channel for a video with the same title and length and switches to it at the same second, fading one into the other.

Limits: videos whose uploader turned off embedding show a "Watch on YouTube" link instead. For a few seconds after you start or skip, YouTube still draws a small pause symbol in the middle of the picture, which a page can't hide. A player link opens paused because browsers block sound until you tap once.

How it was tested:

• Player link: 20 unit tests cover every link form (watch, youtu.be, Shorts, live, embed, start times); the CLI was run for real, and the desktop and iPhone buttons were driven in headless UI tests (the Android button is the same code and was built).
• Player page: unit tests for its link, timing and re-upload logic, then browser checks on the live page and locally: resume after a reload, a start time in the link, a re-upload switch (landing within 0.05 s of the old video), a removed video with a saved second, a link pasted while a search was running, the search failing, and phone width.

SceneBox:

Torrent streaming client for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS and Mac (Catalyst), written in SwiftUI.

Important:

SceneBox is a media player and BitTorrent/HTTP client. It does not provide, host, index, upload, store, or distribute any media content, and it has no affiliation with any content source.

• All catalog metadata, stream listings, and media files come from third-party services and peers that users configure or connect to. These services are independent of SceneBox, are not operated, controlled, endorsed, or reviewed by its author, and may be changed or removed at any time.

versions.localizedDescription:
Important: accounts now need your own Firebase project.

SceneBox no longer connects to a shared Firebase project. Sign-in, profiles and sync between devices now run on a free Firebase project that you create and own. Your data stays in your own account, not mine.

• Guest mode still works without any setup. Everything is kept on the device.
• To sign in, tap Connect Firebase on the sign-in screen and import the GoogleService-Info.plist from your Firebase project (on Apple TV, type in the values). Step-by-step guide and the security rules: https://github.com/donbytyqi/scenebox#firebase-setup
• Accounts made on the old shared project don't carry over. Create a new account on your own project.

New.

Fixes.

• Apple TV: Trakt lists open when you click them. (#10).
• Mac: signing in works on the unsigned build. macOS doesn't let unsigned apps use the Keychain, so the app keeps your sign-in session and any API keys you enter in a file inside its own sandbox container instead (readable only by your user account).

Still open.

Important: this release is NOT signed. You have to allow it yourself.

Nothing here is signed with an Apple developer account and the Mac app is not notarized. macOS and iOS will refuse to open it until you explicitly allow it. This is expected, it's not broken.

Mac:

• Open the dmg and drag SceneBox to Applications.
• Open SceneBox. macOS will say it "could not verify" the app or that it's from an unidentified developer. Press Done (not Move to Trash).
• Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security and press "Open Anyway" next to SceneBox, then confirm.
• From then on it opens normally.

If you'd rather skip the dialog, run this in Terminal after copying the app to Applications:

If you had an older signed version installed, delete it first.

iPhone/iPad: the ipa isn't signed, you sign it yourself with Sideloadly, AltStore, SideStore, Feather or ESign with your own Apple ID. Free Apple ID = resign every 7 days (AltStore/SideStore do it for you), paid dev account = one year.

Apple TV: Sideloadly works over Wi-Fi. On the TV go to Settings > Remotes and Devices > Remote App and Devices so it shows up, then pick it in Sideloadly.

apps.name: Kikoto
apps.subtitle: A local personal DLsite audio library, source browser, and player
apps.localizedDescription:
Kikoto keeps one entry per work, keyed by its product code, and attaches DLsite-style metadata, local folders, a rebuildable cache, and Kikoeru-compatible remote sources to it. It runs on your own server and opens in any browser and in the Android and iOS apps.

Kikoto is self-hosted software only and provides no service or content. It is designed solely for DLsite works you have purchased yourself; see the Disclaimer.

Features:

Scans, syncs, file edits, and AI tasks run as workflows you can follow in Activity, roles decide who may browse, fetch, edit, and administer, and all state lives in one SQLite database. The APK and IPA for the apps are attached.

versions.localizedDescription:
Upgrade notes. Back up config/ and keep the existing data/ mount. v0.8.3 databases advance from schema 068 through migrations 069–082; fresh installs use baseline/082_v0.9.0.sql. The first start of a large library takes longer while every work's circle is recorded.

• Enabled Follow triggers become subscriptions of the account that set them up, and Availability Watch now runs on the subscription refresh. Review Refresh schedule on the Subscriptions page.
• Existing lyrics assignments become each track's Fallback lyrics.
• LAN and container-host addresses now bypass the proxy by default; edit Bypass proxy in Settings → Proxy to keep one routed through it.

Upgrade with docker compose up -d --pull always; update KIKOTO_IMAGE first if it is pinned.

The Windows PowerShell helper is no longer maintained; version v0.2.1 says so on start. Switch to Kikoto Helper.

Kikoto v0.9.0 makes Manage lyrics a lyrics workshop: lyrics per language, speech-to-lyrics transcription, and LLM translation of lyrics and metadata, all reviewed before saving and governed by one content safety policy, with Kikoto Helper for local models. It also adds Subscriptions for new releases, smart lists in Favorites, official bundle contents, and Edit files, and makes circle and voice actor pages much faster.

• Manage lyrics keeps one lyrics file per track and language. A language strip switches between Fallback, the lyrics used when none of a listener's languages has lyrics, and Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, and Korean. Lyrics assigned before the upgrade become fallback lyrics.
• Manage lyrics puts its sections in a tab bar under the title, with the language strip, folder alignment, and reset in one toolbar. Each folder of tracks counts the tracks that have lyrics, a mark on every row shows whether the track has lyrics, and the lyrics preview lists line times in their own column.

• Manage files has Manage as lyrics, which opens Lyrics files with the selected lyrics files, and hides the lyrics in those folders unless Show in the list is on.
• Transcribe lists the local tracks with the languages they have lyrics in, filtered to the tracks without lyrics or without lyrics in the original language, and turns the speech of the selected tracks into timed lyrics with a configured speech recognition service. The audio language starts as the work's original language. Each transcription is an Activity workflow that sends parts of at most five minutes, cut in quiet moments, and gives the queue to other waiting work between parts. Service configuration, permissions, and content policy are checked again right before audio is sent. Add to lyrics saves the reviewed result as a WebVTT file in the language's lyrics folder and assigns it to the track.
• Translate shows the local tracks against the lyrics languages, green where a track has lyrics and red where it has none. Choosing red cells, or a whole language column, translates those tracks with a configured LLM provider from their original-language lyrics, or from another language chosen in the row. Each translation is an Activity workflow that keeps the file's timing and waits for review; Add to lyrics saves it in the target language's lyrics folder under the track's path and assigns it to the track.
• Check rating in Transcribe and Translate shows the content safety class of the work or of each lyrics file without sending anything, and marks the services that may not receive it. The check runs only when pressed.
• Edit files, Lyrics files, and Add to lyrics never replace a folder or link at a target. A file that sits where a folder belongs is named and can only be kept or have the incoming file renamed, and a file or folder Kikoto did not create that blocks the lyrics folder asks you to rename or move it.
• A failed lyrics edit restores moved source files even when an earlier publication occupies their original path. If restoration is obstructed, staged files and their recovery mapping remain on the target storage pool.

• A new Subscriptions page collects new works from the circles, series, and voice actors you subscribe to with the bell beside Favorite on their pages. Subscribing is separate from Favorite. A subscription starts from the catalog as it is, so existing works never flood the feed; a catalog that was not pulled recently is pulled first, now or at the next refresh.

• A circle subscription includes its series: a series of a subscribed circle cannot be subscribed separately, and subscribing to the circle replaces its series subscriptions after a confirmation.
• One shared Refresh schedule (every 24 hours by default) pulls each subscribed catalog once, syncs the metadata of new works, and then checks Availability Watch. A subscription can also add its new works to Availability Watch.

• Availability Watch's configuration and pool move to the Subscriptions page; Workflows keeps its run history and links there.
• The Follow presets are renamed Sync a circle catalog, Sync a series catalog, and Sync a voice actor catalog, under a Catalog sync category, and run on demand only. Their triggers section links to Subscriptions, and the circle and voice actor More menus read Sync this circle's catalog… and Sync this voice actor's catalog….

• Favorites has smart lists. A smart list shows the works that carry all of its required tags, at least one of its any-of tags, and none of its excluded tags, using shared metadata tags and your own tags. Matching works are not favorites; works you add by hand are, and a matching work you remove stays out. The shelf counts and marks works that started to match since you last chose Mark all as seen, and Convert to regular list keeps the current works as an ordinary list. Personal data exports leave smart lists out.
• Add to list on work cards and work detail has a search field, saves each list you check or clear at once, and creates a list from a name no list has. It notes a smart list that holds the work through its rule. Change lists on selected Favorites works shows what each list will add or remove before you apply it and can also create a list. On phones both open as a bottom sheet.
• Add list and a shelf's Edit list open a focused editor for that one list, with the icon beside the name, a note when another list has the same name, and Delete list. Edit lists lists every list on its own and returns to it after an edit. Moving a list saves at once without a notification or switching shelves. Japanese, Korean, and Chinese call Edit lists "Manage lists" so it differs from a shelf's Edit list.
• The List button on a work's detail page names the list that holds the work. When several do, it names the first and counts the rest, and its tooltip names them all.

• Official bundles such as complete packs list the works they contain. Metadata sync fills the list when DLsite names the contents, and a library editor adds or removes works under Bundle contents in the metadata editor, with suggestions from the bundle's DLsite series. The bundle's detail shows Includes and each work's detail shows Included in; the works stay separate. Searching for a work's code or title also finds the bundles that include it.

• A work whose files lie in several local folders shows each folder in its directory, lists one folder at a time in Manage files, and tells a library manager how to bring the copies into one. The same notice appears when another edition of the work is in the library.
• Quick select in Manage files has Find identical files, which compares the local files of every edition and folder of the work by content, marks the files that have an identical copy, and can select the copies that also exist in another folder or are repeated in the listed one.
• Manage files keeps the folder choice, Quick select, and Edit files in one toolbar above the list. Quick select holds the selections by location and format, the head of the list selects the whole folder, and a file names its copies only when it has more than one.
• Cards leads the display options of the Library, circles, voice actors, and Subscriptions. Automatic wide-screen columns fit up to 5 full, 6 compact, or 7 mini cards in a row and fewer in a narrower window. Choosing a card mode returns wide-screen columns to automatic and sets works per page and Library cover source marks to that mode's starting point: 24 works for Full and Compact, and 48 works with no source marks for Mini.
• The Library and Favorites offer 24, 48, or 96 works per page on every tab. Remote sources drop the 12-per-page choice, and a device that had chosen it shows 24.
• The bottom page bar shows more page numbers on wider screens and keeps the same number of items on every page, so its arrows stay in place. The ellipsis between page numbers opens a field that goes to a typed page.

• The voice actor list, the circle list, and circle pages load much faster, and a circle page stays as fast however large the rest of the library is. The favorite circles and voice actors on Favorites only summarize the creators you favorited, so these lists hold up other pages far less when many people use the server at once.
• A voice actor's works are paged on the server. The search, the availability filter, and the chosen order apply across all of the voice actor's works before a page is returned, and selection covers the page on screen. The search matches like a plain Library search, including titles in other languages and voice actor names, and every edition of a work counts as one work.

• Translate with LLM in the metadata editor translates a work's title, description, and missing shared tag names into a language the chosen model supports. Check content without sending shows how the content safety policy classifies the request without contacting the provider. The result is a preview that waits for review; accepted titles and descriptions are marked LLM in the language menu and on cards, are searchable and sortable, and never override a manual title or an official edition. A changed original field retires its translation, and Revoke and Restore take a translation out of presentation or bring it back.
• Queue background translation translates up to 100 named works as an Activity task that survives restarts and keeps finished parts. A request whose result is uncertain is never sent again automatically; Resend uncertain request asks you to acknowledge that another charge may occur.
• A local scan keeps every folder in which it finds a work's code as a folder of that work and indexes all of them, instead of raising duplicate folders for review in Activity.
• Refreshing a work's local files preserves indexed files in additional folders outside the scan depth or in offline storage pools.
• A local scan no longer takes a lyrics folder that From remote created inside a work folder, such as Lyrics - CHI_HANS - RJ00000001 - 20261008-153012, for a separate work. The next scan restores the work folder that holds such a folder.

• Lyrics follow your metadata languages: a track uses the first of them that has lyrics, then the fallback lyrics, then another language, and the lyrics list names each file's language.

• Settings → LLM & ASR lists the configured LLM providers and ASR services above the content safety policy that governs both. Each service is added or edited in a dialog that lists the presets on the left and the chosen preset's form on the right. A service's switch turns it on or off from the list, and deleting one asks for confirmation.
• The tab stays behind an external service notice until an administrator accepts it: external services may forbid the content sent to them, the content safety checks are advisory, and Kikoto is not responsible for suspended accounts. The server refuses LLM and ASR configuration until then.
• LLM providers are built-in or custom OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, Ollama, and Kikoto Helper endpoints. ASR services are OpenAI-compatible speech recognition services: OpenAI, a local deployment, or a custom service. A service on the server's own machine is reached through the host gateway, so only its port is entered.
• A provider or service offers several models from one connection, one of them the default. Translating and transcribing choose a provider and model, and a task keeps the model it started with. Model discovery for OpenAI speech recognition suggests only Whisper models.
• An LLM provider sets its request timeout, 10 minutes by default, so a local model has time to finish. An Ollama provider can also set its context length and turn off thinking, and Kikoto constrains Ollama's output to one entry per tag or lyrics line, so a small local model cannot drop or merge lines.
• Kikoto Helper is both an ASR service and an LLM provider preset. It reaches a Kikoto Helper on the server's machine on ports 17656 and 17657 by default, or on another machine by origin, with the API token the helper shows. Fetching models records the translation directions the helper's model supports: translation starts from the interface language when the model can translate into it, shows other languages as unavailable, and refuses an unsupported direction before queuing. A helper without an installed model, with a model that cannot start or ran out of memory, or with a risk notice that is not accepted names that cause.
• The content safety policy grades works as General, Sensitive, or High sensitivity. Each service declares the highest level it may receive, separately from its data boundary, and new services receive only General content. Tag rules are removable chips with per-tag actions and keyword rules are compact rows; either can mark high-sensitivity content or block every service, including for all-ages works. Prechecks show the matched rules and the chosen service's maximum.
• A default-off option rates LLM translations only by keywords in the complete selected source text; transcription always assesses the work's metadata.
• Proxy has an LLM & ASR scope for providers and services at another address, off by default; one on the server's own machine always connects directly. A translation or transcription request that a proxy drops after it was sent fails instead of moving to the next proxy, so the service never receives it twice.
• Proxy has a Bypass proxy list of hostnames, *.domain suffixes, IP addresses, and networks that every scope reaches directly. A network also matches a hostname that resolves into it. It starts with this machine, the container host, private networks, and *.local, *.lan, *.internal, and *.home.arpa, so a LAN source behind a configured proxy connects directly unless its entry is removed.

• Insights in Demo shows a simulated listening history over the admitted works, with a notice that it is simulated.
• Subscriptions in Demo shows a fixed, read-only sample feed and subscription list with fictional names.
• Manage lyrics in Demo shows Transcribe and Translate with sample transcriptions and translations, an example service and provider, and sample previews. Demo sends nothing to a service, and starting, rating checks, adding, and discarding stay off.
• About lists its reference projects as compact credits, one line of project names per area. Show details adds what each project informed.

• The Library page, work detail controllers, circle, voice actor, and Favorites pages, and the backend favorites, circle reads, and DLsite sync and client are split by responsibility.
