apps.name: Rigs of Rods
apps.subtitle: Rigs of Rods on iPhone: native port built on free GitHub Actions macOS runners
apps.localizedDescription:
Rigs of Rods — iOS:

под Apple/iOS (patches/ror/apply_ios_patches.py). Сборка — **без Mac и без Sideloadly).

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned, ad-hoc-signed RoR IPA for arm64 iPhone/iPad, built from 215e31998.

Files (release-dependent):

• RoR-ios.ipa - the full game, ~112 MB. Ships its data in RoR.app/rorres/ (not resources/ - see below).
• RoR-ios-lite.ipa - the same app with the content-only archives dropped (meshes/textures/sounds/caelum/SkyX/ hydrax), ~40 MB. Every archive the startup path loads is kept, so it launches exactly like the full build - this is what makes it a usable launch diagnostic.
• RoR-ios-tiny.ipa - NOT the game. Shares Info.plist/signature/packaging with the game. Installs and launches (green screen).
• RoR-ios-bin.ipa - diagnostic (only on 'diag' tag). Real RoR binary, no data directory at all. The known-good baseline.
• RoR-ios-res0.ipa - diagnostic (only on 'diag' tag). bin plus a single file in resources/. The known-BAD reference.
• RoR-ios-res0r.ipa - diagnostic (only on 'diag' tag). bin plus the same single file, in rorres/ instead. What the fix does.

Why the directory is called rorres:

An .app whose bundle contains a top-level directory named resources (or Resources - the check is case-insensitive) is refused by the iOS installer with the generic "Unable to Install", while the very same directory under any other name (zzz/, Base.lproj/, rorres/) installs and runs. Measured on device: bin - no directory -> installs zzz/rotest.txt -> installs Base.lproj/rotest.txt -> installs resources/rotest.txt -> refused Resources/rotest.txt -> refused.

codesign is what flips. With a resources/ (or Resources/) directory present it switches its resource rules to the macOS "resource envelope" set - rules=^Resources/, plus a '^[^/]+$ -> nested' rule in rules2 - and iOS will not install a bundle sealed that way. With any other directory name it keeps the plain ^.* rules that iOS accepts. The ad-hoc signature was never the problem: an unsigned variant with resources/ is refused just the same.

If the game installs but crashes right after launching:

It now writes Documents/ror-trace.log - one line per startup phase, plus every OGRE log line and, if it dies, the reason (SIGSEGV, or the uncaught exception's message). That file is flushed line by line with write(2), so it is complete even when the process is killed mid-line. Open it on the phone: Files app -> On My iPhone -> Rigs of Rods -> ror-trace.log. The last lines are the interesting ones. The same folder holds RigsOfRods/logs/RoR.log, which OGRE writes - but that one is buffered and loses its tail on a crash, so prefer ror-trace.log.

Hand the file itself to ESIGN / Sideloadly / SideStore - it is served as a plain file, nothing to unpack. An .ipa is a zip whose root contains Payload/.

CHECK THE DOWNLOAD BEFORE INSTALLING.

A truncated download makes every installer fail, and the error looks like a build problem ("Truncated input file", "Unable to Install"). Compare the byte size of the file you downloaded with the list below; if it differs by even one byte, download the file again.

RoR-ios.ipa 114898722 sha256:18819e2e36f5fd24c0fdb519575148074fc85b4650347c2e334996733dbaabd4 RoR-ios-lite.ipa 43258671 sha256:088700530d9b465af5485808e896d4cd3adc38417dc984bee41d85b702a1ec04 RoR-ios-tiny.ipa 37864 sha256:f6567d291ffa8e8ff47d26c8bb91b1057e64e34f3bf1ddc0e75be6b4b3660d52 RoR-ios-bin.ipa 6767343 sha256:32d0cdbba6adf147b302e3bc52f088217ba3b5f31b24092e9e05799d1792bac4 RoR-ios-res0.ipa 6767807 sha256:4ef9dbffcec3b4fb51a09c661c13f5b32af7b696e4aa9fe251730533f612dfed RoR-ios-res0r.ipa 6767802 sha256:bfb5ff53ff4bec9d6d6cf69b0d6afb86729d19de0b072f18568114d1a90c8c27.

apps.name: MiniWatts
apps.subtitle: An iPhone battery, charging and thermal instrument built on private iOS APIs — real charger watts, what actually reaches the cell, all 30 temperature sensors, and the USB-PD handshake
apps.localizedDescription:
MiniWatts:

An iPhone and iPad battery and charging monitor built on Apple's private APIs. It reads the device's own power-management sensors — the ones iOS uses to run the charge — and shows what the charger is delivering, how much of it reaches the cell, where the rest goes as heat, and what every temperature sensor in the device is doing while it happens.

Sideload only. Private APIs mean this can never be on the App Store — you sign and install it yourself. There is no network code of any kind: nothing it reads leaves your phone.

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned build — sign it with your own Apple ID before installing. https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts#install

Improvements:

• An incomplete input reading is no longer shown as the input. On an iPad Pro and an iPhone 18 Pro Max the input sensors see only part of the power (21.8 W shown for a real 43.5 W, for one). When more power is reaching the cell than the input reading accounts for, the dial now shows the "into battery" figure, efficiency and adapter utilisation are not worked out, and the Power and Adapter pages say why.
• Battery temperature is a median. Some models have four battery temperature sensors under one name, one of them reading clearly high. The Battery readout, the heat map's battery pin and the zone header all use the median now; all four are still listed.
• Impossible temperatures are left out. These no longer reach the heat map or the hottest reading, and stay in Raw data with a reason: a PMU sensor below −10 °C, a charge-IC temperature above 85 °C that its junction sensor does not back up, and a sensor at exactly 0.0 °C.
• iPad support. All orientations, and content no longer stretches edge to edge. The sensor mapping on iPad is unverified, so treat its numbers with care.
• More accurate wording. "From charger" is now "At phone port" / "At charging coil", and the Adapter page says the rating is a negotiated ceiling, not a wall-meter reading.
• Raw data is easier to report from. Every sensor carries its service index, and excluded readings are listed.

Fixes:

• Adapter: the profile list no longer shows an invalid "65.5 V × 65.53 A" entry.
• Live Activity: with the app in front, it updates on a 0.05 change instead of waiting for 0.2 W or 0.5 °C.

Notes:

• These fixes were made from data users reported and were not verified on those devices. If readings still look wrong on your model, copy the dump from Settings → Raw data and report it.
• On an iPhone 18 Pro Max the full input power at high-power charging still cannot be read; a Raw data dump taken at 45 W on that model is needed.
• Once the app is in the background the Dynamic Island reading stops. That is a system limit; use the floating meter for a live reading.

What works: patches that edit archives, packages (.pkg) or files, and patches that change data in the executable. 39 of the 150 patches in Knuxfan24's collection run, for example Disable Fog, Disable Character Stumble, Disable Hint Rings, Disable Music, E3 Timers, Correct Sonic Jump Animation and Opposite Button Prompts. What doesn't (yet):

• Patches that edit Lua scripts as text (29 of them) need decompiled scripts. The game ships compiled ones.

Both kinds stay listed with the reason, instead of failing silently.

apps.subtitle: Open-source desktop app for a local coding agent. Watch every tool call, diff, and terminal command. Bring your own models; sessions stay on your machine
apps.localizedDescription:
OpenAgentd:

Get started ·.

Facebook Group ·.

Contribute.

Why OpenAgentd:

Most coding agents live in a terminal or an editor. OpenAgentd is a coding-first native desktop app and mobile companion where you can run an agent, follow work in real time, inspect what changed, and keep moving without losing context.

• See the work. Streamed replies, tool calls, arguments, results, timings, files, diffs, terminal output, and agent status are visible in one interface.
• Track tasks. A clean, user-readable taskboard checklist keeps current work and progress visible at a glance.
• Work in real repositories. Coding sessions open local folders, support isolated git worktrees, show changes and history, and return language-server diagnostics after edits.

versions.localizedDescription:
Breaking Changes:

• Project skills, commands and snippets are now read only from .agents/. Move anything in a project's .openagentd/skills, .openagentd/commands or .openagentd/snippets (or .opencode/) into the same subfolder of .agents/, and anything in ~/.config/opencode/skills into ~/.agents/skills. .openagentd/ still holds local runtime state.

• When Claude declines to continue, you now see an error card with Anthropic's explanation and options to retry or switch models. The turn no longer ends silently, and the refused reply is dropped from context, so asking the agent to continue is no longer refused again.
• Stop always works: a turn that doesn't respond to Stop is force-ended, and the session goes back to idle within about 10 seconds.

• A mode you pick while a plan review or question is open now applies to the next message you send.
• Desktop Reload reopens the session the window was on, instead of the latest session in the last workspace.
• A JS plugin stuck in a busy loop is interrupted after 5 seconds instead of hanging the server. Plugin hooks time out after 60 seconds.
• MCP tool calls that never get an answer now fail after 210 seconds instead of waiting forever. Each server can set its own timeout (1–270 s) under Tool timeout in Settings, or with timeout in mcp.json.
• Drafts in the composer, in answers to agent questions and in plan-review comments now survive a reload.
• Quick Open and the @ picker now find gitignored workspace files, such as rendered videos or build output. They appear below other matches, and node_modules, .env files and very large ignored folders are left out. A workspace opened at a repository subfolder now applies every parent .gitignore.
• Workspace videos play right in the panel; use the player's own fullscreen button for full screen.
• About 150 more file types and well-known files (.jsonl, .astro, .svelte, .vue, lockfiles, Cargo.toml and others) get proper icons, and their text previews, attachments and syntax highlighting now work the same everywhere.

• Plan and agent files are written safely, so a crash can no longer leave them empty or cut off.
• Transcript find and the ⌘F / Ctrl+F shortcut have been removed. Session search is still in the sidebar.
• The agent's read tool no longer has an outline option.

NotBlood Chosen:

NotBlood (a Blood source port) with bots, new match types, co-op saves, internet play without port forwarding, a live game dashboard, a MODS menu and a LAN game finder, for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iPad. Every player in a network game needs the same version; all platforms of one version play together.

Downloads.

Unzip, copy your Blood files (One Unit Whole Blood: CD, GOG or Steam) next to the game and start it. The README in each download explains the rest.

• Match types: gun game, king of the hill, juggernaut, last man standing; teams: team bloodbath, capture the flag, king of the hill, last team standing; co-op survival. SET TEAMS for any mix of players and bots, mutators (gravity, vampire, one-hit kills, weapon sets) and match stats.

versions.localizedDescription:
NotBlood Chosen 1.2:

NotBlood Chosen is NotBlood (the Blood source port) with computer players (bots), new match types, co-op saves, internet play without port forwarding, a live game dashboard, a MODS menu and a LAN game finder. It runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iPad/iPhone, and all of them play together.

You need your own Blood files (One Unit Whole Blood: CD, GOG or Steam). The game files are not included.

Downloads:

Everybody in a network game needs 1.2. Older versions can't join a 1.2 game, and 1.2 can't join theirs.

Setup:

Windows / Linux.

• Unzip into a folder of its own, for example NotBlood.
• Copy your Blood files next to the game: BLOOD.INI, BLOOD.RFF, GUI.RFF, SOUNDS.RFF, SURFACE.DAT, TABLES.DAT, VOXEL.DAT and TILES000.ART to TILES017.ART.
• Start notblood.exe (Windows) or ./notblood (Linux; if SDL2 is missing: sudo apt install libsdl2-2.0-0).

macOS.

• Copy your Blood files into the folder, next to NotBlood.app.
• The app isn't signed by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time. Open Terminal and type xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine with a space at the end. Drag the NotBlood folder onto the Terminal window and press Return.
• Double-click NotBlood.app.

Android.

• Install the APK and start it once. Allow it "access to all files".

• 1.2 installs over NotBlood Chosen 1.0 and over the bots test builds, and keeps your files and settings.

iPad / iPhone.

• Sign and install the IPA with Signulous, Sideloadly or AltStore, and start it once.
• Copy your Blood files to Files > On My iPad > NotBlood.

Optional extras (all platforms, in the game folder).

• movie/: the cutscenes from the Blood CD's MOVIE folder.
• addons/: add-on episodes, one folder each (for example Cryptic Passage in addons/cryptic).
• mods/: mods as folders, .zip, .grp or .pk3 files. Pick them in the main menu under MODS.
• CD music: save the CD audio tracks as blood02.ogg, blood03.ogg, and so on, then turn on OPTIONS > SOUND > REDBOOK AUDIO.

What NotBlood Chosen adds to NotBlood:

Bots (new in 1.2).

• Computer players that play like people. They hide, jump, chase, flee, ambush you at doorways, flank, take the high ground, ride lifts and open doors. They only know what a player could know: what they see and hear, and where they last saw you.
• 4 difficulties (easy, normal, hard, nightmare) and 6 personalities (balanced, rusher, camper, trickster, coward, jumper), or a mix of them.
• FINE TUNING for all bots: aim, reaction time, aggression, jumping, ambushes, flanking, camping, high ground, taunts, the cultist look, and how much damage they take. GRUDGES and ADAPTIVE DIFFICULTY are optional.
• SET EACH BOT (new in 1.2): give each bot its own name, difficulty, personality, team, damage and fine tuning.
• Offline: MULTIPLAYER > PLAY WITH BOTS, plus a 10-match CAREER and WATCH BOTS (only bots play while you watch).
• In LAN and online games (new in 1.2): the host adds bots in the MULTIPLAYER setup under BOTS. The host's computer plays them, so everybody sees the same bots.
• BOT ORDERS (ESC): follow me, hold this spot, go ahead. These are for the bots on your side in co-op and teams.

Match types and mutators.

• Bloodbath: normal, gun game, king of the hill, juggernaut, last man standing.
• Teams (new in 1.2: all four modes): team bloodbath, capture the flag, king of the hill, last team standing.
• Co-op: normal, survival (waves of monsters).
• SET TEAMS (new in 1.2): put every player and bot on AUTO, BLUE or RED. Uneven teams are allowed.
• Mutators: low or moon gravity, vampire, one-hit kills, random or single weapon.
• MATCH STATS: frags, deaths, aim, best streak, favourite weapon, nemesis.

Co-op saves.

• 8 slots, saved on every player's machine.
• Load where you saved (positions, keys, enemies) or restart the level with your gear.
• Players get their saves by name. New players start with the pitchfork. When somebody leaves, the game saves itself.

Online and LAN.

• Online lobbies through your own relay server (how to run it: SERVER.md). They are protected by a key and need no port forwarding. There is no default server: enter your own server's address and key.
• A live dashboard in the browser: lobbies, players' health, armor, weapons and keys, a live level map and an event list.
• FIND LAN GAMES. The host screen shows your address, and you get clear messages when versions or mods differ.

Everything else.

• MODS menu for add-on episodes and mods. A mod that breaks the start is switched off again.
• Cutscenes from the CD's movie folder in any upper or lower case.
• Touch controls, gyro aiming and render scale on Android and iPad. The touch buttons hide while a controller is connected.
• A macOS app (Apple Silicon and Intel) that needs no administrator. Android keeps everything in the NotBlood folder.
• Settings are saved whenever a menu closes. On Android there is a crash report in notblood.log.

New in 1.2:

• Bots, the match types, mutators and match stats (all of these were only in the bots test builds before).
• Bots in LAN and online games, SET EACH BOT and SET TEAMS.
• Team bloodbath without flags, and last team standing.
• MODE now sits right under GAME in GAME SETTINGS.
• No default online server.
• Android: the black sky, explosions turning the world black, settings not being kept and slow drawing are fixed.

apps.subtitle: PC Emulator for iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
Fathom:

An x86-64 PC emulator for iOS. Fathom runs x86-64 Linux programs on an iPhone or iPad by translating them to ARM64 as they execute, using FEXCore — the dynamic recompiler behind FEX-Emu — with a native SwiftUI front end.

What it does:

Import an x86-64 Linux executable, open it, press Run. Fathom maps it into a guest address space, hands its instructions to FEXCore's JIT, answers its Linux syscalls, and shows you its output.

The emulator core is genuinely doing the work: FEXCore compiles the guest's x86-64 basic blocks into ARM64 at runtime, and Fathom supplies the kernel half — an ELF loader, a guest address space, and a Linux syscall layer covering files, memory, time, and process basics.

An x86-64 PC emulator for iOS, running guest code on FEXCore.

JSRF Unleashed:

Jet Set Radio Future, running natively on Mac, Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone and iPad. Not an emulator — the game's own code, statically recompiled into C and built as a native application.

This project is about one game. It is not an Xbox emulator and it will not run other Xbox titles. Everything here — the graphics translation, the audio path, the file layout, the per-function fixes — is aimed at getting Jet Set Radio Future right. If you want to run Xbox games in general, you want xemu; if you want to port a different Xbox title, you want the toolkit this is built on.

versions.localizedDescription:
Jet Set Radio Future, natively on Mac, Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone and iPad. You need your own copy of the game (the USA release): these downloads are the engine only.

Android: on-screen controls and controllers on more phones:

Two players saw the intro play with no on-screen controls, and their Bluetooth controllers (an Xbox Series X controller, an 8BitDo Ultimate 2) did nothing. Many phones list one of their own parts as a gamepad: the device their fingerprint reader or side buttons send keys through declares gamepad buttons. The app counted it as a controller and hid the on-screen controls, and it was also opened first, as player 1's controller, so a real controller went in as player 2's, which the game does not read.

A device now counts as a controller only if it has a stick, or a d-pad that reports as one. On those phones the on-screen controls show, and a controller connected to them is player 1's. The log (Android/data/com.jumatt.jsrfunleashed/files/Logs/last-run.log) now says what the app made of each device Android calls a gamepad, and whether the on-screen controls are showing: if your phone still misbehaves, those [PAD] lines are what to send.

Tested in the Android emulator with a stand-in for such a phone part, there from the start, and a controller connected 20 seconds in that pressed Start and A. With 0.4.6 the on-screen controls were missing and the controller did nothing; with 0.4.7 the controls showed, went away when the controller connected, and the controller started the game.

The APK installs over the previous one. Only the Android download is new: the others are 0.4.6's, unchanged (0.4.6 fixed the black city in the Skyscraper District and Pharaoh Park on every platform).

apps.name: Kant
apps.subtitle: Private, end-to-end encrypted messenger. No phone number, no one in the middle: messages go device to device, and relays only carry what they can't read
apps.localizedDescription:
Kant is a free, open-source messenger with no phone number, no email address and no company server keeping a copy of your messages. They're encrypted on your device and decrypted only on the devices of the people you're talking to.

Devices behind home routers, mobile data and office firewalls can't usually reach each other directly, so a relay passes the encrypted messages between them. A relay can't read what it carries and doesn't store it. Anyone can run one: on a server, on a computer at home without opening a port, or inside the Kant desktop app itself.

Kant is in public beta and hasn't had an independent security audit yet. The threat model and kant.network/security say exactly what has been checked and what hasn't.

versions.localizedDescription:
Kant 0.6.0 (Beta):

Kant on Mac and iPhone, and anyone can host a relay without opening a single port.

New:

• Mac. Kant for macOS, for Apple Silicon (Kant-0.6.0-mac-arm64.dmg) and Intel Macs (Kant-0.6.0-mac-x64.dmg), with the same built-in relay as the Linux and Windows apps. It isn't notarized by Apple yet, so the first time you open it macOS says it can't verify the developer: open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway (check the file's SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt first).
• iPhone. Kant for iOS 15 and later, as Kant-0.6.0.ipa for sideloading (with AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly), since it isn't on the App Store yet. Unlock with Face ID or Touch ID, open and save files through the share sheet, and get notifications while Kant is open or for about 30 seconds after you leave it. Notifications while Kant is closed need Apple push, which needs an Apple developer account. With a free Apple ID, sideloaded apps have to be refreshed every 7 days.
• Host a relay without port forwarding. Run a relay from any computer at home, even behind a router you can't configure or a mobile connection, through Tailscale, Tailscale Funnel, Cloudflare Tunnel or ngrok. One command sets it up, checks it from the outside and prints the address to share: scripts/relay-tunnel.sh funnel. See RELAY_TUNNELS.md.
• Easier relay deployment on a server. scripts/deploy-relay.sh asks what it needs (HTTPS with a domain, or HTTP on a local network), checks that the domain points at the server, gets the certificate, and makes the keys for desktop notifications itself. No Firebase, no push proxy and no key tools are needed to run a relay.

Fixed:

• Desktop notifications from self-hosted relays. Relays only accepted Web Push keys in an unusual format, so keys made with the standard tool (the one the instructions pointed to) silently didn't work. Both formats work now, and a relay with bad keys says so when it starts.
• HTTPS relays without Firebase. The HTTPS setup refused to start unless Firebase settings were filled in, which only the official relay has. It starts without them now.
• Certificates for new HTTPS relays. The setup used a placeholder email that Let's Encrypt rejects, so the certificate could fail. It now asks for your email.
• Local-network relays set up with deploy-relay.sh --mode http told apps to connect to 0.0.0.0, which never works. They now use the machine's network address.
• Typing a Tailscale address (like 100.101.102.103:3001) as your relay now connects over http://, as other local addresses do.

Everything 0.5.0 was tested with, plus:

• the iPhone app in the iOS Simulator: onboarding, messages both ways with another Kant user, and Face ID unlock.

• a relay hosted at home through a real Tailscale Funnel: messages, a 1 MB file and the app's screens, all through the tunnel.
• relays reached through a single port (as every tunnel works): messages, groups, files, relays restarting and phones switching off and on, on one relay and across two linked relays.
• ten minutes of connections held open through an HTTPS proxy without a drop.

JIT on iOS 26 (Trusted Execution Monitor):

iCube runs the JIT recompiler again on iOS 26. TXM will not execute a freshly written code page until a debugger has written to that page, so iCube asks an attached broker to touch every page of its 288 MB code region once at startup. After that the broker can detach and the region stays usable for the life of the process.

• Users: see JIT & Performance for how to turn it on with StikDebug, what to expect without it, and troubleshooting.

apps.localizedDescription:
VoxelTrail for iOS:

A native iOS build of the Gen 1 recomp engine — the Generation 1 Pokémon games, reimplemented in Lua on LÖVE — with the Dramatic Shape voxel mod built in, so the overworld can be played as a 3D diorama or in first person.

You need your own ROM. None is included here and none will be. The app reads a Game Boy ROM you already own and extracts its data on first launch.

Load your ROM:

Two ways, no computer needed for either.

With the picker — tap Import ROM, choose your .gb / .gbc file from Files, and wait for extraction. It runs once, takes a few seconds, and after that the game boots straight in.

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned IPA — install with SideStore or AltStore. Requires iOS 16+, tested on iOS 26.6. Bring your own ROM.

Pokémon Stadium battle models:

3D BATTLES can fight with the Pokémon Stadium models instead of the flat Game Boy pictures — STADIUM A on the map, STADIUM B on two discs against the sky.

You supply the cartridge. Import Stadium ROM in the launcher's MODS panel, or STADIUM ROM in the options menu, opens the Files picker for your Pokémon Stadium (US) 1.0 file. The models are built on your device, once, and the ROM is read and forgotten rather than kept.

That picker is new work on my side: iOS had no way to hand the mod a cartridge at all, so it printed a sandbox path and asked you to put a file somewhere a phone cannot reach. Now upstream as.

US 1.0 specifically — every model offset is measured against that revision. Another one builds, and the screen tells you the models may be wrong.

The battle HUD reads the right way round:

1.7.2 draws the battle HUD mirrored on iOS — PIKACHU, the HP numbers and L100 all backwards, while FIGHT/ITEM/RUN reads fine. It comes from a fix that assumes iOS presents the HUD canvas upside down and corrects for it; this build's renderer doesn't flip it, so the correction was the mirror. Fixed, and the frosted panels behind the HUD come back with it.

More of the mod:

• RENDER DIST — FIT / WIDE / WIDER / WIDEST / OFF. The first thing to reach for if 3D runs slowly: FIT skips whole connected maps before they cost anything.
• Fog and god rays in Viridian Forest, every battle location rebuilt, and a lot of new voxel work — diner stools, mansion desks, CUT trees.
• ROUND WORLD gained two rungs, GLOBE and PLANET. PLANET is a true half-sphere: the town sitting on a little world.

The Stadium screens and the whole STADIUM ROM flow are translated. Two older gaps closed: CANCEL was the one English word left on a fully Spanish options menu — structurally unreachable, now fixed and — and ten strings carried Ñ, ¿ or ¡ onto the 8×8 font, which has no glyph for any of them and drew holes instead.

The translation is.

Kept from before:

The live-tuning panel, the look stick, readable setting names, third person, the battle camera, and Spanish Red/Blue ROM support.

🇪🇸 En español:

IPA sin firmar — instalalo con SideStore o AltStore. Requiere iOS 16 o posterior; probado en iOS 26.6. Necesitas tu propia ROM.

📖 Instrucciones completas en español.

Modelos de combate de Pokemon Stadium:

COMBATES 3D puede pelear con los modelos de Pokemon Stadium en vez de con las imagenes planas de Game Boy: STADIUM A sobre el mapa, STADIUM B sobre dos discos contra el cielo.

El cartucho lo pones tu. Importar ROM de Stadium, en el panel de MODS del menu inicial, o ROM STADIUM en las opciones, abre el selector de Archivos para tu Pokemon Stadium (US) 1.0. Los modelos se crean en tu dispositivo una sola vez, y la ROM se lee y se olvida en lugar de guardarse.

Ese selector es trabajo nuevo de mi parte: en iOS no habia forma de entregarle un cartucho al mod, asi que imprimia una ruta interna y te pedia dejar un archivo en un sitio al que un telefono no llega.

US 1.0 en concreto: cada medida de los modelos esta tomada de esa revision. Otra distinta se construye igual, pero la pantalla te avisa de que pueden salir mal.

El HUD de combate se lee del derecho:

La 1.7.2 dibuja el HUD de combate reflejado en iOS: PIKACHU, los numeros de PS y L100 al reves, mientras que LUCHA/OBJETO/HUIR se lee bien. Viene de un arreglo que da por hecho que iOS presenta ese lienzo del reves y lo corrige; el motor de esta version no lo voltea, asi que la correccion era el reflejo. Arreglado, y los paneles esmerilados de detras del HUD vuelven con ello.

Mas del mod:

• DISTANCIA — AJUSTE / LEJOS / MAS LEJOS / MAXIMO / NO. Lo primero que tocar si el 3D va lento: AJUSTE descarta mapas enteros antes de que cuesten nada.
• Niebla y rayos de sol en el Bosque Verde, todas las localizaciones de combate rehechas, y mucho trabajo nuevo de voxeles.
• MUNDO CURVO gano dos niveles, GLOBO y PLANETA. PLANETA es media esfera de verdad: el pueblo sobre un planeta pequeño.

Las pantallas de Stadium y todo el proceso de ROM STADIUM estan traducidos. Se cierran dos huecos antiguos: CANCELAR era la unica palabra en ingles que quedaba en un menu de opciones completamente en español, y diez textos llevaban Ñ, ¿ o ¡ a la fuente de 8x8, que no tiene glifo para ninguno y dibujaba huecos.

Se mantiene todo lo anterior:

El panel de ajuste en vivo, la palanca de vista, los nombres legibles de los ajustes, la tercera persona, la camara de combate y el soporte de ROMs de Rojo y Azul en español.

**An iOS feed reader for Archive of Our Own and Ambrosia. An unofficial AO3 reading application. **.

apps.localizedDescription:
MCX360 Edition: Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition for iPhone:

A native iOS port of Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition (Title Update 9), built with the ReXGlue static recompilation SDK. The Xbox 360 code is recompiled ahead of time to run natively on iPhone. Graphics run through Vulkan on Metal via MoltenVK. Developer mode MIGHT be required on older and newer iOS, enable it going trough: Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom, toggle on Developer Mode, and restart your device.

You need your own copy of the game. This release does not include the game's data files (textures, sounds, worlds, the original default.xex). You provide them from a disc and title update you own. This project is not affiliated with Mojang, Microsoft, or 4J Studios.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

• On-screen touch controls, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with touch_controls, touch_controls_opacity and touch_haptics in mc360.toml.
• Save thumbnails: your worlds now show a picture in the world list.
• Exit Game now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen.

Performance:

• Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds.
• Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (framerate_limit, default 60).
• The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores.
• Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame.

Fixes:

• Fixed random crashes after playing for a while.
• Fixed choppy audio.
• Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed.
• Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing.

Known issues:

• Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps.
• The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save.
• Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement.

Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.

apps.localizedDescription:
tangoAW2:

Rollback netplay for Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising (GBA, USA).

A fork of Tango (mGBA, rollback, matchmaking) for Advance Wars 2. Both players run the real game in its own Versus mode; your ROM is never modified (changes are applied in memory). No game is included: you need your own dump of the USA cartridge.

Get it:

Download the latest build from.

changed is in each release's notes): Windows (.exe installer), macOS on Apple Silicon (.dmg, not signed: right-click the app and choose Open the first time), Linux (.AppImage), or iPhone and iPad (.ipa, iOS 16 or later: install it with AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly; it plays with on-screen buttons or a controller at 60 to 120 Hz, sideways fitted between the buttons or stretched (Settings > Graphics), and online with desktop players).

versions.localizedDescription:
tangoAW2 0.8.0: Online overhaul.

The iPhone/iPad .ipa and the Apple Silicon Mac build are included as usual.

Online rooms of 2 to 5 players.

• One shared match for the whole room: every player's game runs the same console, with each waiting player watching the match in a window of their own.
• Armies screen of its own: each player picks a CO and a colour no other army has; teams (2v1, 2v2, 3v1, 3v2 .), a team wins together (partners get VICTORY, the beaten team DEFEAT).
• A player who has been eliminated may leave the match without ending it for the others. A living player who drops keeps the 60 second reconnect window and the match is saved for RESUME.
• Host migration: when the host of a room of 3 to 5 leaves (quits, crashes or freezes) after being eliminated, the match does not pause and is not saved: the lowest-numbered player still in the match becomes the host, the others reconnect to them automatically (same room, through the matchmaking server or the relay), and play continues after a few seconds, behind a message box ("Host left. NAME is hosting now. Reconnecting."). Everyone keeps the same game state; the new host's name is marked "host" in the status bar. A host who is still playing and quits makes way the same way; one who is simply lost gets the 60 second window first. Either way the army of a host who was still playing yields, as if its player had chosen Yield. If the new host cannot be reached within 20 seconds the match is saved for RESUME as before.
• A player whose game freezes or whose device sleeps is noticed after 5 seconds of silence (short hiccups are ignored) and gets the same reconnect window; if they come back in time the match goes on.
• The reconnect countdown is an AW2 message box ("Waiting for NAME to reconnect. 40s", B: Disconnect) over the match picture.

Picking the map.

• Every player proposes a map in turn on the game's own SELECT MAP; one of the proposals is drawn.
• Every player has 120 seconds to pick (a countdown is shown on every window); when it runs out, the map under their cursor is their pick.
• The draw is a roulette: every proposal is hidden as "?????", the highlight runs round the proposals, slows down and lands on one, whose "?????" turns into the map's name beside its owner's gamertag, with the map's picture next to it on the same screen. The map stays up for 9 seconds (a countdown shows), or until the host presses A. The chosen map is named on the army screen and the Rules page.
• SELECT MAP shows only the maps for the room's player count, on two tabs: "NP" and "NP Predeploy". Pre-deployed means the map starts with units placed and has no base, airport or port (owned or neutral).
• Pentagon Atoll, a 35 x 35 pre-deployed map for five armies (no production at all: every army starts with the same forty units, among them a Megatank, a Stealth and three B-Copters; rivers, bridges, roads and a central lagoon), is the first 5P Predeploy map.
• Maps that need Dual Strike content (the Black Crystal and Black Obelisk maps, Pentagon Atoll, and every other map with Dual Strike art or units) are offered online only when EVERY player of the room has the Dual Strike pack, and offline only with the pack. The lobby decides this when the match starts, so a player without the pack never sees a proposal they cannot play, and every window lists the same maps.
• The map list holds up to 110 maps per tab (it stopped at 50 before) and no longer garbles names while it scrolls.

Online connection that fails over.

• Every free public service online play uses is now a list with automatic failover and load balancing: the matchmaking server (5 s each, then the list again twice with a short backoff, then "Matchmaking unreachable - try again, or join by code"), 11 public STUN servers (checked with one binding request, 3 handed to each connection, shuffled per session), the lobby browser's 10 public Nostr relays (each client uses at most 3 and swaps one that fails; a host announces on 3 and a browser listens on 3, picked so they always meet), and the Tango TURN relay (no other free public TURN exists).
• Polite to the services: a failure backs a server off 5 s, 10 s, 20 s. up to 10 min (jittered, kept across restarts); "blocked", "rate limited", 403 or 429 backs it off for an hour or more; a lobby is announced every 15-20 s (never more than 12 events a minute on a relay); health checks are one STUN request per server at most every 5 minutes, only while the ONLINE menu is open or a connection is made, never during a match.
• The ONLINE screen shows Online / Limited / Offline in its top middle, and R opens a Connection page: matchmaking, lobby browser relays, direct connect (STUN), relay fallback (TURN), time of the last check.
• Advanced (hidden): TANGOAW2_EXTRA_SIGNALING / _STUN / _TURN / _NOSTR (comma separated) add your own servers; TANGOAW2_ONLINE_LOG=1 logs which endpoint was used.

Offline Versus.

• SELECT MAP lists the maps by player count as well: "2P", "2P Predeploy", "3P". "5P Predeploy" (empty tabs are skipped). L and R pressed together swap them for AW2's own lists (Classic, Vs. Maps, Pre-Deployed, 3P Maps, 4P Maps, War Room, Design Maps, 5P Maps) and back; the choice is kept until you quit. L or R alone still change the tab; SELECT on a 2P Dual Strike map still marks the second front.
• Every map is on exactly one player-count tab (AW2's, the Dual Strike pack's and tangoAW2's). War Room mode itself is unchanged.

Waiting windows.

• A waiting player watches the mover's walks play out, with the camera sliding to the action at the game's own pace; with Fog of War, only what that player can see. The mover's own menus, cursor and questions are never shown. Captures are shown to the players who see the cell; the game's own messages (an army has lost) go to everyone.

Look.

• The new online screens, hints, status and timers use AW2's own plates, windows and font. A password room shows its password to the host and a padlock to guests.

iPhone and iPad.

• Tested against the Mac app in 2 and 3 player rooms, UNRANKED, relay-only and a resumed match; the game picture now fills the width of an upright iPhone.
• A key held as a match begins (the START that started the room) is no longer passed to the game: a resumed match opened AW2's overview for the host.

Known limits.

• After a host migration the departed player's seat never gets READY, so the room cannot start another match (B goes back to the lobby). A guest (not the host) who is still playing and drops keeps the 60 second window and the saved match.
• "5P Predeploy" has one map, and it needs the Dual Strike pack: without the pack that tab stays empty.
• A fog-on walk can still make the camera jump a few pixels as it begins.

Updating: online, everyone in a room needs 0.8.0.

Reynard Browser:

Reynard is a Gecko-based web browser for iOS 13+.

Unlike other browsers on iOS that are forced to use Apple's WebKit engine (including Safari and all third-party browsers), Reynard uses Gecko. This is the same engine that powers the Firefox browser on desktop and Android devices.

Besides providing an alternative, up-to-date browser engine[^1], Reynard supports Firefox add-ons, including more capable ad-blocking extensions, along with privacy features such as Enhanced Tracking Protection and DNS over HTTPS.

iOS 14 (iPhone 6S Plus, 14.1):

These sites are known to break or render incorrectly on iOS 14. The screenshots below compare how they load in Safari versus Reynard.

iOS 26 (iPhone 13 mini, 26.1):

Improvements:

• Improved audio handling, with better echo cancellation, voice processing, recovery after interruptions, and handling of audio device changes.

versions.localizedDescription:
Playport 0.4.0: GOG, Epic Games and your own games:

Playport is no longer only for Steam. Sign in to GOG or Epic Games and install your games from there, or bring any DRM-free PC game from Files. Games now sign in to their store as they would on a PC.

🛒 GOG and Epic Games:

In Settings › Accounts, next to Steam, you can now sign in to GOG and Epic Games (the setup checklist's Accounts step offers all three). Your Windows games from each store show up in the Library, with their own filter and the store's artwork.

• If Epic's sign-in asks you to do something first, such as accept an updated privacy policy, the sign-in sheet tells you what. Do that on Epic's site, then press Try again.
• Games that use anti-cheat or another company's launcher are refused before the install, and their page says why.

A game now gets what its store's launcher would give it, with nothing to set up:

• Epic: every Epic game starts signed in to your Epic account, including games that check you own them. Games using Epic Online Services sign in too: Snakebird Complete reaches its menu signed in.
• Steam: games get the tickets Steam gives them on a PC, so online sign-ins through Steam work. Valheim logs in to its online service this way.
• GOG: games built with GOG Galaxy sign in to it. Moonscars signs in.
• Sign-in pages in a panel. When a game opens a web page, such as Epic's "Allow" page the first time an online game signs in, it appears in a panel over the game; close it to go back to the game.

📁 Add a game from Files:

Have a DRM-free PC game already? Press X in the Library, or choose Add a game, and pick its folder or a .zip from Files. Playport copies it into its own drive and adds it to your Library under Local. Pick the game's .exe on its page if Playport doesn't find it.

Installers (setup.exe) are not run: pick the installed game's folder instead. For GOG games, use the GOG account. It needs no installer.

🚪 Death's Door runs on:

Some Unity games, such as Death's Door, quit after about 14 seconds because Windows ran out of address space for them. Playport now places those allocations where there is room, and Death's Door plays into the game.

Also new:

• iOS 26.0 fix: 0.3.3 closed at launch on iOS 26.0.x. It starts again.
• Steam demos show in your Library.
• Report a problem shares one zip with the game's logs.
• A Memory step on the first-run checklist shows whether your sideloader kept the increased memory limit. How to fix says which sideloaders keep it. The setup also explains why it needs pairing and LocalDevVPN.
• Online games connect more often: web connections trust the usual certificates, and games see the phone's network instead of thinking it is offline.
• Faster and steadier: quicker thread synchronisation and code translation, a smoother Vulkan path, and a fix for a rare freeze in Hollow Knight's menus.
• Newer components: Wine 11.19 with Valve's latest Proton Wine changes, and current FEX, DXMT, DXVK, vkd3d-proton and Mesa.

The README and playport.dev now walk you through setup:

• Install, by sideloader. Which sideloaders keep the increased memory limit (AltStore Classic 2.2 or later, Impactor and Xcode do; SideStore with a free Apple ID does not), and why it matters: without it an 8 GB iPhone gives Playport about 3.3 GB.
• SideStore: when Memory has no tick. A one-time fix with GetMoreRam that adds the limit to Playport's App ID; SideStore's weekly refresh then keeps it.
• Why pairing, JIT and LocalDevVPN, and Do I need a computer? (once, to install; after that it depends on your sideloader).
• Your first game: sign in, Install, connect a controller, Play.
• Reporting a problem: Report a problem on the game's page, save the zip toThe form asks for the device, iOS and Playport versions, sideloader and JIT method.shows every game we and players have tried, with its status. Played one, working or not? Report it and it goes on the list.

Good to know:

• Not working yet: Among Us crashes, Monster Train (GOG) shows a black screen, and Jurassic World Evolution (Epic) does not start.
• Valheim: pick DXMT on its page. On Vulkan its picture is black.
• Sign-in panels for 32-bit games don't open yet; 64-bit games are covered.
• Tested on one phone (iOS 27.0) with Hollow Knight and Valheim from Steam, Moonscars and Shogun Showdown from GOG, Death's Door and Snakebird from Epic, and an imported folder. If a game from GOG or Epic misbehaves, please tell us which one.
• Your Steam games, saves and login are untouched by this update.

Download Playport-0.4.0.ipa and sideload it with your own Apple ID, keeping the increased memory limit and the JIT helper extension. If you have an earlier version, install over it: your games, saves and logins stay. Bring your own games from Steam, GOG, Epic Games or Files.

The complete Corresponding Source of this exact build, the notices and the rebuild instructions are attached as Playport-0.4.0-source.tar, NOTICES.tar and INSTALL-REBUILD.tar. SHA256SUMS covers every file.

Playport is GPL-3.0-or-later; every component keeps its own licence.

apps.name: zanzibarr
apps.subtitle: zanzibarr streams NZB content from Usenet without downloading — instant start, true seek, PAR2 repair, Dolby Vision. Windows · macOS · Linux · Android · Android TV · iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
zanzibarr turns Usenet into your personal streaming library. Point it at any .nzb and the video starts playing in seconds — no download queue, no waiting for the full file, no disk space sacrificed. Scrub to the final scene of a 4K remux before the first act would have finished downloading. It feels like magic; it's really just a very disciplined engine.

Why zanzibarr is different:

Play instantly, never download The Rust engine maps every seek position to the exact Usenet segments that hold it, fetches only those, decodes yEnc on the fly and serves the result through a lazy, range-aware local stream. Pause the player and the network goes quiet. Close the app and nothing is left behind on your disk.

versions.localizedDescription:
zanzibarr v1.9 — season-pack picker polish:

Stream anything from Usenet. Own nothing. Wait for nothing. zanzibarr plays NZB content without downloading it — instant start, frame-accurate seek, and nothing left behind on your disk.

What's new in v1.9:

• Episode numbers are finally visible. Posts that write subjects as "<directory>/<file>" used to bury the episode number behind the long batch directory name. The picker now shows the actual file name and wraps long titles to two lines — the continue-watching cards and the player title got the same treatment.
• Episodes in natural order. The picker no longer sorts by size, which scrambled equal-sized episodes; entries now follow natural name ordering — E9 before E10, with NCOP/NCED extras listed after the episodes.
• No more ghost codec errors. A harmless mpv error event (an audio codec falling back from hardware to software decoding) used to pop an 8-second error banner during perfectly healthy playback. Post-startup errors are now shown only if playback actually stops progressing.

(All three reported on GitHub issue #5 — thanks for the precise follow-up!).

Already inside:

• Cast to your TV — Chromecast & AirPlay; the receiver pulls straight from zanzibarr's token-gated LAN endpoint.
• Built-in indexer search — Newznab search with quality badges, tap-to-play inside the app.
• Multi-file NZB picker — choose the episode inside season packs, fully D-pad navigable.
• Obfuscated NZB sets — hash-named RAR volumes identified by content, reordered by embedded volume numbers.
• Archive-aware — multi-volume RAR5/RAR4 (incl. -hp encrypted) and 7z (STORE, LZMA/LZMA2 solid, AES-256) reassembled in memory.
• Compressed RAR, seekable — volumes that actually compress stream too: decode-ahead serves the player while unpacking continues.
• PAR2 repair — missing/corrupt segments rebuilt with Reed-Solomon, byte-exact against par2cmdline.
• Full picture pipeline — SDR / HDR / HDR10 / Dolby Vision selector with BT.2390 tone mapping; TrueHD/Atmos, DTS-HD MA, AV1.
• Android TV, fully remote-driven — settings, indexer setup and search work end-to-end with a D-pad, with visible focus everywhere.
• Continue watching — playback positions remembered per episode, with a resume row on the home screen.
• Smart Canvas — draw your own crop with live aspect preview, applied on the GPU.
• In-app updates — zanzibarr checks for new versions itself; Android installs them in place with one tap.
• Player essentials — PiP, frame stepping, speed, audio sync, external audio/subtitle loading, double-click ±10 s seek, subtitle color & font pickers, fit ↔ fill toggle.
• 14 languages — EN, TR, ES, DE, FR, PT, IT, RU, ZH, JA, KO, HI, AR, FA (RTL included), dark & light themes.
• Private by design — NNTP credentials live only in the OS keychain; no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Getting started:

• Install the build for your platform.
• Open the settings gear and enter your Usenet provider's NNTP details.
• Open any .nzb (or search with the built-in indexer) and press play.

apps.name: Applesauce
apps.subtitle: A playful emulator for iOS. Plays supported 32-bit iPhone games on iOS 15+ — no jailbreak needed, though JIT is. An unaffiliated fork of touchHLE and HyperHLE; neither project endorses it
apps.localizedDescription:
Applesauce:

A playful emulator for iOS. It plays supported 32-bit iPhone games on modern iPhones — no jailbreak required, though JIT is. It installs and runs on iPadOS too, but every game runs as an iPhone guest for now: the core's iPad device families are not yet reachable from the app.

Applesauce is an unaffiliated fork. The emulation is entirely the work of touchHLE and its fork HyperHLE; this project is the iOS app built around them — the interface, the build system and the packaging. Neither project is connected to Applesauce or endorses it, so please report problems here rather than to them. No games or Apple software are included.

versions.localizedDescription:
Applesauce 0.4.1:

This update improves the library, game-session cleanup and AltStore Classic distribution. It keeps the same bundle identifier as 0.4.0, so it updates an existing Applesauce installation and retains its library and saves.

In AltStore Classic, open Sources → + and add:

Choose Applesauce from the source. Future releases appear in AltStore; you do not have to download a new IPA manually each time. Signing, refresh and JIT requirements still apply. The source does not enable JIT automatically.

Full installation and JIT guide.

Fixes:

• Importing copies files away from the main UI thread and coordinates access with Files providers such as iCloud Drive. A failed copy is cleaned up before it can appear as a partially imported game.
• Repeated taps cannot queue overlapping game launches. Library reloads are also suppressed while a game or import is active.
• Malformed game metadata that causes the HyperHLE parser to panic is caught at the native bridge. The library uses this parser regardless of the chosen gameplay core and falls back to a filename when metadata is unreadable.
• The FPS timer no longer retains the game-controls screen after exiting.
• The exit button respects the screen's safe area, and returning to the library uses the iOS 15 orientation fallback too.

• Building a second core copies only that core, avoiding accidental overwrite of a newer core with a stale file from another checkout.

• Migration instructions include saves and correctly explain which settings need to be reselected.

The AltStore source is checked against the unsigned IPA's version, build, minimum iOS, size, checksum and permissions. A release workflow updates the source for future published releases; prereleases and TrollStore packages are excluded from that automatic update.

Downloads:

• Applesauce-iOS-unsigned.ipa: AltStore Classic and other ordinary sideloaders.
• Applesauce-iOS-trollstore.ipa: the existing TrollStore route for supported older iOS devices, with JIT enabled through TrollStore.
• Applesauce-iOS-trollstore-permanent-jit.ipa: A11 and older only. Do not install this variant on A12 or newer devices.

The emulator versions remain HyperHLE v1.0.6 and touchHLE 0.2.3. This release does not claim additional game compatibility or fix the known Sims Medieval.

fresh device regression testing of 0.4.1 is still needed.

No games are included. Full credit for emulation belongs to touchHLE and HyperHLE. Applesauce is an independent, unofficial port.

apps.subtitle: TwitchUnblock is an open-source Twitch client that lets you watch VODs and
apps.localizedDescription:
🟣 TwitchUnblock:

TwitchUnblock is an open-source Twitch client that lets you watch VODs and live streams without a subscription, at full quality. Native iOS app built with SwiftUI — also available in your browser.

🤖 Vibe-coded project. TwitchUnblock is built with AI coding assistants (prompted, reviewed and tested by a human). Expect rough edges: bug reports on Discord help a lot.

Install it and it works. There is nothing to configure, no server to set up, no key to paste. The backend is already hosted and shared by every install.

Watching:

• 🚫 No subscription required — watch any VOD or live stream at full quality.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automatic build of the master branch on 2026-10-15.

• Polls: the developer can ask a question under the home announcement; vote without an account, change your mind until it ends, and see the results once you've voted.
• Settings → Channel points tracks, like drops, the time you watched and the points you earned by watching: right now, in total and per channel.
• Predictions show, like the Twitch app, the points bet on each outcome, its return ratio, how many people bet and the biggest bet, plus what your bet would win.
• The Home live list refreshes on its own when you come back to the app and every 3 minutes while it's on screen.
• While a live loads, the player says which source it's trying and can be minimized or closed; the screen now only stays awake while a video plays on screen (paused, minimized or audio only, it sleeps).
• Apple's player (immersive player off) resumes VODs and clips where they were, even after a quality change, and its lock screen activity follows pause and progress; the sleep timer now also stops multi-live.
• Closing the player or starting another video during Picture in Picture now ends it cleanly, changing quality keeps your place, and a stream that drops shows a Retry button instead of freezing.
• When no source can play a live stream, or Twitch doesn't answer, the player now says so with a Retry button instead of calling the channel offline; lives also start when Twitch's own API is unreachable.
• Cloud sync keeps each Twitch account's history apart, and a VOD or channel you delete in the app is removed from the backup right away.
• A category you follow on Twitch now shows as followed on its page and can be unfollowed there; category lists get Retry and pull to refresh.
• Search opens clip links and starts VOD links at their?t= time; channel pages open faster, and the VOD filter can look through older VODs.
• Restoring an expired Twitch web session now asks you to sign in again, and drops stop counting for an account you signed out of.
• Playback resumes on its own after a call or another app's audio: VODs where they left off, live streams back at live.
• Opening the app no longer stops music playing in another app: the sound only switches over when a video starts, and goes back to that app when you close the player.
• Multi-live now mixes lives and VODs (up to 4 videos): add a VOD from the player's ⋯ menu, by long-pressing a VOD card or My VODs, or by pasting its link or ID in the mosaic.
• VOD tiles resume where you left off, with play/pause, ±10 s, a seek bar and “Watch again”; their progress is saved and synced.

• The multi-live “+” accepts a channel link or @name.

• Subscribed to a channel (or Turbo)? With the web session connected, its lives now play through your Twitch account, without ad breaks (Settings → Player → Watch ad-free with my sub).
• During a channel's ad break, the player now explains the purple “Commercial break in progress” screen, shows when the stream comes back and mutes the sound meanwhile.
• Live source descriptions no longer claim the proxies are ad-free: they still get the channel's ad breaks.

• Reopening a VOD in the same session no longer shows its restored muted parts in orange on the progress bar.
• Muted parts of recent VODs in the MP4 format keep their sound again when Twitch still serves it, instead of being swapped for the silent version.
• Emote cards also open from a message thread, with sharp FrankerFaceZ emotes and badges.
• Emote cards now show the scope and author of BetterTTV, FFZ and 7TV emotes, the 7TV original name, zero-width and modifier emotes, and a link to the emote's page.
• Twitch emote cards show the emote type (global, sub tier, channel points), the channel it belongs to (live or not, with See channel) and its other sub emotes of the same tier.

• Long-press an emote in the emote picker to open its card or copy its name; the picker is now translated.
• VoiceOver can open emote and badge cards.

• Unfollowing from the player or a channel page now asks for confirmation, with a shortcut to hide the player Follow button.
• Hype train: the bar shows the progress of the current level.
• Hide a channel or a category from Top and Categories with a long-press, and show it again from Settings → General.
• Apple TV: hide channels and categories too (press and hold a card).
• A channel's VODs load past the first 100 again.
• Without an account, categories, live channels in a category and a channel's clips now load past the first 100.
• Without an account, top streams on Home get a Load more button (30 at a time).
• Preferred quality in Settings → Player (Source, 1080p, 720p, 480p, 360p, 160p or audio only): lives, VODs and clips start in it, or in the closest one below when the channel doesn't have it.

• Qualities are sorted by height then frame rate, and "audio_only" now reads "Audio only".

• Apple TV: preferred quality in Account → Settings, with the same closest-below rule.
• Playback speed for VODs and clips (0.25× to 2×) in the ⋯ menu of the player; the VOD speed is remembered, shown next to the timer, and live streams always stay at normal speed.
• The lock screen and the Live Activity follow the playback speed of a VOD.
• Resuming from Picture-in-Picture now updates the play/pause button.
• Live streams no longer speed up to catch up with the live edge, which could pull the sound out of sync; the player now makes a small jump only when it really falls behind.

• When the developer replies to one of your reports (or changes its status), you get a notification, even with the app in the background; tap it to open My reports.

• BetterTTV: personal emotes of BTTV Pro users show up once BTTV announces them, and emotes added to the channel during the stream appear right away.
• Pin your favourite streamers: long-press a followed channel (live or offline) and pick "Pin to the top of Following". Pinned channels show first, with a small pin next to their name.

• Live notifications through ntfy: fixed on the server side (ntfy.sh was turning the server away), and the Test button now tells you when ntfy.sh is refusing messages for now instead of saying the server can't be reached.
• Other improvements and fixes.

apps.name: Penumbra
apps.subtitle: Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows (2010), enhanced for modern systems on the Supersonic Engine: widescreen, gamepads, touch, eleven languages; Windows, Linux, Android, macOS, iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows — Enhanced:

The 2010 action platformer by André Santee, enhanced for modern systems.

versions.localizedDescription:
Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows - Enhanced 1.0.10:

The 2010 action platformer by André Santee, enhanced for today's computers and phones. Be the wizard: grab your sword, throw fireballs, light up the dark and defeat the king who rules the castle. Play alone, with a friend, or against each other in Versus.

New in 1.0.10:

This update is about a picture that stays blurry on weak phones. Everything else plays as in 1.0.9, which stays available.

• The picture can become sharp again. To keep the game smooth, the game draws a smaller picture when a phone cannot keep up, and enlarges it again when the phone has room. A tester's Galaxy A05 showed that this could get stuck at the smallest size (both of the tester's screenshots were drawn at 480x216), so text, damage and enemies were hard to see. Now the game tries a larger picture whenever the phone has a little room, instead of waiting until it runs far above what it needs, and it keeps the picture at least 360 lines high unless the phone would run slower than 30 frames a second there.
• A "Picture sharpness" row on a phone's Settings screen, under the refresh rate: Automatic (the game decides, as before, now with the quicker return), Sharp (the full size), Balanced (70%) and Fast (half the size). Your choice is kept. Sharp can make a weak phone slow; that is what the row lets you decide. It exists in all eleven languages.
• What we do not know. We have two screenshots from one phone and no measurement from it, so we do not know what pushed that picture down first, or whether this update is enough for that phone. Weak phones can still end up with a soft picture; the new row is the way out when they do.

How far each download has been checked:

• Android: the game has been played through on a real phone by the person who made it, the screen that adjusts the buttons included (an earlier build). What is new in 1.0.10 was only tried on an Android emulator: it installs over 1.0.9 as an update (same package name and signing key), the language and the difficulty stay, the new row shows in the Settings screen, a chosen size is kept after the game is closed and opened again, and level 1 plays. It has not been tried on a real weak phone. The quicker return to a larger picture never ran on any phone, and did not even trigger on the emulator, whose software graphics are too slow; it was tested only by the game's automated tests and by simulations of weak phones. The part of the game that real phones run (the arm64 program) is in the file but was never started. We still do not know whether this fixes the blurry picture the Galaxy A05 tester described.

• Mac: it was tested automatically on GitHub's Macs and its Intel half under Rosetta. Nobody has played it on a real Mac, and it is not notarised by Apple.
• iPhone and iPad: experimental. It has never run on any iPhone or iPad, so it may not start.
• Languages: eleven, switchable in the game. The translations were made with AI help and have not been checked by native speakers.
• Free. No ads, no in-app purchases, no accounts. The game never connects to the internet.

Checksums (SHA256SUMS.txt):

Every file is built from commit cda253feaa0febb24eacdc0fa5e9fe551cfae79f.

Credits:

Original game (2010): André Santee (programming, game design, Ethanon Engine), Arthur Santee (3D modelling, game design), Gabriel Duarte (soundtrack), Approaching Thunderstorm (music). Enhanced edition: Ivan Cvetanović, developed with Claude Code, on the Supersonic Engine. Touch buttons, the options screen's frames, buttons and icons, and the touch-controls editor's buttons: from Magic Rampage, by Asantee Games.

Free; the source code is on GitHub. Provided as is, without any warranty; see LICENSE.md.

Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows - Enhanced 1.0.10 (Português):

O jogo de plataforma e ação de 2010 de André Santee, aprimorado para os computadores e celulares de hoje. Seja o mago: pegue a espada, lance bolas de fogo, ilumine a escuridão e derrote o rei que domina o castelo. Jogue sozinho, com um amigo, ou um contra o outro no modo Versus.

Novidades da 1.0.10:

Esta atualização trata de uma imagem que fica borrada em celulares fracos. O resto joga como na 1.0.9, que continua disponível.

• A imagem pode voltar a ficar nítida. Para manter o jogo fluido, o jogo desenha uma imagem menor quando o celular não dá conta e a aumenta de novo quando o celular tem folga. O Galaxy A05 de um testador mostrou que isso podia ficar preso no menor tamanho (as duas capturas de tela do testador foram desenhadas em 480x216), e por isso texto, dano e inimigos ficavam difíceis de ver. Agora o jogo tenta uma imagem maior sempre que o celular tem um pouco de folga, em vez de esperar até ele rodar muito acima do que precisa, e mantém a imagem com pelo menos 360 linhas de altura, a não ser que o celular rodasse a menos de 30 quadros por segundo nesse tamanho.
• Uma linha "Nitidez da imagem" na tela de configurações do celular, abaixo da taxa de atualização: Automática (o jogo decide, como antes, agora com o retorno mais rápido), Nítida (o tamanho total), Equilibrada (70%) e Rápida (metade do tamanho). Sua escolha fica guardada. Nítida pode deixar um celular fraco lento; é isso que a linha deixa você decidir. Ela existe nos onze idiomas.
• O que não sabemos. Temos duas capturas de tela de um celular e nenhuma medição dele, então não sabemos o que fez aquela imagem diminuir primeiro, nem se esta atualização basta para aquele celular. Celulares fracos ainda podem ficar com a imagem suave; a nova linha é a saída quando isso acontecer.

Até onde cada download foi verificado:

• Android: o jogo foi jogado do começo ao fim num celular de verdade por quem o criou, inclusive a tela que ajusta os botões (uma versão anterior). O que é novo na 1.0.10 foi testado apenas num emulador de Android: ela se instala sobre a 1.0.9 como uma atualização (mesmo nome de pacote e mesma chave de assinatura), o idioma e a dificuldade ficam, a nova linha aparece na tela de configurações, um tamanho escolhido continua depois de fechar e abrir o jogo de novo, e a fase 1 roda. Ainda não foi testada num celular fraco de verdade. O retorno mais rápido a uma imagem maior nunca rodou em nenhum celular, e nem chegou a acontecer no emulador, cujos gráficos por software são lentos demais; ele foi testado apenas pelos testes automáticos do jogo e por simulações de celulares fracos. A parte do jogo que os celulares de verdade executam (o programa arm64) está no arquivo, mas nunca foi iniciada. Continuamos sem saber se isto corrige a imagem borrada que o testador do Galaxy A05 descreveu.

• Mac: foi testado automaticamente nos Macs do GitHub, e a metade para Intel no Rosetta. Ninguém jogou ainda num Mac de verdade, e ele não é autenticado (notarised) pela Apple.
• iPhone e iPad: experimental. Nunca rodou em nenhum iPhone ou iPad, então pode não abrir.
• Idiomas: onze, à escolha no jogo. As traduções foram feitas com ajuda de IA e não foram revisadas por falantes nativos.
• Grátis. Sem anúncios, sem compras no app, sem contas. O jogo nunca se conecta à internet.

Somas de verificação (SHA256SUMS.txt):

Todos os arquivos são feitos a partir do commit cda253feaa0febb24eacdc0fa5e9fe551cfae79f.

Créditos:

Jogo original (2010): André Santee (programação, game design, Ethanon Engine), Arthur Santee (modelagem 3D, game design), Gabriel Duarte (trilha sonora), Approaching Thunderstorm (música). Edição aprimorada: Ivan Cvetanović, desenvolvida com o Claude Code, na Supersonic Engine. Botões de toque, as molduras, botões e ícones da tela de configurações e os botões da tela de ajuste dos controles de toque: do Magic Rampage, da Asantee Games.

Grátis; o código-fonte está no GitHub. Fornecido como está, sem nenhuma garantia; veja o LICENSE.md.

apps.subtitle: The first iOS browser to bring ScriptCat-class power to userscripts — background execution, @crontab scheduling, and a sandboxed GM API — and run real Chrome Web Store extensions, all wrapped in a Chromium-inspired interface
apps.localizedDescription:
The first iOS browser to bring ScriptCat-class power to userscripts — background execution, @crontab scheduling, and a sandboxed GM API — and run real Chrome Web Store extensions, all wrapped in a Chromium-inspired interface.

iOS has never had a true power userscript runtime. Safari extensions like Userscripts and Stay brought Greasemonkey-style injection to mobile, and Gear Browser proved a dedicated userscript browser can ship on the App Store. But none of them deliver the one thing ScriptCat gives desktop users:

Scripts that keep working in the background — on a schedule — without a tab open.

Gevun:

A music player for your Navidrome library on iPhone and iPad.

Features:

• Browse albums, artists, and songs, or search your library.

ReFlo+ 1.0.6:

A free, touch-first controller for the Behringer Flow 8, built for working live techs. Fader strips for every mix, a drag-to-edit parametric EQ, graphic EQ, FX control, output limiter and delay, sends matrix, scenes, and mute groups.

Free to download and use. No account, no ads, no tracking. It works fully offline: the only network request is an optional check on the first screen for a newer version.

What's new in 1.0.6.

• Mac app: a double-click ReFlo+ for macOS 12 or newer (Apple Silicon and Intel). It opens the full app in your web browser. See Install below for the one-time "Open Anyway" step.
• Update notice: the first screen now checks this page for a newer version and shows a note with a link if there is one. It does nothing when you're offline. On Android this adds an Internet permission, used only for that check.
• No Windows version: I tried. A Windows PC connects and sends commands fine, but Windows never delivers the mixer's replies, so the app can't load the mixer. It works on Mac, Android and iPhone/iPad.
• Nothing else changed from 1.0.5.

Still to confirm from 1.0.5 (please tell me if you see problems): the black screen after connecting should be fixed, but I can't test every device, and the Troubleshooting notes on the first screen help me find out why if it returns. The output EQ frequency and Q writes and the Main balance write aren't yet confirmed on a real mixer, so check them against the mixer's display.

What's new in 1.0.5.

• Output EQ, two modes: every output (Main, Mon 1, Mon 2) has a GEQ mode (nine fixed octave bands: drag up and down, paint across bands) and a Parametric mode (each of the nine nodes has its own frequency, gain and Q). Lock frequencies, Reset and Flat are there too.
• Channel EQ: the lowest band is a bell with a Q control, like the others.
• Main output Balance slider.
• Full-screen EQ: an amber Expand button opens any channel or output EQ full screen. Close returns you; on Android the Back button closes it first.
• FX tap tempo: the TAP button flashes on every beat.
• Gain reduction: a light overlay on the level meter with a solid edge.
• Disconnect from mixer and Leave demo return to the start screen.

Earlier: 1.0.4 added the Troubleshooting notes. 1.0.3 added phone layouts, a Display size slider, full-height faders and a loading message. 1.0.2 added demo mode, optional tap animation and button haptics (off by default).

Downloads:

Android.

• Open it. Allow "install unknown apps" for your browser or file app when asked.
• If Play Protect warns about an unknown developer, choose Install anyway.
• Open ReFlo+, press Pairing on the Flow 8, then tap Connect to Mixer. Allow the Bluetooth / Nearby devices permission.

iPhone / iPad The IPA is unsigned. Install it with your usual sideloading tool (for example AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly or TrollStore), which signs it for your device. Then pair as above and allow Bluetooth access.

Mac.

• Unzip reflo-plus-mac.zip and open ReFlo+ (move it to Applications if you like).
• macOS will say it can't verify the app, because it isn't notarized by Apple. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway (on older macOS, right-click the app and choose Open).
• Allow Bluetooth when asked. ReFlo+ opens in your web browser; keep its small window open while you work and click Quit when finished.
• Press Pairing on the Flow 8, then click Connect to Mixer.

Good to know:

• The Flow 8 accepts one control connection at a time. Close the official FLOW Mix app before connecting ReFlo+.
• It sends live commands to the mixer (levels, phantom power, routing). Check settings before a show.
• The mixer controls (faders, sends, mutes, solos, gain, comp, EQ, 48V, graphic EQ, output delay, scenes, mute groups) were tested on a real Flow 8. Still being confirmed on hardware: the FX presets and tempo, the Setup toggles, channel renaming by press-and-hold, and the iPhone/iPad app itself. Please report anything odd.
• FX preset names are ReFlo+'s own and may not match the official app. The effects themselves are the mixer's.
• Gain-reduction display is a rough guide (four steps), not a dB reading.

versions.localizedDescription:
iGhostVT 1.6.15 adds a drop zone to the relay, so a file moves between two devices with ighostvt-cli drop instead of being pasted through a terminal.

• The relay keeps a file for 30 minutes after the last device that put or got it disconnected, ighostvt-cli drop rm removes one sooner, and the relay forgets every file when it restarts. Drop zone files are not encrypted, unlike terminal sessions through the relay: keep secrets out of it. Update the relay's image to use it; RELAY_DROP_BYTES sets the space it may take (4 GiB by default) and 0 turns it off. The app itself has no drop zone controls, and devices on 1.6.14 keep working with this relay and with 1.6.15.

To run the relay, use the attached compose.yml; the image is ghcr.io/owngoal-dev/ighostvt-relay, and the digest is in relay-image.txt. SHA-256 sums are in SHA256SUMS, and the Mac app's in SHA256SUMS.macos.

About:

Blinker Fluid is an experimental privacy-focused browser that ports Chromium's Blink rendering engine and V8 JavaScript engine to iOS, allowing websites to run without relying on Apple's built-in WebKit engine.

The project primarily targets jailbroken and TrollStore-capable devices, bringing a Chromium-based browser to older iOS versions where the bundled version of WebKit may struggle with some modern websites.

Why?:

I started Blinker Fluid because Ungoogled Chromium is my primary desktop browser (not counting Tor), and I wanted to see if Chromium's Blink engine could run on jailbroken iOS.

Another reason was that many modern websites no longer work correctly with older versions of WebKit bundled with older iOS releases, which many jailbroken users are unable or unwilling to update from.

BlueWake 0.8.0 brings the Wind Waker HD look, HD textures you make from your own Wind Waker HD game inside the app, more speed by default on Windows and Linux, the same menus on every computer, and an experimental Android build. The Wind Waker HD look, off by default.

HD textures from your own Wind Waker HD game.
