apps.localizedDescription:
← Back to main Moonfin project.

Moonfin is a media client for Jellyfin and Emby servers, built with Flutter. One shared codebase powers phones and tablets, Windows, macOS, and Linux, Android TV, Fire TV, and Apple TV, and the browser. It's made for people who want a modern, customizable experience on every screen they own.

Platform Support:

Android TV, Fire TV, and Apple TV ship from this same codebase with a TV-tuned interface and D-pad navigation. Fire TV runs the same native backend as Android TV. Web runs as an installable PWA through the Moonbase server plugin.

Features:

• One codebase, every screen. Phones, tablets, desktop, Android TV, Apple TV, and web, with navigation tuned for touch, pointer, and remote.

versions.localizedDescription:
Moonfin 2.7.0 Release Notes:

Moonfin 2.7.0 lands less than two weeks after 2.6.0 with around two hundred and forty commits. If your server runs the Achievement Badges plugin you can now add friends and chat with them, phones get a redesigned bottom bar in three styles, and a seasonal Home row brings out the holiday movies at the right time of year next to a rebuilt set of seasonal effects. The in-app remote gained a D-pad and can type a search onto your TV from your phone, Live TV recovers from a stalled channel on its own, and you can now set your library order and hide detail screen sections. On the fix side, Moonfin finally honors the self-signed certificate setting on every server connection, DTS and TrueHD passthrough got another round of work, Android Auto actually plays on Media3, and Windows and Linux go back to the Skia renderer to end the laggy scrolling some of you saw in 2.6.0.

Moonfin now checks your server's certificate on every connection. If your server uses a self-signed or private CA certificate, sign-in will say it isn't trusted and offer to allow it, or you can turn on Settings > Account & Security > Allow self-signed certificates before you update.

Friends and Chat:

• Friend requests, incoming and sent, with an Add friends search across the people on your server. Each friend gets a card with their stats and badges plus Send message, Remove and Block, and blocking stops direct messages without pulling you out of groups you share.

• Privacy holds the plugin's own settings for appearing offline, hiding what you're watching or last watched, and message notifications. They're stored on the server, so they apply on every client.
• New message banners, held back while a video or game is playing unless you turn Mute during playback off.
• A Friends button for the top bar, the sidebar and the phone's You sheet, with a count of friend requests and unread messages. It's off by default under navigation settings, and only shows up where the plugin has friends turned on.
• Unlock notifications. A switch above Badges on the Achievements screen shows a banner when you earn a badge. It writes the plugin's own setting, so jellyfin-web follows it too, and the plugin decides the minimum rarity and whether several unlocks share one banner. Tapping it opens Achievements.

A New Bottom Bar on Phones:

• Pin up to three tabs between Home and You, or leave it on Automatic to follow your navigation button switches.
• The You tab shows your avatar and opens a hub with your account, tiles for everything you haven't pinned, from Libraries, Favorites, Genres, Live TV and Seerr Discover to Shuffle, SyncPlay, Quick Connect and Remote Control, and rows for Friends, Server Messages and Settings.

Seasonal Row and Effects:

• A seasonal Home row. Holiday movies from your library, plus Seerr suggestions if Seerr is set up, in a row right after Continue Watching and Next Up. It covers New Year's, Valentine's Day, Easter, Pride, Halloween, Thanksgiving in the US and Canada, Christmas from the day after US Thanksgiving, Lunar New Year and Diwali. Turn it on under Settings > Integrations > External Lists > Seasonal Row.
• Each holiday can be unticked on its own, and the country follows your device region unless you pick one, which is how Lunar New Year and Diwali show up where they're celebrated. It's off by default and syncs through Moonbase.
• The seasonal effects were redone. Snow, Fireworks, Confetti and Falling Leaves used to be text symbols redrawn every frame that started from an empty screen. They're drawn as real sprites now, start full and fade in, move at the same speed whatever the frame rate, and fireworks are actual rockets that burst into sparks.
• Four new effects. Christmas is snow with baubles and stars, Spring Petals has cherry blossoms and bees, Fireflies, and Halloween brings bats, ghosts, candy and orange and purple leaves.
• A Density setting of Light, Normal or Heavy. Effects also pause behind the screensaver, respect the system's reduce motion setting, and run at a lower frame rate on low performance devices.
• Seasons picked in the original Android TV app and older Moonfin for webOS and Tizen builds carry over onto the new effects instead of drawing nothing.

Remote Control:

• The in-app remote has a D-pad. A round pad with OK, plus Back and Home, sits alongside the playback and volume controls and works whether or not anything is playing. Each button only shows if the device you're controlling supports it.
• Every Moonfin client can be driven from a remote now, not just TV. Phones, tablets, desktop and web take navigation as real key presses, so menus, overlays, Next Up and the screensaver react the same way they do to a physical remote.
• Search from your phone. A Search button opens Search on the device you're controlling and brings up your phone's own keyboard. On a Moonfin receiver the query updates live as you type, predictive text and paste included, and Back takes the viewer back to where they were. Text sent from the Jellyfin dashboard or another controller opens Search with it too.
• The Apple TV player answers the remote, including its menus, the channel carousel, SyncPlay and the info panel, and Home closes dialogs, the TV keyboard and the player.
• Remote volume reaches more devices. Apple TV applies it as playback volume, phones and tablets set the system volume, unmute goes back to the level you had, and Moonfin for webOS and Tizen get TV volume and mute buttons when nothing is playing.

Live TV Recovery:

• A stalled channel recovers on its own. A picture frozen for eight seconds, or a fresh tune with no picture after thirty, starts up to three paced attempts: reopen the stream, get a fresh session from the server, then have the server remux or transcode that channel. You see Reconnecting (1 of 3) while it works, and your own pause or a phone call taking the audio is never mistaken for a stall.
• A Retry card when it can't. If all three attempts fail, the tuner is freed and a Failed to play card with Retry stays up until you act, with the guide and channel list still usable. The attempts come back after a clean minute, so the next hiccup isn't an instant give up. Apple TV reconnects quietly without the overlay.
• Live channels can remux when Live TV Direct is off, keeping the original codecs instead of forcing a full transcode, and a recovery no longer turns direct play back on by itself.
• On demand transcodes recover too. One that runs dry well before the end gets the same limited retries, and tells you it couldn't recover instead of sitting on its last frame.

Libraries and Details:

• Library Order. Settings > Personalization > Libraries > Library Order sets the order of your libraries for My Media, the recently added rows and the navigation bars. It's saved to your server account, so other apps you sign in to follow it too, and libraries hidden from My Media are still listed with a Hidden tag.
• Hide detail screen sections. Settings > Personalization > Details Screen > Sections lists the parts your current style draws, from the logo, tagline and version badge to cast, crew, chapters, extras, More Like This, the Seerr sections and person biographies. One switch hides a section in every style, kept per kind of device and synced through Moonbase.
• Sort & Filter got a Clear for each category and a search box on any list of ten or more values, so a TV remote can find and undo one filter without scrolling the whole panel. The search ignores accents.
• View Details on playlist items, right after Play and Play Next, with Back returning you to the playlist. On the Classic layout, selecting a video in a playlist now plays it like the other layouts do.

Playback:

• External PGS subtitles without a transcode on Android. Media3 reads .sup files itself now, where any external PGS file used to have the server burn it into the video. Embedded PGS tracks are still burned in when a transcode is needed.
• YouTube trailers in up to 1080p, through YouTube's Vision Pro client, with the 360p file as a fallback.

Interface:

• The TV interface is bigger. 2.6.0 put every TV on one 1324 point canvas, which made Android TV noticeably smaller than it had been. Every TV now lays out on 1150 points, so everything is about fifteen percent larger than 2.6.0 on Android TV, Fire TV and Apple TV.
• A Great-Grandparents UI scale, a step above Grandparents at 1.6x.
• Playback languages in the setup wizard. The last step has an optional section under the themes for your default audio language, preferring the default audio track, subtitle language and subtitle mode. Only what you change is saved.
• A Top Shelf setting on Apple TV. Home Screen settings have an Apple TV home screen section where Top Shelf shows either your latest media or a Moonfin banner. It's kept per device.

Windows:

• A Microsoft Store build for x64 and ARM64, which updates through the Store rather than the in-app updater.

Diagnostics:

• Android reports how the last run ended. On Android 11 and later, a crash, ANR, failed start or memory kill shows up in the diagnostic log on the next launch, and Android 12 and later add the crashing thread and its last error logs. Like other crash reports these only go to your own server, and only while Send crash reports to server is on.
• The diagnostic report also carries the system uptime, since some Amlogic and MediaTek audio drivers misbehave after long uptimes, plus why image fetches failed and how long they took.

Passthrough and Audio on Android:

• TrueHD Atmos stays TrueHD after a seek with App (IEC) passthrough. The first buffer after a seek can start between TrueHD sync points, the packer failed on it, and the session gave up on IEC and came out as Dolby Digital Plus for the rest of the film. Those units are skipped until the next sync point now.
• DTS-HD MA titles start again. Some receivers take longer than 700ms to start a bitstream, and 2.6.0's silence detector tore the track down during that wait and left nothing playing, which showed up as an unexpected playback error or a black screen. A stream that hasn't played yet now gets three seconds of grace.
• Blu-ray DTS in .ts and .m2ts files has sound. Media3 skips Blu-ray's DTS stream types, so DTS, DTS-HD MA and DTS:X in transport streams played silent. Moonfin reads them itself now, only when the stream is marked as Blu-ray so broadcast TV keeps working.
• DTS Core passthrough sends a DTS-HD track as its core when DTS-HD MA passthrough is off, instead of decoding it in the app.

Playback on Android:

• Resuming after a pause no longer buffers forever. Some devices come back from a pause of half a minute or so with a decoder that never restarts. If a resume is still buffering after three seconds with plenty already loaded, the player reloads at the same spot.
• No more strips of artifacts along the edge of 4K video on Shield and Fire TV. Flutter's last UI frame was left under the video and showed through the softened edge when the UI plane is upscaled, and video whose height isn't a multiple of eight let its padded rows through as a line.
• Transcodes with external subtitles stop stalling. Media3 only loads whichever source is furthest behind, so a subtitle the server was still extracting from a large file held the video at one segment, sometimes for minutes. Subtitles are only fetched once you pick one now and never hold the video back, and adding external subtitles no longer restarts playback once per subtitle.
• Transcoded subtitles stay in sync after a seek. 2.6.0 shifted sideloaded subtitles by the same offset Media3 uses to correct the video, but Media3 already corrects the video, so subtitles ran about ten seconds early, mostly after seeking. The shift and its Auto label are gone, a manual delay takes effect straight away, and the delay resets for each new viewing.
• Bunched frames no longer get dropped. Some files deliver frames in pairs a few milliseconds apart, so on a display already at the content's rate two frames landed on one refresh and about a quarter never showed, which Media3 never counted as dropped. Each frame is held to its own refresh now, which clears the judder on pans in 50fps video on a 50Hz display.
• Android Auto actually plays on Media3. Every Media3 player lived inside a video view, so with no view on screen, as when a car cold starts the app, playback reported success and made no sound. Audio plays without a view now. Signing in from the car no longer loops, car browsing survives the phone app opening, CarPlay's shuffle and repeat buttons work, and failures show as offline or unavailable instead of a silent playing.
• Two ANRs are gone, one when adding a long WebVTT subtitle and one when leaving playback while a passthrough track was being set up.
• The DLNA cast picker stops crashing when two scans overlap.
• 4K TV boxes stop piling up GPU memory behind the screensaver. Skia sized its cache to the screen, around 400MB at 4K, and it's capped at the 1080p budget now.

Playback Everywhere:

• Max Resolution applies to VP9, VP8, MPEG-4 and MPEG-2, so a 4K VP9 file is transcoded down on a device that can't handle it instead of direct playing.
• Hi-res TrueHD direct plays on Android, Windows and Linux. 2.6.0 capped bridged audio at 48 kHz on every player when only the Apple engine needed it, so 96 kHz TrueHD and similar tracks were transcoded on Media3 and mpv.
• An external audio file no longer shifts the embedded tracks. Tracks were numbered with the external file counted, so picking the main track could play the commentary. Choosing the external file asks the server to mux it in.
• mpv picks the right subtitle. If an external subtitle failed to load because the server was still extracting it, mpv fell back to a position in its track list and could select another language. That track stays off now and is retried every ten seconds, up to five times, and a failed subtitle no longer raises a playback error.
• Subtitles set to Off stay off on web. Every external track was made visible as it loaded.
• Trailers keep their original soundtrack. YouTube lists its auto-dubbed tracks first without marking a default, so players picked a dub.
• The player controls hide on their own after Resume. The hide timer ran out during the slow open and seek, and nothing set it again.
• Wide logos in the player stay a sensible size, at most about a third of the screen width.
• Offline progress syncs when you reopen the app online. The sync only ran when the server went from unreachable to reachable, so a cold start with the network already up never sent it, and pressing Resume saved the server's older position over yours. It runs after each sign-in now, and only to the server it belongs to, where it had been pushing one server's progress to another.

• Cast, DLNA and AirPlay status survive a cold start from a car or a media button on Android and iOS. The event streams connected before the app had a native handler, died for the session, and filed a crash report on your server.

Live TV:

• Recording tiles open with Select or Enter on the Recordings, Schedule and Series Recordings screens, where they took focus but only answered taps. The Recordings header also wraps on phones instead of overflowing.

Android TV:

• Back from a movie lands on its details page. The player closed on key down, and the system back Android sends once the key comes up popped the details page too.
• Back works right after closing a player menu, and Android 12 and older no longer swallow the first Back on a details page.
• Back leaves the details page once focus is back on Play instead of getting stuck after you've been down in the tabs.

Apple:

• Music remote controls work on Apple TV and iPhone. 2.6.0's engine update opened its own Now Playing session for music, which the system showed instead of Moonfin's, so the Siri Remote, the iPhone remote, the Watch and earbuds did nothing and the Now Playing card was blank. Moonfin fills that session with the title, artist and artwork and takes its presses now, and next and previous track show instead of ten second skips.
• AirPods play and pause keep working after Picture in Picture closes on iPad.
• Downmix to Stereo works on macOS, iOS and tvOS. The engine can't downmix on its own, so the setting did nothing while the device kept advertising surround. It asks the server for stereo now.
• Intel Macs are back on the Skia renderer. Flutter 3.47's Impeller default garbled text and lagged on Intel graphics.
• Top Shelf only shows your Latest rows and clears on sign out. Favorites, Last Played, Since You Watched and Rewatch rows could fill it, and the last account's artwork stayed on the Apple TV home screen after signing out.

Windows and Linux:

• Library scrolling is smooth again. Flutter 3.47 made Impeller the desktop default, which made scrolling laggy on Windows and held the GPU near full while idle on Linux. Both are back on Skia.
• Moonfin launches on machines with a missing or outdated Visual C++ runtime, which now ships next to moonfin.exe.
• Launching in fullscreen no longer leaves a gray window. Restoring fullscreen before the window was shown saved a hidden window style that got written back later.

• Uninstalling removes the moonfin:// link handler from the registry.
• The AppImage stops adding a second menu entry under Gear Lever, AppImageLauncher and AppManager. 2.6.0's fix missed that Gear Lever's copy of the desktop entry starts the same as Moonfin's own, so Moonfin took it for its own and wrote another. moonfin:// links pass through a manager's copy now too.

Home, Search and Libraries:

• Search shows results without waiting on People. A slow People lookup held the whole search, for thirty seconds on some servers. Results show within about a second and people fill in when they arrive.
• Multi-server search covers every signed-in server, with each result labeled by its server. It only ever searched the active one.
• Continue Watching is current on launch when it's merged with Next Up. That row never saved to the home cache and loaded after everything else, so a cold start showed episodes you'd already finished for half a minute. Next Up also sorts a round trip sooner on Jellyfin and Emby.
• An empty Home stays empty. When every library was gone, the old cached rows came back on every cold start, and the last backdrop and theme music stayed behind the empty message.
• The first Home card you reach from the media bar or toolbar plays its preview.
• Home rows and the media bar stop going blank on Firefox after scrolling away and back. A shown image was decoded a second time, which paints blank on Firefox.
• Blocked ratings apply to IMDb, TMDB and MDBList rows, and once you block any rating they hide unrated titles too.
• Custom rows load large lists. They wait forty five seconds for a response instead of fifteen, and the check when you add or edit one shows the real failure instead of No results returned.
• Mixed and home video libraries sort properly. Every sort put folders first, so shows came before movies, Premiere Date and the rating sorts were missing, and a saved sort reset to Name. They open on Folders First now and sort by exactly what you pick.
• Collections of Live TV channels show their channels. Modern collections get an Other tab for anything that isn't a movie or series, and channel cards in a collection tune the channel in every layout.
• Collections open on Movies with Expanded Tabs, where a Studios tab that loaded late took the selection.
• Classic details show a row for every collection a movie belongs to, not only the first.

Details and Interface:

• Detail and player buttons follow UI Scaling on desktop and TV. Text grew with the scale while the Modern, Spotlight, Minimalist and Nouveau buttons and the player controls stayed the same size.
• Play only highlights when focused on desktop and TV, like the buttons beside it, and focus only shows while you're using keys or a remote, so Play no longer stays expanded next to the button under your mouse.
• Detail rows line up. Every row starts its cards the same distance under its title, Classic's Next Up keeps the same header height as the rest, and extras rows lose the big empty gap under featurettes.
• The last content on detail and settings pages clears the bottom bar and the system navigation buttons on phones.
• A long artist list no longer stretches the top bar music player across the screen. The title is capped and scrolls.
• Classic home row titles stop drawing over the info overlay while you scroll with a mouse.
• Animated avatars redraw half as often. Every GIF frame redrew the whole window twice, which kept the GPU busy on an idle desktop.
• The server messages button fills the top bar on hover.

Emby:

• Next Up matches Emby's own. 2.6.0's workaround only looked at your last hundred played episodes, so a binged show could crowd out everything else, leaving one user with a single item where Emby showed sixty one. Moonfin asks Emby 4.10 for the same Next Up list Emby's home screen uses.

• All Genres and the home Genres row fill again. Emby's genre list has no item counts, so every genre looked empty.
• Unable to connect after a restart is gone off LAN. Emby answers its ping with a 401 from outside its network, which read as the server being down.

Seerr:

• Seerr notifications show up in the app. The plugin's settings stream timed out before the server's heartbeat and kept dropping, web never received it at all, notifications without a page to open were thrown away, and one screen closing could unhook the rest.
• Seerr rows load quickly after sign-in. Sign-in waited on that same stream, which the server can hold until its heartbeat and which never finished on web, and a late home reload stole focus. Moonfin also skips signing in to Seerr again when the plugin already holds the session.
• Seerr banners on TV use the theme's text style instead of Flutter's debug style with a yellow underline.

Connections and Admin:

• Deep links open as the user they name on a warm app, and on a cold start that restores the last user. Both opened under whoever was signed in, so the item came up as not found. Kids Mode, a PIN or always authenticate still block the switch.
• New Jellyfin libraries keep their folders. Moonfin sent them in a field the server doesn't read.
• The add library buttons are button sized again, admin card highlights are rounded, the plugin page loses its second back button, and the previous admin page no longer shows through during a page change.

Huge thanks to everyone who contributed this release:

Translations were updated through Weblate by mikey (Finnish), Kisnov (Catalan), SCHIZOPHRENE (French), Adrian Szyłak and oskarkasprzyk (Polish), eliastitecnologia (Brazilian Portuguese), therealresonix and rekiznuh1 (German), idezentas (Turkish), managemygroup (British English), Benedek Dunavölgyi (Hungarian), Licaa21 (Romanian), Sergio Suarez (Mexican Spanish), and everyone who translated anonymously. If you want to help translate Moonfin into your language, check out our Weblate project.

Ito is a free, open-source client for iPhone and iPad. It combines dedicated readers, native video playback, AniList integration, and an extensible WebAssembly plugin system in a single app.

Features:

• Anime, manga, and novels — Keep different media types together in one library.
• Native reading — Dedicated manga and novel readers designed for iOS.

• AniList discovery — Browse, search, and filter titles using AniList.

• On-device storage — Library data and history are stored locally, with tracker credentials protected by Keychain.
• No advertisements — Ito is free and ad-free.

apps.name: NuggetVPN
apps.subtitle: NuggetVPN is a A fast, good-looking VPN client for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, built with Wails v3 and React 19
apps.localizedDescription:
NuggetVPN:

A fast, good-looking VPN client for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, built with Wails v3 and React 19.

Every proxy core it can run is compiled into the app as a Go library. There is no bundled executable, nothing is downloaded at runtime, and nothing is shelled out to.

Connecting:

• Four cores to choose from (see Cores).
• Subscriptions, with data usage and expiry shown when the provider reports them. Share links (vless://, vmess://, ss:// and others), full sing-box configs, and Clash configs are all accepted.
• Proxy chains, where each hop dials through the one before it.
• Fastest server: the tunnel keeps measuring the best few servers and moves to whichever is fastest.
• Kill switch and automatic reconnect.

versions.localizedDescription:
NuggetVPN 2.3.0:

A big one: a guided first start, a new home screen, iOS, updates that install themselves, a rebuilt Activity tab, and a lot of speed where it counts — connecting, the first seconds after it, and how much the app costs while it sits there.

Windows (PowerShell).

macOS / Linux.

Both check the download against GitHub's SHA-256 before installing, and running them again updates. Or pick a file from the assets below.

New:

• First start is a setup, not a sync-server form: language, a look (theme and where the navigation sits), your subscription, and the few settings worth deciding up front — launch at login, auto-connect, the kill switch. Every step but the first can be skipped, and Settings can run it again.
• New home screen built around the connect button: what it will do, in words; the configuration and the server as one strip; live speed, latency and your public IP only while connected.
• Updates install themselves. Windows runs the installer silently (one UAC prompt) and reopens the app; macOS swaps the app in place, safely, and relaunches.
• Silent installer for Windows (…-silent-installer.exe): no pages, no questions.
• Server flags, read from server names however providers write them (flag emoji, country or city in English, Russian or Ukrainian, ISO code). Bundled with the app — nothing fetched from the internet.
• Servers a core can't run are marked ("needs another core") and can't be picked by mistake; settings a core ignores are locked with a note saying so.
• Subscription announcements: a message from your provider shows on the home screen, with their link, and can be folded or dismissed until they say something new.
• Activity tab: Statistics, Connections and Logs in one place.

• Connections grouped by app: how many each has open, through which server, by which rule, received and sent with the speed right now. An app opens on its sites. System programs fold into one "System" group, which opens on its programs.
• Statistics by app, with a day chart named by weekday or date, a legend, and a choice of charts in Appearance.
• Program icons on macOS and Windows.

• Routing: pick apps from a list on macOS, Windows and Linux (it was Android only), including programs running right now, so portable apps are there too. Typing a process name still works.
• Routing: undo/redo on any keyboard layout (Ctrl+Z on a Russian layout works now), and Delete removes the selection.

• Accent colour of your own over any theme, with a colour picker.
• Exact corner radius, animation speed (0.25×–3×) and the delay between parts of a page.
• An inset sidebar style.
• Custom themes can start from any built-in theme.
• Units: speed in bytes or bits per second, data in auto or fixed KB / MB / GB.

• New setting, Connection → "Try other servers if one fails" (on by default).
• Double-click a header to maximise or restore the window, like a native title bar.

• Every notification can be closed.

Faster and lighter:

• Connecting with Automatic is much quicker: servers are ranked within 1.5 s instead of waiting out every unreachable one (50 dead servers took 16 s; now 1.5 s).

• Idle while connected: 2–3 % CPU instead of 20–29 %. Animations play when something happens and then rest.
• Nothing polls while the window is hidden in the tray.
• Memory is handed back after connecting and refreshing subscriptions instead of staying in the app's footprint for minutes.

Fixed:

• A failure that is your computer's, not the server's — the TUN adapter on Windows ("The system cannot find the file specified"), a port in use, permissions — stops at once with an explanation, instead of being tried on every server and blamed on them.
• iOS reports the tunnel's real state, and a tunnel that drops is noticed; the tunnel's MTU and addresses match the config, so large packets aren't lost.
• "Update" and other links open in your browser on Android and iOS, instead of replacing the app's own screen.
• Windows: local socket paths with a drive letter are no longer mistaken for network addresses.

• Statistics: switching period no longer blinks or shows the previous period's numbers; the page uses the window's full width.
• Connections: rows no longer jump or re-animate every second; received and sent line up.
• Routing: a block fills its frame while it's being resized.
• Settings rows no longer run off the edge in a narrow window; the top bar's tabs no longer shift.

Removed:

• Importing from Beam.

Under the hood:

• Wails v3.0.0-beta.28.

apps.subtitle: Your anime, movies, and shows: discover, track, and watch in one beautiful app
apps.localizedDescription: Your anime, movies, and shows: discover, track, and watch in one beautiful app

versions.localizedDescription:
MiruShin continues to evolve as a modern and comfortable way to watch and discover media, with each update focused on making the experience smoother, cleaner, and more enjoyable across the app.

What's New:

• Fixed incorrect episode-behind badges on finished anime.

• Handled broadcast statuses consistently across AniList, MyAnimeList and Shikimori without changing watch progress or library data.

v2.9.20:

• Airing metadata refreshes independently of watch progress and syncs between devices through Google Drive without generating upload echoes.
• Added Shikimori aired-episode counts and next-airing dates as a fallback when AniList scheduling data is unavailable.
• Added Russian and Japanese episode-backlog labels and regression tests for provider refreshes and cross-device schedule updates.

v2.9.19:

• Reduce Library-related UI stalls by reusing unchanged metadata and moving large native decoding and checksum work off the UI thread.
• Defer Google Drive sync while the player is open, keep progress saved locally, and automatically resume queued changes after leaving the player.
• Improve sync coordination during episode transitions and player shutdown, with safer deferred-sync status handling.

v2.9.18:

• Export your active Local Library from Settings to MyAnimeList XML or Shikimori JSON, including pending local edits, manga volumes, scores and dates where supported. Export works offline and reports entries without verified target IDs.
• Find Sources now starts with saved titles and enriches Russian, Japanese and English names independently, so AniList outages no longer block Russian searches. Provider matches are verified and cancelled searches stop their enrichment requests.
• Added optional MPV/FVP playback diagnostics with D-key micro-pause marking and manually saved, redacted reports. Diagnostics are at the end of Player Settings; no marker buttons or automatic report uploads.

v2.9.17:

• Choose AniList, MyAnimeList, or Shikimori as the only incoming library sync source; AniList is the default.
• Keep other connected catalogs as outgoing mirrors without allowing their edits or outages to overwrite the local library or switch the source.
• Safely retire obsolete destination conflicts and queued imports when changing the source, preserving local edits and audit history.
• Recover outgoing updates independently after restart and preserve unknown catalog-specific fields.

v2.9.16:

• Prevent unrelated catalog write echoes from downgrading Completed entries or clearing disputed dates and notes.
• Save conflict choices immediately and sync in the background without locking other entries.
• Fix duplicate sync delivery records and safely reconcile legacy account aliases and Google Drive confirmations.
• Report local database errors correctly without marking healthy catalogs unavailable.

v2.9.15:

• Reliable, independent library sync across AniList, MyAnimeList, Shikimori, and Google Drive, with immediate local saves.
• Automatic retries and catch-up after outages, reconnects, and app resume, without one unavailable catalog blocking others.
• Safer per-field reconciliation using genuine edit times, preserving precise scores, explicit clears, local-only fields, and change history.
• Clear per-anime conflict warnings and delivery details, including retry timing and sent-versus-confirmed status.
• Improved catalog pagination, write confirmation, and recovery of existing queued changes and verified duplicate records.

v2.9.14:

• Keep library progress and status unchanged when Auto Progress is disabled, while preserving playback resume positions.
• Restore shared episode progress from Google Drive and protect intentional resets from stale legacy checkpoints.
• Improve playback responsiveness with progressive proxy streaming and request-isolated retries.
• Reduce player UI rebuilds, repeated FVP metadata reads, and playback checkpoint overhead.
• Correct buffer range reporting and preserve existing seek, startup, and fallback behavior.

v2.9.13:

• Fixed a macOS shutdown bug where closing the window could leave MiruShin running or crash on Quit.
• Closing MiruShin now waits for the final playback checkpoint, background tasks, and all library databases before shutting down Flutter.
• Interrupted tracker deliveries remain queued and are checked before retrying on the next launch.

v2.9.12:

• Fixed cross-device status, score, and Favorite inconsistencies; Library cards and Edit now read the same canonical local state.
• Prevented stale provider previews, background queue writes, and rounded tracker scores from overwriting newer local changes.
• Isolated per-episode checkpoint revisions and deduplicated false sync conflicts while preserving genuine concurrent edits.
• Added safe, history-backed recovery for legacy library inconsistencies and 36 regression tests.
• Improved reactive local-library updates and avoided redundant no-op database writes.

v2.9.11:

• Restore fresh Google Drive Library changes before tracker sync on another device.
• Preserve Updated sorting and safely resolve cross-device conflicts.
• Keep delete/re-add operations ordered, and show clearer sync status.

v2.9.10:

• Local Library stays responsive while Google Drive restores data.
• Google Drive sync uploads small changes without rebuilding the full backup after every edit.
• Reduced backup processing on the UI thread and improved sync progress and counts.

v2.9.9:

• Fixed direct-media playback through the local proxy without requesting signed streams twice.
• Reuse a proven playback route for the next episode while keeping fallbacks.
• Redacted signed media URLs from player diagnostics.

v2.9.8:

• Fixed Google Drive Sync getting stuck after uploading local changes when a tracker API is unavailable.
• Improved sync progress, retry handling, and background storage-size refresh.
• Added details and a safe Ignore option for Library entries with unavailable metadata.

v2.9.7:

• Faster cross-device Library sync: recent Google Drive changes arrive before tracker reconciliation, without duplicate uploads from the receiving device.
• AniList, MAL and Shikimori now deliver rapid delete and re-add actions in order, with independent retries and safer confirmation after failures.
• Completing anime fills the known episode total and finish date together; unknown totals are requested explicitly.
• Reduced unnecessary Google Drive backups and improved sync progress reporting.

v2.9.6:

• Fixed Google Drive Library Sync convergence across new and existing devices.
• Devices now pull snapshots and immutable operations independently of the delivery lease.
• Added safe recovery for missed progress, additions, and removals without overwriting concurrent local edits.

• Improved sync progress counts and partial-sync messages in English, Russian, and Japanese.

v2.9.5:

• Fixed video freezing while audio continued by restoring MediaKit/mpv platform-tested frame-dropping and A/V-sync defaults.

v2.9.4:

• Restored native Google Drive sign-in on iPhone, iPad, and Android phones/tablets.
• Kept the secure Cloudflare Worker browser flow as a fallback for re-signed, LiveContainer, TrollStore, jailbreak, and Android TV installations.
• Added regression tests for platform-specific Google Drive login routing.

v2.9.3:

• Rebuilt Local Library as an offline-first source of truth with separate AniList account workspaces and safer AniList, MyAnimeList, and Shikimori reconciliation.
• Expanded Google Drive Sync for complete library metadata, settings, addons, connections, playback state, and faster cross-device restoration.
• Fixed repeated Google Drive synchronization when nothing changed, improved pending and progress states, and made real local changes upload promptly.
• Added AniList outage fallbacks and cache-first Board, Discovery, Library, and details loading for faster navigation.
• Fixed immediate library add, edit, and remove behavior, per-page Library filters, account isolation, and local database placement.
• Fixed crashes when removing anime from the Library editor and when closing MiruShin on macOS.

v2.9.1:

• Improved Google Drive Library Sync with more reliable cross-device restore.
• Added complete library checkpoints with metadata and artwork for faster setup on new devices.
• Improved sync integrity with safer atomic restores and validation.
• Library data can now restore and display before connected trackers finish loading.
• Fixed MyAnimeList fallback handling for manga.
• Improved metadata synchronization and overall Library Sync stability.

v2.9.0:

• Added a canonical local-first Anime and Manga Library with safe offline mutations, Library Log, undo, conflict protection, and per-account workspaces.
• Added independent bidirectional sync for AniList, MyAnimeList, and Shikimori with exact ID matching, provider snapshots, safer reconciliation, and richer metadata fallback.
• Added optional Google Drive Sync for libraries, playback progress, stream preferences, addons, accounts, API connections, Watch with Friends preferences, and per-workspace settings.
• Added all AniList score formats, including 100-point, decimal, 10-point, 5-star, and smiley scoring.
• Improved OAuth login flows across mobile, desktop, TV.

v2.8.9:

• Added instant local Library updates for add, edit, delete, progress, score, notes, and repeat actions.
• Added more reliable AniList, MAL, and Shikimori synchronization.
• Added offline change support with automatic synchronization after reconnecting.
• Fixed newly added anime not appearing until a manual refresh.
• Fixed completed anime remaining in Watching.
• Fixed incorrect episode progress, such as 13/12.
• Fixed changes being applied to the wrong anime after Library reordering.
• Removed unnecessary Library reloads and delayed UI updates.
• Improved favorite and score update consistency.

v2.8.8:

• Fixed missing next-episode countdowns when AniList libraries are merged with MAL fallback data.

v2.8.7:

• Improved Watch Order with theme-colored current-title highlighting, personal score, and favorite status.

v2.8.6:

• Fixed player sessions not terminating correctly and restored proper playback speed handling.
• Fixed expired airing schedules still appearing in the Library.
• Improved seeking controls by separating arrow tap and hold behavior.

v2.8.5:

• Fixed streams freezing during startup and playback unexpectedly resuming after being paused.
• Fixed playback-speed changes causing stalls or showing a speed that was not actually applied.

• Added accumulated seek-distance feedback when repeatedly using the left and right arrow keys.
• Improved the Library AniList outage notice with scrolling, MyAnimeList fallback status, dismissal, and correct spacing.

v2.8.2:

• Improved add-on import, export, and backup reliability across devices.
• Fixed add-on restoration so exported configurations retain required module data and settings.

v2.8.1:

• Fixed MAL and Shikimori fallback responses overriding AniList library status and progress after an AniList outage.
• AniList now remains canonical when selected as the primary tracker, while fallback snapshots stay available without reopening completed titles.
• Local changes made during an outage remain queued and sync to AniList first, then independently to connected MyAnimeList and Shikimori accounts.
• Prevented automatic playback progress from reopening completed titles or dropping rewatching status.
• Entry edits now sync only fields that actually changed, so score or notes edits cannot overwrite status or progress.

v2.8.0:

• Added MyAnimeList fallback for AniList outages across Board, Discovery, media details, Library, and Watch Order, with automatic return to AniList after recovery.
• Added local-first tracking: progress, favorites, status, score, notes, repeat count, and dates are saved locally and safely synchronized later.
• AniList, MAL, and Shikimori now synchronize independently using stable media identity, offline mutation queues, provider health tracking, and conflict resolution.
• Library filters, sorting, Watch, Edit, Play, and continue-watching now work with locally cached and MAL fallback data during AniList outages.
• Fixed AniList outage banner spacing in Library to match Board and Discovery.

• Video quality can differ between participants while the episode, module, server, and voiceover remain synchronized.

• Added a dedicated Buy Me a Coffee support card after Accounts in AniList Settings and below MiruShin updates in TMDB Settings.

v2.7.12:

• Fixed Security Check verification loops on macOS and iOS.
• Fixed content not loading after completing verification.
• Prevented duplicate Security Check windows from opening.
• Improved cookie persistence and browser session handling during verification.
• Fixed offline HLS playback on macOS.

v2.7.11:

• Improved AniList reliability with a 30-second timeout and one automatic retry before falling back to cached data.

v2.7.10:

• Added automatic anime Watch Order with full franchise discovery and a Main story only filter.
• Added AniList progress and bold, theme-colored status labels to Watch Order.
• Replaced Related Titles with a cleaner, transparent Watch Order list.
• Cached Anime Themes for the current session to prevent repeated loading.

v2.7.9:

• Added clean share links for AniList anime and manga and TMDB movies and TV shows.
• Improved link safety while keeping existing MiruShin links fully compatible.

v2.7.8:

• Added clearly labeled IMDb ratings to TMDB movie/series and matched AniList anime detail pages, displayed directly after the original score.
• Profile action cards now fit up to five per row on larger screens, with additional cards wrapping cleanly.

v2.7.7:

• Fixed Compact Cards appearing outside the row edges while scrolling, while preserving hover effects.
• Compact Cards are now disabled by default; existing saved preferences remain unchanged.

v2.7.6:

• Expanded the AniList Board with Favorites, Airing, Upcoming, Finished, Newest, and Recently Updated sections.
• Added adaptive pagination to Board and Discovery: compact rows load automatically, while wide grids offer Load More and fetch results based on screen size.
• Made compact cards the default and improved responsive layouts with up to eight columns.
• Polished poster clipping, gradients, hover animations, and button press effects.
• Reduced the media-details hero height and improved Board loading feedback.

v2.7.5:

• Added a Fanart.tv-powered Gallery to Media Details with 4K-first backgrounds, cached results, and an optional securely stored API key in Settings.
• Added a fullscreen Gallery viewer with original-resolution artwork, swipe and arrow navigation, zooming, and an image counter.

• Improved Discovery on large screens with responsive filter controls and up to eight poster columns while preserving compact mobile layouts.

v2.7.4:

• Added cross-platform MiruShin deep links for opening AniList and TMDB titles directly in the app.

• Opening an AniList or TMDB MiruShin link now automatically switches to the matching catalog.
• Watch with Friends default invites now use normal clickable HTTPS links, while existing mirushin:// invite links remain supported.
• Improved Self-hosted Relay invites with cleaner direct HTTPS links and browser landing pages for opening rooms in MiruShin.
• Added a Setup Guide button for Self-hosted Relay configuration, with English, Russian, and Japanese localization.
• Improved macOS fullscreen transitions so the player waits for the native fullscreen transition to actually finish before closing or opening the next episode.
• Improved timeline hover and drag handling, preventing seek previews and player controls from getting stuck after fullscreen or window-state changes.
• Improved progressive seek previews to prefer the later thumbnail when two cached frames are equally close to the selected position.
• Fixed backup exports not correctly including some saved list-based settings and filters on desktop platforms.

v2.7.3:

• Added cross-platform MiruShin deep links for opening AniList and TMDB titles directly in the app on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS.
• Added shareable MiruShin links to media details, alongside the original AniList or TMDB page links.

• Opening an AniList or TMDB MiruShin link now automatically switches to the matching catalog.
• Watch with Friends default invites now use a normal clickable HTTPS link that opens the room in MiruShin, while existing mirushin:// invites remain supported.
• Improved Self-hosted Relay invites with clean HTTPS links using the relay address directly, without redundant relay or transport parameters.
• Added browser landing pages for Self-hosted Relay invites with an Open in MiruShin action.

v2.7.2:

• Added full MiruShin configuration backup and restore in Settings → Data & backup.
• Backups include app and player settings, saved page and library filters, viewing progress, per-title stream choices, Watch with Friends relay and trust settings, installed Sora add-ons, source cookies, and local source state.
• AniList, MyAnimeList, and Shikimori sessions, profiles, saved AniList accounts, user settings, access tokens, and avatar URLs are included, along with configured TMDB and TVDB credentials.

• Improved Watch with Friends so guests retain their local and tracker progress while episode navigation and auto-next remain controlled by the host.
• Prevented locked guests from triggering next-episode actions through automatic playback, player controls, keyboard shortcuts, or Picture-in-Picture.
• Improved Watch with Friends synchronization by ignoring implausible cross-device timestamp differences that could incorrectly advance playback.
• Reworked compact media detail pages with responsive poster and text scaling, improved forced-compact behavior, and better narrow-screen layouts.
• Improved the fullscreen poster and background viewer: single tap closes it, double tap resets zoom, and existing zoom, drag, Escape, and system-back controls remain supported.
• Added complete English, Russian, and Japanese localization for backup and restore controls, warnings, confirmations, results, and errors.

v2.7.1:

• Added an option to enable or disable seek previews in Player Settings.
• Improved Watch with Friends with copyable invite links and additional localized room, connection, and relay controls.
• Posters can now be opened and viewed fullscreen from media details.
• Background images can now be opened and viewed fullscreen from media details.

v2.7.0:

• Added Self-hosted Relay support for Watch with Friends as an alternative when the default peer-to-peer connection does not work.
• Self-hosted rooms support one host and multiple guests at the same time.
• Added relay configuration and connection testing directly in Watch with Friends settings.
• Guests can join self-hosted rooms through invite links without manually configuring the relay.

• Added a complete open-source Cloudflare relay implementation that users can deploy and host themselves.
• The relay only handles Watch with Friends synchronization and never proxies video or audio streams.

v2.6.9:

• MiruShin now remembers your selected server and quality for each title and restores them automatically.
• Next episodes are prepared in the background for faster, smoother auto-next transitions.
• Added cache retention settings for metadata and artwork, with options from 1 week to never expire.
• Improved cache management so artwork and metadata share the configured cache size more efficiently.
• Watch with Friends hosts can now allow guests to change streams during a watch party.
• Guests can see which playback controls they have permission to use.

v2.6.8:

• Added progressive seek previews for online videos.
• Previews generate across the entire timeline in multiple refinement passes.
• The closest available preview appears immediately and improves as more frames generate.
• Generation continues in the background while the player is open.
• Choose between Progressive timeline (default) and On demand in Player Settings.
• Offline seek previews remain unchanged.

v2.6.7:

• Fixed Cloudflare security verification getting stuck in a refresh loop.
• Fixed source parsing starting before verification was complete.
• Removed duplicate WebView navigation events on Windows.
• Improved Cloudflare reliability across Windows, Android, iOS, and macOS.

v2.6.6:

• Added seek thumbnail previews for faster and more accurate timeline navigation.
• Improved timeline hover and seek behavior without moving the real playback position.

• Auto-next now always starts the next episode from 00:00 while manual episode selection still resumes saved progress.
• Fixed auto-next failing after returning to and rewatching a previous episode.
• Fixed episodes occasionally getting stuck at the end instead of advancing.
• Added stricter end-of-episode detection to prevent premature auto-next.
• Fixed manual seeking occasionally jumping back to the previous playback position.
• Improved FVP/MDK handling of stale end-of-stream events during and after seeking.
• Improved playback recovery for premature or inconsistent stream EOF states.
• Fixed fullscreen state being incorrectly carried to the next episode on desktop.
• Fullscreen transitions now follow the player's actual current fullscreen state.
• Improved next-episode stream resolution and retry handling.
• Episode selection now remains visible while the next stream is being resolved.
• Improved offline episode continuation and auto-delete reliability.
• Added safer playback generation tracking to prevent stale callbacks and duplicate episode transitions.
• Added 2.25x and 2.75x playback speed options.
• Improved native PiP completion and progress handling.
• iOS Home Indicator now stays auto-hidden across player navigation and auto-next transitions.
• Various playback stability improvements, race-condition fixes, and regression tests.

v2.6.5:

• Fixed Sora/Cloudflare security checks not completing on Android, iOS, and macOS.
• Fixed protected requests failing after verification by keeping them in the verified browser session.
• Fixed redirected requests losing their original endpoint path and query.

v2.6.4:

• Fixed Sora/Cloudflare security checks not completing on Android, iOS, and macOS.
• Fixed Windows crashes when starting Sora/Cloudflare security checks.
• Fixed protected-source parsing across supported platforms.

v2.6.3:

• Fixed protected-source parsing across Android, iOS, macOS, and Windows.

v2.6.2:

• Fixed Sora/Cloudflare security checks crashing after completion on Windows.
• Fixed browser session and cookie handling across supported platforms.

v2.6.1:

• Fixed Sora/Cloudflare security checks crashing after completion on Windows.
• Fixed browser session and cookie handling across supported platforms.

v2.6.0:

• Fixed Sora and Cloudflare challenge handling on Windows.
• Improved playback reliability with smarter stream fallbacks and DASH-to-HLS support.

• Added faster, more resilient catalog loading with metadata caching.
• Hidden AniList account and tracker connections while using the TMDB catalog.

v2.5.0:

• Fixed offline playback occasionally freezing around 7 seconds with automatic stall recovery.
• Randomized the Board hero from the top 20 anime.
• Improved AniList profile action buttons with a compact mobile layout.
• Added the Z keyboard shortcut for player zoom.
• Added a persistent option to enable or disable horizontal swipe seeking.
• Improved mobile volume behavior and disabled vertical swipe volume gestures on all devices.
• Redesigned and repositioned Watch, Trailer, and Edit buttons for responsive layouts.
• Fixed an AniList details overflow affecting popularity and favorites on narrow screens.

v2.4.4:

• Fixed the blank-window startup crash.

v2.4.3:

• Improved airing notification reliability when platform services are unavailable.
• Improved playback and external-link diagnostic logging.
• Reorganized internal code for clearer feature boundaries and easier maintenance.
• Improved automated testing across catalog, widget, Sora, and Worker components.

• General stability and maintenance improvements.

v2.4.2:

• Improved play/pause responsiveness and playback resume stability.

• Choose whether airing notifications include all eligible titles or only Watching/Rewatching.
• Removed the AniList Profile Feed and Reviews sections.

v2.4.1:

• Added anime opening and ending themes to anime detail pages.
• Fixed playback time jumping backward after seeking or skipping an opening or ending.
• Fixed Skip and Undo buttons appearing at the same time while buffering.

v2.4.0:

• Expanded Russian and Japanese translations across filters, settings, profiles, libraries, and media details.
• Localized player and trailer controls, along with AniList entry labels.
• When Russian (Shikimori) is selected, Shikimori YouTube trailers now prioritize Озвучка, followed by Субтитры.

v2.3.0:

• Added much better filters in Discovery, Library, and Source Modules.
• Filters now support include and exclude actions.
• Added much better filters in Discovery, Library, and Source Modules.

• Added AniList source/origin filters, adult content filter, licensing filter, and improved tag browsing/search.
• Improved Library filters with sorting/grouped tags and extra metadata filters.

• Added ASS/SSA subtitle parsing support.
• Improved player stability when streams fail to load or internet is weak.
• Made seeking more reliable so the player position and progress UI stay in sync.
• Fixed player controls sometimes not hiding properly on mobile/iOS.
• Improved keyboard shortcut handling in the player.
• Improved Skip OP/ED button visibility so it follows the player UI correctly.

v2.2.0:

• Watch with Friend: watch any episode in sync with a friend over a peer-to-peer connection.
• Create a room, share the 6-character code or QR, and playback stays locked together automatically.
• Host playback actions like play, pause, seek, and speed changes are instantly mirrored to the guest with drift correction.
• The host can optionally allow the guest to control playback, seek, or change speed.
• The guest resolves the stream source locally, so video is not routed through a server and quality is unaffected.
• Auto-reconnect after brief network drops, so the party can resume without rejoining.

v2.0.2:

• Added left-edge swipe-back gesture support on mobile.

v2.0.0:

• Added Cloudflare verification support: when required, a webview opens for captcha verification, then continues automatically after verification is complete.

• Improved subtitle parsing, including more accurate language detection and display.
• Improved the quality picker for better handling of streams with multiple quality options.

v1.9.0:

• Added MyAnimeList and Shikimori account connections alongside AniList.
• Sync your status, episode progress, and score across AniList, MyAnimeList, and Shikimori.
• Sign in securely from Settings -> Connections using OAuth.
• Choose your Library source from AniList, MyAnimeList, or Shikimori.
• Offline updates are now queued and synced automatically when you are back online.
• Added optional custom API credentials for MyAnimeList and Shikimori.
• Your tokens are stored securely on your device.

v1.8.1:

• Fixed auto next episode and watched progress triggering too early on unstable or reloaded streams.
• Next episode button now counts down 5 to 1, then closes the player if you don't continue.
• Next episode button shows shortly after the episode ends instead of instantly.
• Added a keyboard shortcuts and touch gestures panel in player settings.
• New keys: C toggles subtitles, P enters Picture in Picture, V skips intro/outro or goes to next episode.

v1.8.0:

• Added an Episodes button in the player so you can jump to any episode directly.
• Improved player controls so labels switch to icons earlier and never feel cramped.

• Now Playing now shows the real AniList/TMDB title in your selected language, with smart fallback support.
• Fixed TMDB library progress showing 0% instead of the correct watch percentage.
• Settings now adapt to your selected catalog mode.
• TMDB mode now hides AniList options and accounts.
• AniList mode now hides TMDB-specific options.
• Removed the redundant TMDB enable toggle.
• Added a new Compact cards toggle for Board cards.

• Removed unused settings: Poster card style, Subtitle preferred language, and Region/country.
• Removed the redundant Discovery status bar for a cleaner browsing experience.

v1.7.3:

• Added an MSI installer for Windows (.msi), alongside the existing setup .exe and portable .zip. The MSI lets you choose a per-user or all-users install.
• Fixed Android TV D-pad navigation on the Home and Discovery screens: focus no longer skips the movie posters and jumps straight to the "see more" / "Load more" button, so you can now reach and select every poster.

v1.7.2:

• Fixed playback speed not being restored after the player restarts.
• Added a short delay before auto-playing the next episode after the current stream finishes.

v1.7.1:

• Added Clear All and Apply buttons to the source filter.
• Updated several localization strings.

v1.7.0:

• Added a new Sources page. You can open it from the Sources button on the Addons page.
• You can now add your own catalog by pasting a catalog URL, for example example.com/modules.json.
• You can open a source, browse its addons, and install them into your library with one tap.
• Addons that are already installed are now clearly marked.
• Added search by addon name, author, language, and type.
• Added filters for multiple languages and types at the same time, for example Russian + English or anime + movies.

• You can now refresh, rename, copy the URL, or remove a source.
• Removing a source will not remove your installed addons.

v1.6.4:

• Added support for adding addons by addon ID.

v1.6.3:

• TMDB season picker now shows the real number of seasons from the addon.
• Fixed watch progress not tracking for TMDB episodes in the local library, including across auto-next season changes.

v1.6.2:

• Fixed auto-next episode and watch progress for auto-played episodes.

• Previously, when an episode started automatically, watch progress was not saved and the next episode did not play correctly.
• Now every episode saves progress, marks itself as watched at 85%, and reliably continues to the next episode.

v1.6.0:

• Android TV support with Leanback launcher/banner, TV-aware navigation, focus rings, and d-pad-friendly cards.
• Player remote fixes: OK play/pause, paused UI focus navigation, Settings/Quality/Episodes/Subtitles reachable by d-pad, sliders no longer trap focus, Back hides chrome first.
• Android TV WebView cursor improvements: smaller/smoother cursor, native tap fallback, better keyboard/textbox handling, and cursor support for YouTube trailers.
• AniList editor improvements from TV: hold OK on media cards opens entry edit actions where supported.
• Library/search/addon/settings text fields improved for d-pad escape.
• Playback fixes including seek/d-pad fixes, PiP handling fixes, iOS PiP fix, and player back-button fixes.
• AniList and Shikimori metadata/library fixes.

v1.5.0:

• Improved auto-next episode, mark as watched, and AniList sync.
• Fixed progress on finished streams, even when the stream jumps back to 0:00.
• Fixed player controls and mouse cursor not hiding after auto-next.
• Fixed buffering spinner sometimes staying visible after playback resumes.
• AniList now marks anime as Completed when you finish the last known episode.
• Fixed Trailer button, now it appears correctly on all devices.
• Moved Auto AniList progress setting, now it only shows in the AniList catalog.
• Fixed settings not saving after app restart.
• Poster card style and compact mode are now remembered.

v1.4.4:

• Added a built-in TMDB key, so MiruShin works out of the box.
• TMDB metadata now loads on first launch without setup.
• Added a Use custom API key option in Settings -> API Connections.
• You can still use your own TMDB Read Access Token if needed.
• TMDB metadata is now enabled by default.

v1.4.3:

• Improved video playback reliability.
• Fixed some streams not playing when proxy playback failed.
• The player now automatically tries another playback method when needed.

v1.4.2:

• Episodes in the TMDB Catalog are now sorted by season.

v1.4.1:

• Fixed WebView support on Windows. YouTube trailers now play correctly on Windows.

v1.4.0:

• Added trailer support for AniList and TMDB catalogs. The trailer button is shown only when a trailer is available.

v1.3.8:

• Improved the anime and manga detail pages with a cleaner and more polished layout.
• Improved the Edit button design and placement.
• AniList cards now always open the Edit page in AniList mode.
• Fixed Auto-Next so it now keeps the server selected inside the player. The next episode will resolve using the chosen server instead of falling back to the old or default one.

v1.3.7:

• Added pinch-out gesture support in the player to switch to Zoom mode.
• Added pinch-in gesture support to switch back to Normal mode.
• Improved the left sidebar behavior, so it now switches states earlier and feels more responsive.
• Reduced the height of the top and bottom black fog effects in the player UI for a cleaner viewing experience.
• Fixed player initialization: the video now repaints immediately instead of waiting for mouse movement to trigger a rebuild.

v1.3.6:

• Added a custom accent color picker.
• Removed unused options from Settings for a cleaner experience.

v1.3.5:

• Added a floating popup notification for new app updates.
• Improved mobile auto-next playback. The next episode now opens immediately in fullscreen player mode for a smoother watching experience.

• Fixed slow Choose Episode loading for custom/addon sources.
• Episodes from the addon now appear first, using the addon’s own episode name and poster when available.
• AniList/AniZip episode titles and thumbnails now load lazily only after the episode list is already shown.
• Improved support for custom Sora episode formats, including grouped episode lists and chapter-style APIs.
• Reduced stale search work when switching from Find Sources to Choose Episode.
• Auto-next now fetches the latest addon episode list instead of relying on old cached episode data.

v1.3.4:

• Added animated hover backgrounds for Windows PiP buttons, making the controls feel smoother and more responsive.

v1.3.3:

• Smarter Escape key in the player.
• Infinite scroll on AniList Favourites.

v1.3.2:

• Improved Picture-in-Picture support on Windows for a smoother and more native-like experience.
• Fixed the missing app icon in the Linux .deb package.

v1.3.1:

• Fixed the Linux crash when opening an episode, video playback works again.
• Added a .deb package for Debian/Ubuntu (AppImage and tar.gz still available).

v1.3.0:

• Added a second player engine for improved playback stability.
• Added PiP-style mini player support for Windows and Linux.
• Added ARB localization support for English, Russian, and Japanese.
• Added a local HLS proxy for the MPV player engine.

v1.2.2:

• Added startup page selection in Settings.
• Added skip-marker source selection in Player Settings.
• Improved iOS PiP exit handling so the player restores correctly.
• Fixed AniList sync for the Favorite heart button.
• Changed the default catalog mode to AniList.

v1.2.0:

• Added support for custom headers for subtitle tracks and network requests.
• Fixed the AniList favorites list and added a Load More button.
• Added a Windows installer for easier installation.

v1.1.1:

• Updated the player loading indicator to use a cleaner white circular spinner.
• Added timeline preview on the player progress slider.
• Fixed the Android splash screen logo display.

v1.1.0:

• Added airing anime notifications for supported platforms.
• Added favorites support for anime, manga, and edit pages.
• Added AniList status badges on Board and Discovery posters.
• Improved mobile double-tap seeking speed and feedback.
• Changed swipe seeking to use 2-second steps.
• Improved temporary speed badge position and styling.
• Fixed iOS PiP close cleanup so the player overlay clears correctly.
• Polished AniList edit dialog progress controls.
• Improved anime and manga tags.
• Added Edit action for Board and Discovery pages.

v1.0.2:

• Added a shortcut in Settings to open AniList settings.

v1.0.1:

apps.name: Nyxian
apps.subtitle: IDE to develop native code iOS apps and utilities on stock iOS it self just via a certificate and a custom micro kernel for those apps
apps.localizedDescription:
What is it?:

Nyxian is an iOS app that empowers developers with a full toolchain they can use while even being offline for iOS development on iPhone. It supports Swift, C, Objective-C, C++ and Objective-C++. It’s a powerful IDE that made the impossible possible, a fully on-device iOS IDE that doesn’t even need a cloud and can even be used with airplane mode enabled after it downloaded the SDK and resources from our server. It supports officially iOS 18.0 all the way up to the latest iOS version (iOS/iPadOS 27.2 Beta 2 tested). You can compile and run iOS apps on the go with ease, using the entire iOS 26.5 SDK.

apps.name: Swift Radio
apps.subtitle: Professional Radio Station App for iOS!
apps.localizedDescription:
Swift Radio:

Open-source iOS radio app with a SwiftUI interface. Used by 80+ apps on the App Store.

Looking for Android? See Swift Radio Android. Same station format, native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.

Features:

• Stream live radio with background audio playback.
• Scrubber and progress bar for non-live streams.
• Apple CarPlay support.
• Album art and track metadata from streams and iTunes API.
• Lock screen and Control Center integration.
• Multiple stations from a local or remote JSON file.
• Pull to refresh and optional search bar.
• Localization-ready via Xcode String Catalog.
• About screen with email, sharing, and external links.

Built on FRadioPlayer for streaming, metadata parsing, and iTunes album art fetching.

versions.localizedDescription:
Swift Radio’s stations list, Now Playing, station information and About screens have been rebuilt in SwiftUI, preserving the familiar station cards, artwork, marquee titles and popup player.

What’s new:

• Rebuilt navigation, popup presentation and options-sheet transitions, including returning directly to the player after sharing.
• Improved playback and audio-session coordination. Scrubbing resumes playback, while a later Pause, Stop or station change takes precedence over an older seek.
• Shared station and playback state across iPhone and CarPlay, keeping artwork and metadata aligned.
• Loading, retry and pagination support for larger CarPlay catalogs.
• SwiftRadioCore separates playback, catalog loading, artwork and system-media integration from the interface, making the app easier to maintain and extend.
• Swift 6 with complete concurrency checking.

apps.name: Tolkara
apps.subtitle: Tolkara runs unmodified arm64 macOS applications on an iPad, with
apps.localizedDescription:
Tolkara:

Tolkara runs unmodified arm64 macOS applications on an iPad, with experimental iPhone support. It loads the original executable as data, executes its instructions natively on the device's Apple silicon, and translates the macOS API calls it makes (AppKit, Metal, CoreAudio, Carbon, Security, …) into their iOS/iPadOS equivalents.

It follows the model of Wine and Valve's Proton: the program is not ported or patched, and its executable is never modified or re-signed. Only the operating-system calls underneath it are translated. The application's own code, logic, assets and network protocol are left exactly as the vendor shipped them.

Tolkara is a do-it-yourself developer project. You build it yourself.

versions.localizedDescription:
Tolkara 0.2.1: WoW water on the iPad, older iPhones, easier setup.

World of Warcraft Forever's water no longer renders black on the iPad. The iPad hides its GPU from the I/O Registry, so the game took it for an AMD GPU; Tolkara now describes the GPU as a Mac with Apple silicon does (--native-gpu-identity restores the old answers). New opt-in diagnostics: --trace-metal and --trace-iokit.

GPUs without BC texture sampling (A16 and older iPhones) now run games that use BC1-BC7 textures: Tolkara decodes them on the CPU and stores them uncompressed. WoW Classic runs on an iPhone 15 Plus this way.

Tolkara Management finds your team when Xcode is signed in but has never signed anything, asks for the Team ID when Xcode has not saved it, and has you start WoW once on the Mac before copying it, so the copy has the region the game saves on its first start. Steam Cloud now unpacks zipped downloads from Steam's own client.

Commits since v0.2.0:

• 920b4da IOKit: a stand-in GPU entry where the iPad's sandbox shows no accelerator.
• f54662e Metal, IOKit: GPU identified as on a Mac with Apple silicon; creation and registry traces.
• 9b11dd9 Metal: build the BC fallback for the simulator too.
• 691026c Metal: store BC textures uncompressed on GPUs without BC sampling.
• 50611a6 Metal: CPU decoders for BC1-BC7 texture blocks.
• 4a8a677 Tolkara Management: find the team when Xcode is signed in but never signed anything.
• 754bc1b Tolkara Management: start WoW once on the Mac before it is copied.
• 705b134 Profiles: WoW copies need the region the game saves on its first Mac start.
• 454e073 Tolkara Management: ask for the Team ID when Xcode has not saved the team.

Waterfalls now have continuous flowing detail with corrected scrolling/interpolation, transparency and reflection masks. The river near Snowflake Mountain follows its authored flow.

versions.localizedDescription:
R5 — COD4iOS 1.0.4 build 13:

Fixes the pointer corruption identified in the supplied build 12 War Pig crash log. This is an unsigned pre-release IPA;.

Campaign crash:

All three build 12 crashes resolve to Path_UpdateBrushBadPlaceCount, reading entity angles at pointer + 0xec. The bad pointer contains float radius bits 0x43aad91d in its upper half. Path_MakeBrushBadPlace wrote the radius through arc.origin[1] at byte 4 of a union containing an 8-byte entity pointer. It now initializes the union and writes brush.radius at its correct native offset. The AI danger zone remains active, with its pointer and radius preserved.

A regression runs the production initializer and actual union layouts under AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. The old write reproduces the exact supplied fault address 0x43aad91d0604b8f4; the corrected initializer passes. This addresses the reported signature without disabling mission AI or swallowing crashes. Other historical crash signatures in the accumulated log are not claimed fixed by this change.

Black surfaces / fog:

Build 12 only preserved zero masks for MUL/MAD instructions writing directly to a colour output. Fog can first be calculated in temporary registers and then copied or selected into the output. The correction now covers Metal pixel-shader MUL/MAD in those temporary registers too.

The expanded GPU test reproduces the gap: build 12 fails 96 channels across 160 cases; build 13 has 0 incorrect channels. It covers direct/temporary destinations, MUL/MAD, both operand orders, signed zero, finite controls and NaN/Inf. All 299 saved representative shaders translate and compile successfully. GLES/GLSL source fingerprints remain unchanged; no Android APK was produced.

The affected War Pig scene has not been run on the tester's device here. The black-surface cause and full campaign continuation still require on-device confirmation. These GPU tests do not establish device frame-rate performance.

Package:

SP and MP arm64 iPhoneOS engines rebuilt; embedded binaries match build outputs. Bundle, watermark and diagnostics all report build 13. ZIP integrity, exported symbols and temporary ad-hoc signature checks pass; signatures are removed for signing with your usual tool. No retail game files or saves are included.

Install as an update to the same com.devz.cod4ios installation. Keep your existing players folder. If War Pig still fails, provide the new build 13 diagnostics/native-crash.txt and campaign-events.txt; if the surfaces remain black, also provide kisakcod.log.

Code and IPA are committed under this release tag. The corresponding source archive contains the actual local build sources, including earlier uncommitted work; the new code commit is scoped to the changes above.
