About:

Concat is a free, open-source video editor and a CapCut alternative for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. It covers what people actually open CapCut for: auto-captions, text-to-speech, background removal, keyframe animation, effects and titles, multi-track cutting, 4K export. With none of the catches: no watermark, no account, no subscription, no upload.

Everything runs locally on a native Rust engine with a GPU compositor. Install it, drop in footage, cut. The AI models for captions, voices and cutout download once from Settings and work offline after that. Your footage never leaves your disk.

Good for: TikTok, Reels and Shorts, YouTube videos, tutorials and screen recordings, podcast clips, memes.

versions.localizedDescription:
Concat 0.2.7:

Corrected on 16 October: these notes said a blur or a glow no longer stalls an export on Windows. That fix was taken out before the release, and the stall is still there (#297).

What changed:

• 🐛 An export from the window draws on a device of its own on Vulkan, so it no longer loses the GPU part way through (#324).
• 🖥️ An event loop that could not run says why, and the process exits 1.
• 📤 A phone's encoder that says "try again" is waited for, frame by frame and at the end (#286).
• 🐛 On Linux on arm64, closing the app no longer crashes on its way out.
• ✨ A "Use voice from timeline" switch in the Generate Captions sheet (#302).
• 🐛 There is no Microsoft Store edition any more. A blur or a glow can still stall an export on Windows while its shaders compile: that fix did not make 0.2.7 (#297).
• 🖥️ A dropdown's list scrolls under a finger, not only by its scrollbar.
• ✂️ Generate captions on a sounding clip's right-click menu (#302).
• 🐛 The installer speaks the app's languages.
• 🌍 The app speaks 25 languages, the same 25 its READMEs are in, and every script has a face to fall back on.
• 🌍 Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, Ukrainian, Dutch and Polish.
• 🌍 The check prints on a Windows console, and counts the lines still in English.
• 🖥️ New projects on an iPhone, a second Untitled project, a click that moved a clip, Detach that said nothing, and no dialog under the studio borrow (#299, #151, #247, #310, #283).
• 📱 Settings, logs and caches live where an iPhone app may write (#299).
• 🖥️ The section strip's highlight follows the section shown (#250).
• 🖥️ A title's words field follows the clip that is selected, and a blur writes only to the clip it was typed for (#139).
• 🐛 A timeline with more titles than the cache held is painted once, not every frame (#261).
• 🗣️ A voice the GPU cannot read is read again on the CPU (#291).
• ✨ An export that the GPU stops answering ends instead of freezing, and a phone's GPU draws with the limits it has (#297, #312).
• 📁 Opening the app opens no hardware encoder, so a CUDA driver cannot crash it before the window (#309).
• ✨ Open a GUI project with --project on launch.
• 🌍 Add the Vietnamese locale (#304).
• 🌍 Add Bengali (bn) translation (1016 strings).
• ✂️ The add-track menu's rows take their clicks.
• ✨ A ruler with ticks and numbers, wider bars, the clip light over the bars, a peak readout.
• ✂️ Copy and paste a selection, between timelines too, as one undo step.
• 📤 The sheet asks before replacing a file, refuses a name that is not a file's, and no dialog opens under the studio borrow.

• 📝 The CJK fallback face covers every character the locales use.
• 🐛 Text sits on whole pixels on a low-density screen.
• ✂️ A detached sound is a clip of its own, and goes where it is dragged.
• 📝 Chinese and Korean have a face to fall back on, and the setup speaks them.
• 🐛 A still keeps its own shape, instead of being stretched across the frame.
• 📝 Colour emoji render in their own colours, not the words'.
• 📱 A finished export goes into the phone's Movies, where the gallery shows it.
• 📤 The folder the file goes in is made, and a phone's sheet has no Browse.
• 🌍 The Japanese translation is updated.
• ✨ VU meters beside the timeline, so you can see how loud it plays.
• ✨ A preset card shows a word of its own writing, not "Aa".
• 🐛 Languages sits beside Styles on the Text page, not under it.
• ✨ The Text page's Presets shelf is Styles, with Languages under it.
• 📝 A searchable font picker that says when a font is missing.
• 📝 Base fonts every title can use, and presets that are data.
• ✨ A click previews a file without putting it on the timeline.
• ✂️ A click anywhere on the timeline sends the playhead there.
• ✨ Record from the microphone over the picture, onto the timeline.
• ✨ Effects drops its category pills, and reload is a square before the search.
• 🐛 The AppImage carries the X11 keyboard library, so it opens where that is missing.
• ✂️ A clip never lands on top of another.
• 🐛 Read what is held under the queued lock, so nothing is queued twice.
• 🐛 The run-on clock reads one word, so a torn read cannot step back.
• 🐛 A frame that raises a toast publishes it during playback.
• 🐛 Open the file a cut leads to once, not once a frame.
• 🐛 A checked rate is judged in lowest terms.
• 🐛 Let AMF make ten-bit HEVC, as Main 10.
• ⚡ Decode the full window ahead and open the next cut early.
• ⚡ Keep the queue while playback runs on.
• ⚡ Leave the font list alone when no font changed.
• ⚡ Publish only the picture for a frame during playback.
• ⚡ Ask for each frame on time during playback.
• ⚡ Carry the clock between the device's buffers.
• ⚡ Count how smoothly playback's frames arrive.
• 🤖 A method that panics fails that call, not the API.
• 📤 A frame rate no video has is an error, not a panic.
• 🐛 A folder named with either slash is one entry in the recents.
• 🐛 A layer's filter graph runs on one thread.
• 🐛 The encoder lets go of its file before the copy is moved into place.
• ⚡ The caches are sized to the machine, and let go of what is idle.
• 🐛 The page strip sits on the pane's top bar, with no dark track of its own.
• 🖥️ A sound clip's Speed sits under its Sound page.
• 🖥️ Adjust opens on its wheels and curves, and Speed sits under Basic.
• 🖥️ Enhance has a page of its own, and Enhance and background removal switch from their headers.
• ✨ A transition is selected on its own, with its own inspector panel.
• ✂️ The tray's plus opens an Add track menu, with top or bottom beside it.
• ✂️ A track's header keeps Delete in a More menu, and its marks are white.
• 🐛 Clips that were reversed or animated in 0.2.4 say so as the project opens.
• ✂️ A volume drag no longer drops words typed into a title.

Before you install:

• Intel Macs: this build needs macOS 13.4 or later. On macOS 12 it closes as it starts (#333).

A self-contained build for every platform Concat ships on.

apps.localizedDescription:
Overview:

Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra ships a feature called Super Steady with Horizon Lock that keeps your footage perfectly level no matter how much you tilt or shake the phone. It's one of the most impressive stabilisation tricks in mobile cameras right now - and it was exclusive to Android.

Stable Action brings that exact same experience to iOS. Point it at anything, tilt your wrist, run, jump, ride - the horizon stays locked flat, just like on the S26 Ultra. Built entirely in native Swift, runs 100% on-device, no subscriptions, no cloud.

apps.subtitle: A manga, manhwa, light‑novel and video reader for Android and iOS with an
apps.localizedDescription:
Foxlations:

A manga, manhwa, light‑novel and video reader for Android and iOS with an extension‑based source system. Add sources from any site with the built‑in RepoForge generator (beta), sync progress to AniList / MyAnimeList / Kitsu, back up and restore your library, and read behind Cloudflare‑protected sites.

Please note that I do school and work full time, so updates might be slow. I do see your messages and issues — it just might take me a bit to get to them!

RepoForge is in beta. It won't always generate a correct source — check what it produces and adjust the selectors if a site doesn't come out right.

Foxlations is a reader only. It does not host any content — you add your own sources.

versions.localizedDescription:
A big one — light-novel fixes, a Browse overhaul, and a lot of library polish.

Light novels & sources.

• Light-novel (LNReader) sources: fixed a crash when opening some sources, fixed a batch of sources that silently showed nothing, and every request now goes through the Cloudflare-aware path — so more sources load, and a blocked one shows an "Open in WebView" solve button instead of an empty screen.
• When a source fails it now tells you why — Cloudflare, site unreachable, or "needs an update" — instead of a blank "nothing found". Full details stay in More → Debug logs.
• Local sources you build in RepoForge now show up in the Browse repository filter.

Browse.

• Language filter overhaul: the same language is no longer listed twice when repos spell it differently ("English" and "en" now merge), languages show full names, and the picker is a searchable grid where you can pin the ones you use. Filtering by a repository hides languages that repo doesn't have.
• The Repository filter now matches the Language filter, and the Manga / Anime / Novel switch is one consistent control (with a sliding highlight) across Browse, Search and Discover. Pinned sources stay in sync everywhere.

Library.

• Library cards are now yours to arrange (library options → Display): put the title on the cover, below it, or hidden; place the badges in a bar under the cover, in the corner, or stacked on the cover bottom; and show reading progress as a thin line, a mini bar, or a % badge. Local sources get a folder badge, with a legend that explains each badge.
• Filter / Sort / Display was restyled to match the app, and filters are now tri-state: tap once to show only those, again to hide them, again to clear.
• Library updates show new chapters on each title the moment they're found instead of only when the whole check finishes; the Updates tab refreshes when you open it; and a redundant spinner in the header is gone.
• "Chapters read" and "Most-read series" now count your actual read chapters — including ones imported or marked read by hand — so they match the unread badge, streak and heatmap.
• New: a Default category so new titles file themselves automatically (Settings → Library).

Reader & chapters.

• Reader and light-novel settings use the app's sliding pill controls.

Discover.

• The genre filter is now a single "Genres" pill that expands in place, instead of a permanent strip of chips.

Security.

• App lock gained a "Lock after" timeout so a quick app-switch no longer forces you to re-authenticate (Settings → Security). Removed two toggles that weren't wired up yet.

Features:

Focus, simply.

• Drag around the dial to set 1–120 minutes, or tap 15 · 25 · 45 · 60. Start morphs into Pause and End in Liquid Glass.
• AlarmKit alarms ring through Silent mode and Focus, with Take a Break right on the alert.

iPhone & iPad: Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island (three styles), Home Screen widgets that start sessions, Lock Screen and StandBy widgets, a Control Center and Action Button toggle, Siri and Shortcuts ("Start a focus in Pomly", "How much time is left in Pomly?"), iPad and iPhone Duo layouts.

versions.localizedDescription:
Pomly 1.1: a calm Pomodoro timer for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch.

New in 1.1:

• Focus rooms: share a link and focus together, with a quiet "3 people focusing".
• Tasks: pick what each block is for, import from Reminders, then mark it Done or carry it over.
• Calendar (optional, Settings › Advanced): a suggested free gap and sessions logged to a Pomly calendar.
• Weekly insights in History: best hour, how sessions felt, a forgiving streak and a shareable recap card.
• After each session: an optional 1–5 "How did it feel?" and a short break tip.
• Ambient sound: white noise, brown noise or rain while you focus.
• Focus filter and Siri: a Focus can start and end sessions; "Focus on writing for 50 minutes" in Shortcuts.
• Pomly Focus for Safari (Mac), alongside Chrome. Free builds: Safari › Settings › Developer › Allow Unsigned Extensions.

In 1.0.4:

• Check for Updates: a button in Settings › Updates and, on Mac, in the Pomly menu.
• Safer Mac updates: the old app stays in place until the new one is ready, errors are shown, and an app outside Applications asks to be moved instead of retrying.

In 1.0.3:

• Fixed the New Label button, which did nothing on Mac. It now opens a small field on every platform.

In 1.0.2:

• Mac: the menu bar panel, drag line and guided drag now show over full-screen apps instead of on the desktop Space.

• Homebrew: brew tap tapariapurv/pomly https://github.com/tapariapurv/pomly && brew trust tapariapurv/pomly && brew install --cask pomly.
• One line: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tapariapurv/pomly/main/scripts/install.sh | bash.

iPhone, iPad & Apple Watch:

Sideload Pomly-iOS-unsigned.ipa with AltStore or Sideloadly (they sign it with your Apple ID), or build from source in Xcode. See the README.

Updates:

The Mac app updates itself from now on (Settings › Updates). On iPhone and iPad, add the AltStore source https://tapariapurv.github.io/pomly/altstore.json for automatic updates.

Highlights:

Drag-to-set dial · AlarmKit alarms · Live Activities & Dynamic Island · Home/Lock Screen/StandBy widgets · Control Center · Siri & Shortcuts · Mac menu bar timer with drag-to-set, mini timer and global shortcuts · Apple Watch app & complications · pairing-code sync · light & dark.

apps.name: Muguet
apps.subtitle: Precompiled release artifacts and CI orchestration for Muguet iOS. Open-source rebuild under GPLv3
apps.localizedDescription:
Muguet (iOSVN Rebuild):

An open-source native Mach-O ARM64 port of Grand Theft Auto V for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Powered by WebAssembly ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation and Apple Metal graphics.

• Native ARM64 Execution (No JIT Required):.

• Ahead-of-Time (AOT) Compiled: Game bytecode is precompiled into a native Mach-O ARM64 executable segment (__GAME).
• No Debugger / Tethering Needed: Runs at full native machine speed without requiring JIT debugging entitlements, Xcode tethering, or external developer tools.
• Compatible with iOS 15.0+: Supports 64-bit iOS devices running iOS/iPadOS 15.0 or newer.

• Apple Metal Graphics & 120 FPS Activation:.

• Direct Metal Pipeline: Graphics commands route directly through Apple Metal via wgpu.
• Zero Web Overhead: Bypasses browser sandboxes, WebGPU layers, and WebKit compositor overhead, minimizing draw-call latency and memory consumption.

versions.localizedDescription:
Muguet iOS Build 8.9 (Official Release):

Bản phát hành chính thức Build 8.9 mang toàn bộ các thiết lập đồ họa chi tiết của GTA V ra giao diện Launcher bên ngoài và Menu Pause bên trong game, đồng thời tinh gọn giao diện điều khiển cảm ứng, tối ưu kích thước nút bấm và nâng cao độ ổn định trên toàn bộ các dòng iPhone / iPad.

Các điểm mới & cải tiến nổi bật trong Build 8.9:

• Bảng Cài đặt Đồ họa GTA V Chi tiết (In-Game Graphics Settings Panel):.

• Thêm khu vực "🎮 Cài đặt Đồ họa GTA V Chi tiết" trực quan ngay tại Launcher và Menu Pause:.

• Chất lượng Đổ bóng (Shadows): Bình thường (Mượt nhất) / Cao / Rất cao.
• Khoảng cách Đổ bóng (Shadow Distance): Ngắn (0.5× - Tiết kiệm RAM/Pin) / Tiêu chuẩn (1.0×) / Xa (1.5×).
• Chất lượng Phản chiếu (Reflections): Bình thường / Cao / Rất cao.
• Chất lượng Cỏ cây & Thảo mộc (Grass): Bình thường (Chống tụt FPS khi lái xe ra ngoại ô Los Santos/đồi núi) / Cao / Rất cao.
• Chất lượng Mặt nước (Water): Bình thường / Cao / Rất cao.
• Chất lượng Hạt & Hiệu ứng cháy nổ (Particles): Bình thường / Cao / Rất cao.
• Hiệu ứng Hậu kỳ & Ánh sáng (Post FX): Bình thường (Tối ưu FPS) / Cao (Bloom & Tia nắng) / Rất cao.
• Lọc vân bề mặt (Anisotropic Filtering): Tắt (x0) / x4 / x8 / x16 (Rõ nét mặt đường).
• Khử răng cưa viền (FXAA): Bật / Tắt (Tối đa FPS).
• Mật độ Giao thông trên đường (Traffic Density): Vắng vẻ (0% - Tăng vọt FPS) / Vừa phải (50%) / Đông đúc (100% - Như PC).
• Mật độ & Đa dạng Người đi bộ (Pedestrians): Thấp (0% - Tiết kiệm RAM) / Vừa phải (50%) / Cao (100%).
• Tầm nhìn xa & Chi tiết vật thể (LOD Scale): Tiết kiệm RAM (-0.5) / Tiêu chuẩn (0.0) / Tầm nhìn xa (+0.5).

• Tự động đồng bộ và lưu trữ hai chiều vào settings.xml và config.json.
• Có thể tinh chỉnh trước khi vào game hoặc mở Muguet Menu trong khi đang chơi để áp dụng ngay lập tức.

Tinh gọn & Làm đẹp Giao diện Người dùng (UI Ergonomics):

• Giao diện Cấu hình Nhanh tinh gọn: 2 nút thiết lập nhanh ("⚡ 120 FPS Siêu Mượt" và "🍃 Tiết Kiệm RAM") được thiết kế lại dạng thanh ngang đôi (HStack) nhỏ gọn, thanh thoát, đúng chuẩn phong cách iOS.
• Ẩn thanh trượt thủ công dư thừa: Dọn dẹp 6 thanh trượt tọa độ và kích thước nút ở mục Điều khiển cảm ứng ngoài Launcher, tập trung trải nghiệm vào trình chỉnh sửa trực quan HUD Editor (chạm kéo thả và đổi cỡ trực tiếp trên màn hình).

Khóa an toàn các thiết lập gây lỗi & đen màn hình:

• ShaderQuality: Khóa an toàn ở mức 1 (High) tương thích tuyệt đối với bộ shader WGSL trên Metal, loại bỏ hoàn toàn lỗi màn hình đen sau khi đổi cấu hình.
• MSAA & TXAA: Cưỡng chế tắt để tránh quá tải bộ nhớ đồ họa (VRAM) trên Metal, chống văng ứng dụng (Out-Of-Memory).
• DX_Version: Cưỡng chế 2 (DirectX 11) tương thích tối đa với Apple Metal.
• Windowed: Cưỡng chế 2 (Borderless) để giữ nguyên swapchain buffer khi hiển thị.
• Cơ chế tự động khôi phục Metal surface (gpu::OCCLUDED = false) khi người chơi vuốt Control Center hoặc chuyển đổi ứng dụng rồi quay lại.

Tích hợp toàn diện các tính năng đã được kiểm chứng:

• Nút 1 chạm "Khôi phục đồ họa gốc (Sửa lỗi màn hình đen)".
• Cấu hình 1 chạm "⚡ 120 FPS Siêu Mượt" cho màn hình ProMotion.
• Cấu hình 1 chạm "🍃 Siêu Tiết Kiệm RAM (~800MB - 1GB)" cho máy RAM thấp.
• Bộ ghi log chẩn đoán sự cố tự động (Crash Reporter).
• Bộ mã gian lận (Cheat Menu) tích hợp đầy đủ.

Thông tin tệp tin phát hành::

• Tập tin: Muguet-v8.9.ipa.
• Dung lượng: ~70.4 MB (73,859,920 bytes).
• SHA-256: b8a5f8763331501be3d85292ae131767d5f8b152b37c8b6a6f6393d7b28d503f.

Lưu ý khi cài đặt::

• Cài qua TrollStore hoặc ký qua ESign (bật Keep Original Entitlements trong More Settings).
• Dữ liệu game đặt tại: Muguet/game/data và Muguet/game/b.

Cuda:

Your music. A little more calm.

Cuda is a music player for Apple Silicon, built by veikkaheiskanen. A native SwiftUI interface with Apple’s actual Liquid Glass brings Spotify, YouTube, YouTube Music, SoundCloud, optional Audius, and your own audio files into one place.

Built with help from ChatGPT.

Keep Mac and iPhone together with Settings → Device sync: one-time QR/link pairing, automatic offline audio transfer, and two-way playlists and favourites. Sync uses an authenticated encrypted local connection; the same pairing automatically connects iPhone YouTube and SoundCloud playback, with no separate companion command. Setup.

A place for every song:

• Home, made personal. Recommendations, recently played music, and playlists are always close by. Genres come from your listening history; recent listening, favourites and playlists shape what appears next.

versions.localizedDescription:
Home learns your music. Turn services on or off, choose a genre from Last played, and discover new recordings with fewer repeats.

• Streaming service choices apply to this iPhone or iPad. Disabled sources stay out of search and automatic playback, while offline music remains usable.
• Optional Audius catalog and playback through the paired Mac. Update the Mac to Cuda 1.0.11 for the new discovery and service controls.

• Adaptive genre controls keep Home readable with large text and on small screens.

Installation: this is an unsigned IPA for Sideloadly. Downloading an update cannot install it automatically: Sideloadly still needs to sign and install it. Your existing Shelf is retained when updating the same installed bundle ID. Spotify playback still requires separate authorization in Spotify and a correctly registered installed bundle ID.

Validation: 22 unit and integration checks, a native playback/UI test, and 12 iPhone/iPad layout captures. Physical-device Spotify authorization is not verified by the simulator.

apps.subtitle: Mobile variant of Horizon
apps.localizedDescription:
Disclaimer:

The Horizon project and its maintainers are not responsible for Solstice in any way. This includes, but is not limited to: bugs, crashes, data loss, security issues, behaviour differences, or anything else that may arise from using this software. Any issues you encounter should be reported here, not to the Horizon project.

Features:

In a non-exhaustive list, Solstice has these features!

• Profile matching automatically compares your profile with others to determine with whom you are compatible.
• Automatic ad posting repeatedly posts and rotates ads on selected channels.
• Link previews popup shows a preview of an image / video when you hover your mouse over a link.
• Caching speeds up profile loads and other actions.

versions.localizedDescription:
Built on Horizon 2.4.0.

Solstice can now pull your chat log history off Horizon on your computer, exporting logs works on both platforms, and a large import no longer freezes the app.

Changes since v2026.6.4:

• Syncing copes with big log folders. Logs transfer one bounded batch at a time in both directions instead of being packed into a single archive, so neither device holds the whole log set in memory and folders that were simply too big to sync now go through. The sync screen shows progress as each batch lands, and a conversation whose stored log turns out to be damaged is reported at the end instead of quietly ending the transfer.

• A large import no longer freezes the app. Importing a desktop backup locked everything up until it finished: 16 seconds for a 58 MB backup, 85 seconds for a 296 MB one. The import now runs in small batches and gives the app room to redraw between them, so it stays responsive throughout.

• Manage Data survives signing out (#17). Its tabs no longer freeze and its dialogs open again after logging out and back in.
• Tidier sign-in screen. The checkboxes and loading spinner match the rest of the app, the stray theme name under the picker is gone, and the screen now renders in whichever theme you picked rather than only the built-in ones.
• iOS builds against the current SDK (#20). Rebuilt for the iOS 26 and Xcode 27 SDK with scene-based lifecycle support. The minimum supported version is now iOS 15.

From Horizon 2.4.0:

• Dates and times follow your language. Timestamps use your display language's formatting instead of always using English.
• Translated summaries and correct plurals. The messages shown after an export or import are translated, and counted things ("5 messages", "1 channel") use the right plural form for your language, including the missing Spanish plural in the export summary.
• Character pickers show avatars. The character select dropdowns, such as on the profile viewer and the friends dialog, show the selected character's avatar.
• Friend requests show as pending. Sending a request from the profile viewer no longer lists you as that person's friend before they have accepted.
• Channels stay grouped. The grace period for pruning grouped channels is more sensible, so channels you joined correctly are no longer ungrouped moments after connecting.
• Ads and smart filters behave. Smart filters work with "Colorize ads" off, a busy ad queue no longer lets ads slip past unfiltered, and changing a filter setting now applies to ads already on screen.
• The quick switcher respects your channel groups. It follows your group order again.
• HQ profile pictures toggle without a restart. Turning the setting on or off takes effect immediately.
• "Standardize profile fonts" no longer breaks BBCode. Profiles using characters that parse into brackets render correctly, and emoji stay visible.
• Guestbook counts are accurate. Guestbooks with more than 15 posts show the real number.
• Searching the log viewer scrolls properly. Scrolling up while searching loads older messages without having to scroll again.
• Friend colors in the All Friends tab. Names are no longer all green when you color friends and bookmarks differently.
• Accessibility fixes. Colorblind mode colors and button text contrast were corrected, and screen reader labels no longer claim every public and private channel is official.
• Species matching. Lamia and naga are no longer scored as the same species when matching profiles.

Thanks:

• @FatCatClient for cleaning up the sign-in screen (#34) and for making the login screen load non-vanilla themes (#38). Their first contributions to Solstice.
• The Horizon contributors and the Weblate translators behind everything in the section above, who keep the German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian and Russian catalogs current.

apps.localizedDescription:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec24f92e-d29a-4319-8293-439487d60b35

Features:

• Native Engine: Runs flawlessly on iOS, due to the official PICO-8 engine being implemented as a WASM module.
• Quick Save & Load: The only PICO-8 experience with instant save states. Freeze time and resume anywhere, across devices.

• Adaptive Controls: Custom Gameboy-esque controls with tactile haptics. Works in portrait and landscape. Swap to virtual joystick.

Technical Look:

The core engineering challenge was reconciling the asynchronous nature of mobile file I/O with the synchronous requirements of the Emscripten/WASM virtual file system.

PICO-8 demands a synchronous file system. Bridging this to mobile required completely reverse-engineering the Emscripten boot sequence.

apps.localizedDescription:
3X-UI Manager:

Native mobile clients for managing 3x-ui panels over the REST API — dashboard, inbounds, clients (with QR sharing), nodes, and the Xray config, on the go. Multi-instance: connect to several panels and switch between them from one app.

✅ Compatible with 3x-ui panels up to v3.10.0. The app speaks the panel's stable REST API, so a new panel release does not require a new app version — no need to wait for an app update when the panel bumps (the rare exceptions are noted in this app's release notes). Panel 3.10.0 is one: creating Shadowsocks inbounds and MASQUE support need app v0.15.1 or newer.

This branch (main) holds the Android app (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose), built straight from the repository root.

versions.localizedDescription:
Covers everything since the previous stable release, 0.14.3 (0.15.1 and 0.15.2 were experimental builds).

Changed:

• Balancers and the Observatory settings have their own «Balancers» menu item under Routing. The Routing screen keeps the strategy, rules, route tester and the routing-script warning; rules can still target a balancer. The Observatory section has its own Save button, active only while its settings have unsaved changes.

Fixed:

• The update dialog now lists the changes of every version since the installed one, not just the latest. Each version has its own "Version X · date" heading, newest first, so updating over several versions no longer hides what the skipped ones changed.
• After saving Xray settings the app no longer asks to restart Xray. Since panel 3.3.1 the panel applies the change itself on save — live through the Xray API where it can (inbounds, outbounds, routing, balancers), restarting Xray only when a change can't be applied live. The inbound save prompt no longer claims Xray will restart. Outbound-subscription refreshes, moves and deletes are applied by the panel within 30 seconds; only editing a subscription still needs a restart, and the app says so.

Added:

• Observatory settings on the Routing screen, as in panel 3.10.0: for the active observer the probe URL, interval, timeout, sampling and HTTP method, plus the outbounds it watches. The panel and the app manage which observer exists; you tune how it probes.

Fixed:

• A balancer that needs an observatory made Xray fail to start. Least Load, and Random / Round-robin with a fallback, need a connection observer; the app never created one, so Xray stopped with "not all dependencies are resolved". The observer is now created, kept in sync with the balancers and removed when nothing needs it, exactly as the panel does it.

Added:

• Panel 3.10.0 support. The app works with panel 3.10.0 and keeps everything new it adds when you save.
• MASQUE inbounds (panel 3.10+): create them with an address pool, MTU and path; TLS is required, so TLS inbounds now have certificate and key file fields. MASQUE clients get their config only through the JSON subscription, so a client's share sheet now also shows the JSON subscription link when the panel serves it.
• "Use system CA" in outbound TLS (panel 3.10+): Xray-core 26.10.10 verifies servers against its bundled roots, so an outbound to a server with a private CA needs this switch.
• Lua scripts and DNS server ID (panel 3.10+): fields for a DNS server's ID, the DNS Lua script and the routing script. The Routing screen warns when a routing script is set, because Xray then ignores the rules.
• Hysteria and MASQUE outbounds (including WARP over MASQUE) now show their transport and TLS settings for editing.
• Certificate SHA-256 pin field for nodes that use certificate pinning.

Fixed:

• A new Shadowsocks inbound could not be created on panel 3.10. The app now generates a server key of the right length and regenerates it when the method changes; the 2022 ChaCha20 method, which the panel refuses on inbounds, is no longer offered.
• Save in the outbound editor did not write to the panel, so leaving the screen lost the change. It now saves at once, like the routing and DNS editors.
• Saving a DNS server dropped its ID, tag, client IP, expected IPs, skip-fallback and timeout settings. Expected IPs also showed empty for servers saved by the panel, and Skip fallback showed as on when it was not set.
• Saving an inbound reset its custom tag, subscription order, "exclude from subscription" flag and monthly reset day. A custom tag was regenerated, so routing rules pointing at it stopped matching. The Enabled switch in the inbound editor now really turns the inbound on or off.
• Editing a client turned off its weekly renewal and removed its VLESS reverse proxy.
• Editing a node switched "selected inbounds" sync back to "all", and nodes using certificate pinning could not be saved at all.
• A failed attach or detach of a client's inbounds was reported as "Client updated". The panel's error is shown now. With a MASQUE inbound selected, the client editor refuses an email containing ":".
• Changing a balancer's strategy dropped its leastLoad settings.
• The new-inbound list offered "socks", which the panel rejects; it now offers "mixed" (SOCKS + HTTP).
• WebSocket + TLS inbounds now default to ALPN http/1.1, so WebSocket connections no longer fail on h2. The inbound editor also hides transport and security choices that would break MASQUE, XDRIVE and TUN inbounds.
• The QR code is hidden for post-quantum links, as in the panel: such links are too dense to scan.

Android and iOS ports of MegaMan64Recompiled, built with N64ModernRuntime and RT64. This is an unofficial community project, not affiliated with Capcom.

Both platforms include editable gameplay and menu touch layouts, a movement stick, controller support, ROM import, and persistent saves. Use EDIT to move buttons or change size, opacity, and colors. MENU PAD and GAME PAD switch layouts; returning to gameplay from app settings honors pending Apply/Discard changes.

ROM requirement:

Import the ROM using the launcher's file picker. On Android, you can keep it in Downloads and select it there; access to Android's private application folder is unnecessary. On iOS, keep it in Files and select it, or use the app's shared Documents ROM drop folder.

versions.localizedDescription:
Android and iOS mobile builds of Mega Man 64: Recompiled.

• Editable gameplay and menu touch pads: movement stick, N64 buttons, position/size/opacity/color controls, and GAME PAD / MENU PAD switching.
• SDL USB/Bluetooth controller support and configurable bindings.
• Mobile renderer fixes, Android Vulkan surface/descriptor handling, and iOS screenshot/notification size restoration.
• Persistent USA FlashRAM saves, atomic replacement, backup writes, and background save flushing.
• The supplied Mega Man 64 artwork is now the app icon on both platforms.
• Both application IDs are com.devz.megaman64, matching the other ports' naming convention.

Downloads: install the ARM64 APK on Android 8.0+ with a compatible Vulkan GPU. Sign the ARM64 IPA for your own iOS 16+ device using eSign or another signing tool. The IPA contains no personal certificate or provisioning profile. SHA256SUMS.txt covers both downloads.

ROM: supply your own Mega Man 64 USA ROM through the launcher. .z64, .v64, and .n64 byte orders are accepted. Japanese Rockman DASH gameplay is not supported by this USA recompilation; the loader reports that limitation. No ROM or save data is bundled.

Existing saves: the new IDs create separate app storage. Back up the old app's config/saves folder before changing builds, preserve filenames, and keep the old app installed until the backup is safe. Storage locations and restoration limits are described in MOBILE.md. Saves are not automatically migrated between different IDs.

The repository starts with a clean source history and pinned dependencies. It excludes ROM-derived generated sources, ROMs, saves, logs, SDKs, local build folders, personal paths, and signing keys. Required build scripts, application assets, licenses, and upstream attribution remain available.

Upstream: https://github.com/MegaMan64Recomp/MegaMan64Recompiled

apps.name: NFSU2
apps.subtitle: Need For Speed Underground 2 Xbox Original port for iPhone, iPad and macOS. Native Metal renderer, touch, controller and keyboard controls
apps.localizedDescription:
NFSU2 for iPhone and iPad:

Unofficial native port of the original Xbox Need for Speed: Underground 2, based on myUdav4iik/nfsu2-ios and antoxa2584x/nfsu2-sw. Uses static recompilation and a native Metal renderer; no JIT is required.

This repository contains source and build tools. Game discs, extracted game files, translated game-code output, signing credentials and music are not included. Supply your own disc. The icon artwork is the supplied game cover; game names/artwork belong to their respective owners. This project is not affiliated with EA or Microsoft.

Display and frame pacing:

• Fullscreen landscape presentation on iPhone and iPad, with an optional aspect-fit mode. The macOS host also supports fullscreen and the F11 shortcut.

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned PAL build for iPhone and iPad. Sign the IPA with your preferred sideloading tool before installing. Supply your own matching European PAL Xbox disc; game files and music are not included. Other executable regions/revisions require matching translations.

Bundle ID: com.devz.nfsu2 · Version: 0.3, build 2.

Mobile experience:

• Fullscreen landscape play with optional aspect-fit presentation.
• Uncapped presentation by default; optional FPS ceiling through NFSU2_FPS_LIMIT.
• 4× internal width and height by default on iOS; adjustable render scale.
• Racing-style touch controls and a separate simple menu layout. Both layouts support independent positioning, size, opacity, visibility and button mappings, with Save, Cancel and Reset.
• Automatic PAL Menu/Drive switching, including pause/options/frontend detection. A manual toggle remains available.
• Physical controllers take over from the touch pad; disconnecting restores neutral touch input.
• MP3 import from Files, persistent playlist, playback switch, volume and Next Track. Lower the original soundtrack's Music volume in-game to hear only your playlist with game effects.
• Background suspension for the game, GPU work and audio.

Import and distribution:

• Streaming Xbox ISO extraction with path/bounds checks, executable preflight, staged replacement and save preservation.
• PAL Europe and NTSC-U executable profiles. Each build contains one matching executable translation; region-neutral ISO extraction does not provide universal regional playback.
• Active extracted directory and compiled profile shown under Edit → Game files. Default directory: Files → On My iPhone/iPad → NFSU2 → game.
• New game-cover icon, display name NFSU2, bundle ID com.devz.nfsu2, version 0.3, build 2.
• Public unsigned PAL IPA and SHA-256 checksum in dist/; sign for your own device before installation.
• Public source cleaned of local developer notes and compiled test binaries. Game files, generated game code, music and signing material remain excluded from source.

Performance:

• Cache Metal uniform, constant-buffer, texture and sampler bindings within their valid encoder lifetime.
• Reuse unchanged transform-constant uploads within a command buffer; keep fresh allocations for changed constants and instanced draws.
• Combine matching feedback-stage snapshots into one copy per draw.
• Use render-pass clears for complete surface clears while preserving partial and active-pass behavior.
• Native PAL CRT/video conversion fast paths and Apple generated-code optimization.
• Add asynchronous GPU timing diagnostics without waiting for GPU completion.

Validation and limitations:

• Seven input/pacing tests passed, alongside UIKit layout/customization/lifecycle/import tests, MP3 playback tests, XISO checks and Metal GPU regression checks at native and 4× scale.
• Installed and launched on an iPhone 16 Pro Max. All 191 transferred disc files matched source sizes and SHA-1 checksums on-device.
• Synthetic constant-upload benchmarks reduced CPU submission time by about 7–9% for that workload; this is not a measured gameplay FPS gain.
• Real race/pause automatic transitions and sustained gameplay performance still need device validation. Arbitrary regions and executable revisions require their own verified translation.

apps.subtitle: A full-featured, privacy-respecting music player for iOS, watchOS, and tvOS — stream from
apps.localizedDescription:

In-app help:

The app includes a full Help & Feature Guide (Settings → Help) covering every feature above in detail, with usage tips for each.

READ IT!!!

versions.localizedDescription:
Lumisound iOS v1.9.0.90:

Installation: Download the IPA and install with Sideloadly or AltStore.

AltStore users: Add the source URL from Settings → Streaming to get automatic updates.

Fixed:

• Audio flickering during normal playback and track switches (not seeking, which was already fixed). The shared ReplayGain volume stage could snap instantly at an unpredictable moment — either a second or more after a track had already started (while its loudness was still being analyzed in the background), or right as a crossfade/gapless transition began while that same shared stage was still audibly in use by the outgoing track. Both now ramp smoothly instead of snapping.
• Folders grid scrolling well below 60fps, plus device heat during ordinary browsing. Found via a field screen recording: every visible folder tile was paying for two real backdrop-blur effects, a shadow that forced an extra offscreen render pass, and a loading-shimmer animation that ran uncapped at 60fps with no way to pause — up to 100+ instances at once during a fast scroll through a library with many still-loading thumbnails. All four trimmed; a slow-to-reveal custom folder cover's disk read also moved off the main thread, which was contributing to the scroll "holding, then jumping" pattern specifically.
• Main-thread stalls during ordinary browsing, correlated with the device reporting "serious"/"fair" thermal state rather than "nominal." Two library-scan steps (deduping new songs, checking the scan cache) were still running synchronously on the main thread — field telemetry showed 1.3–1.6 seconds of blocking per occurrence, worse as the device heated up. Both moved off the main thread, matching the pattern already used everywhere else in the scan pipeline.

Behind the scenes:

Added an admin API endpoint for the app's existing structured event log (crash/hang diagnostics, main-thread-stall reports with full context) — this is what actually made the thermal/stall correlation above visible and fixable, rather than guesswork.

privacy.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: Lumisound checks your connected Bluetooth accessory's battery level so it can warn you before it dies.
privacy.NSFaceIDUsageDescription: Lumisound can use Face ID to lock the app, since it syncs your playlists and listening history to your account.
privacy.NSHealthShareUsageDescription: Lumisound reads your headphone audio exposure to help you spot loud listening habits, and your sleep data (if you use the Adaptive Sleep Timer) to learn roughly when you fall asleep.
privacy.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Lumisound records a short hum to find a matching song already in your library.
privacy.NSMotionUsageDescription: Lumisound uses head tracking to anchor Spatial Audio in place as you turn your head, and step counting (Workout Mode) to match playback speed to your pace.

apps.name: SymbiosSettings
apps.subtitle: iOS app (SwiftUI + CoreBluetooth) to read and change Halcyon Symbios dive computer settings over BLE — reverse-engineered
apps.localizedDescription:
Symbios Settings — iOS app:

An independent iOS app (SwiftUI + CoreBluetooth) to read and change the settings of the Halcyon Symbios dive computer, based on the reverse-engineered BLE protocol.

⚠️ Reverse-engineered (no official spec). Most settings have been verified on-device, and every write is read back for confirmation. Still — this is a dive computer: always confirm changed settings on the device itself before diving.

Features:

• Connect over BLE, read device info (serial, firmware, battery, pressure).
• Read and display all anchored settings, grouped (Dive profile · CCR/FSP · Timeouts & alarms · Displays · Computer settings).
• Change settings via a safe read-modify-write (fetch fresh → patch one byte → SET_SETTINGS → verify with a re-read).

versions.localizedDescription: Fixes dive numbering after merging: a session now counts as a single dive, so the dives after it renumber automatically instead of leaving a gap.

privacy.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: Verbindung zum Halcyon Symbios Tauchcomputer zum Lesen und Ändern der Einstellungen.

apps.localizedDescription:
Musonic:

Self-hosted music, beautifully played.

A music app for Navidrome and any Subsonic-compatible server, on Android and iOS (a web client is on the way). Your library, on your hardware, with an app that feels like it belongs on your phone.

Why Musonic:

• Free and open source, no account, no ads, no tracking.
• Your server only: Musonic plays what Navidrome serves; nothing is uploaded anywhere.
• More than your library: recommendations and, with OctoFiesta, the online catalogue, side by side with your own music.
• One ecosystem: the mobile app today, a web client and more tools to come, all in this repository.

A new design:

• Full-screen player with a softly blurred cover background, a quality badge (FLAC, MP3 320…) and drag-to-close.

versions.localizedDescription:
Android Auto (beta) and a security fix. Musonic now shows up in Android Auto, the server credentials no longer reach other apps, and two small player touches.

Security:

• Credentials no longer reach other apps — the cover of the playing track was published to the system media session (notification, lock screen) as a server address carrying the account username and password. Apps allowed to read the playing media (notification access, smartwatch companions, Android Auto) could read it. The player now only gets an address internal to Musonic, which reads the cover itself. Changing your Navidrome password after updating is advised.

Added:

• Swipe the full player's cover — left for the next track, right for the previous one, like the mini player. Dragging the player down to close it still works.

Fixed:

• Mini player tint — on very colourful covers, the blurred cover behind the mini player stopped in a hard vertical line next to the play button; it now fades out smoothly.

Android Auto only lists apps installed from the Play Store. Musonic is installed from GitHub, so it stays hidden until you allow it once:

• On the phone, open the Android Auto settings and tap Version ten times, then accept developer mode.
• Menu ⋮ → Developer settings → Unknown sources: turn it on.
• Open Musonic once on the phone, then connect to the car.

GrapheneOS: also open Settings → Apps → Sandboxed Google Play → Android Auto and grant the permissions it asks for, otherwise Android Auto stops as soon as the car connects.

Download: Musonic.apk below (Android 7+). iPhone: Musonic.ipa, to sideload with AltStore or Sideloadly (no CarPlay yet).

apps.localizedDescription:
白 Shirox:

Your anime and manga library, entirely yours.

A free, source-available library manager for iPhone, iPad and Mac. Track what you watch and read, keep it in sync with AniList and MyAnimeList, and play it from the sources you connect.

What it is:

Shirox ships with no content of its own. It's a native SwiftUI shell around three things you bring: your tracker account (AniList or MyAnimeList), your sources (modules, a Jellyfin server, or files on your device), and your library. Everything else — progress, downloads, playback, reading — happens on your device.

Shirox does not host, provide or endorse any content.

Tracking:

• AniList and MyAnimeList side by side, with per-provider toggles for what gets written where.

• Continue Watching and Continue Reading pick up mid-episode and mid-chapter.

versions.localizedDescription:
Extensions: besides Sora modules and Seanime providers, Modules now takes Stremio addons and Nuvio, Vega and SkyStream repos. Paste an addon's link to add it, or a repo's link to pick its providers from a list, one at a time or all at once. Each works like any module: search, the anime page, the player, downloads, Continue Watching and backups, on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple TV, and updates from its repo. Stremio addons find shows through the addon itself, Kitsu or Cinemeta; Nuvio scrapers through TMDB. From an anime page the right show and the right part of a split season come first.

Safe for work only: adult addons and providers are never listed or installed, and are removed if their source later marks them adult; adult titles are left out of results. Torrent links are never played.

Streams: links that are dead, web pages or ZIP files are left out before you pick, so the list only has ones that play. When a provider's site is behind Cloudflare (AnimePahe from Nuvio, for one), its row says so and offers Verify Cloudflare, including on MyAnimeList pages.

Downloads: Shirox.ipa (iPhone, iPad), Shirox-macOS.dmg (Mac), Shirox-Catalyst.dmg (Mac, Catalyst build).

apps.localizedDescription:
VortX:

The Android APK is an early technical preview, not the finished app. VortX is Apple first: the Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac apps are the complete experience today. Android is just getting started, sharing the same native engine, and the preview exists so Android users can watch the port take shape and help steer it. Expect missing features, rough edges, and fast-moving builds. If you want the full VortX experience right now, use the Apple apps; if you try the Android preview, please report what you hit, because every report shapes the port.

versions.localizedDescription:
VortX 0.5.5: Lighter Sync, Hero Trailers and Your Next Episode:

Build 274. VortX 0.5.5 fixes repeated conversion of unchanged 0.4 account data and reduces unnecessary background polling while live sync is healthy. These changes address a source of lag, stutter and delayed taps across the Apple apps. Hero trailers start again, Mac and iPad series pages open on your episode, and watched episode cards dim evenly. All packages are built by the public release workflow.

Fixed:

• Repeated background conversion. 0.5.4's check for changed 0.4 account data could give a different answer for the same data because it rebuilt a preferences archive before fingerprinting it. This triggered unnecessary conversion and account uploads, including during playback. The check now fingerprints the original legacy fields consistently and ignores native fields rewritten by routine sync. Unchanged routine syncs skip conversion after it succeeds. Genuine legacy changes still convert, and separately linked Stremio profile accounts retain their periodic 30-minute refresh. Removing this repeated work also reduces competition with opening your account.
• Hero trailers never started on Home and title pages on iPhone, iPad and Mac, or on title pages on Apple TV. The clip waited for a step that never ran. It runs now.
• Mac and iPad open a series on your episode. A long season opened on episode 1. The episode grid now scrolls to the episode in progress, or the next one after the episode you last played.
• Watched episode cards are dimmer and clean. The whole card darkens and loses its colour evenly, instead of fading into a smeared double image.

Changed:

• Less background polling, with live updates retained. A newer-change notification over the live sync connection still triggers a pull immediately. While that connection is responding, the fallback check runs every five minutes instead of every 3 seconds. If it disconnects or goes silent for 75 seconds, frequent fallback checks resume.
• A bigger Home billboard on Mac, running down to just above Customize.

Android:

Android checks for missed changes every five minutes while its live sync connection is up, instead of every 3 seconds.

VortX is Apple first. The Android APK is still an early technical preview rather than the finished app, so expect missing features and rough edges.

Please test:

• Use the app for a few minutes after the first launch, then watch something and check menu, tap and player responsiveness. With unchanged legacy data, the diagnostics log should no longer repeatedly show legacy_conversion run reason=changed. A first conversion, genuine legacy edits or a linked-account refresh can still produce a conversion entry.
• Close and reopen the app: the splash screen should be shorter than on 0.5.4.
• Leave Home open: the featured billboard should play its trailer muted.
• On Mac or iPad, open a series you are partway through: the episode list should open on your episode.
• Check that watched episodes look dimmed and clean.

Android phone, tablet and TV. VortX-0.5.5-full-mpv-universal.apk includes VortX Player. VortX-0.5.5-play-media3-universal.apk is the Media3 variant. Each APK contains both the phone and the Android TV interface. Choose the variant you already use so it installs over your current version. The Play bundle is also attached for its distribution workflow.

The Apple and Android packages were built by the release workflow from the v0.5.5-rc.1 tag, the same commit as v0.5.5. SHA256SUMS-ci.txt lists a SHA-256 checksum for each Apple package so you can confirm your download is intact; check the Android packages with SHA256SUMS-android.txt and SIGNING_PROVENANCE.txt.

apps.localizedDescription:
Star Fox Enhanced:

A native C++/SDL3 port of UltraStarFox, with Original Star Fox and Star Fox EX experiences, high-frame-rate presentation, widescreen support, and optional visual enhancements using Codex AI (5.6 Sol, 6 Astra, 6 Sol).

THIS PROJECT WAS PORTED AND CODED BY AI/CODEX:

AI disclosure: This project is made with AI assistance, including OpenAI Codex and AI tools used for programming, testing, documentation and some visual assets.

This is an alpha release, not a cycle-accurate SNES emulator. A supported, unmodified retail ROM supplied by you is required. No retail ROM is included.

Get started:

• Launch the game. On desktop, place your supported .sfc/.smc ROM beside the executable, or set STARFOX_RETAIL_ROM to its path. Mobile apps provide a first-launch file picker.

versions.localizedDescription:
Star Fox Enhanced 0.0.8.7:

This update includes the changes since 0.0.8.6. Supply your own supported retail ROM; no ROM or private game data is included. Nintendo 3DS development remains paused, and no 3DS package is included.

New renderer and display options:

• Added CarltonCracker's MODERN — Experimental renderer on desktop Windows and Linux. It draws the scene through the shared VR rendering path, reducing dependence on the per-pixel Super FX rendering layers. It remains optional; Software, GPU and GPU FAST are retained.
• MODERN includes world-anchored ground, smoother background movement, native space horizons, 3D corridors for compatible artwork, and widescreen HUD and communications. Optional replacement model textures, portraits, HUD sprites and landscape textures can be loaded from a local textures directory.
• Added a texture-dump tool for preparing your own replacement artwork.

• Added a lightweight display-area guide to the pre-game menu and remembered desktop window dimensions.
• Opening HUD/touch layout customization from F1 options now edits the paused live game without restarting the stage. Apply and Cancel return to the same options session without carrying button presses into it.

Gameplay and audio fixes:

• Fixed sound-bank initialization when entering stages through Level Select.
• Restored stage-results counting, completion and bonus-credit sound feedback, with consistent timing across presentation frame rates.
• Fixed encounter music continuing through player death and preserved the replacement Player Down cue, including cockpit death paths.
• Native boss stop/fade commands now also stop or fade replacement MSU music. The fade follows source timing and is shared with VR rather than being a desktop-only effect.
• Fixed returning to the title after the ending, including restarting after the credits music has finished and preventing stale ending scroll state from leaking into subsequent screens and stages.
• Reduced Android playback buffering without changing simulation or audio cadence.

Rendering fixes:

• Improved alignment of banked native backgrounds and enhanced horizons across atlas wraps.
• Fixed enhanced-sky sampling that could select unrelated atlas sections, repeat panoramas within a wide view, or stretch the sky's upper edge.
• Improved distant planet continuation when looking downward, avoiding stretched photographic columns.
• Expanded death/revival red and white screen fills to cover widescreen and supersampled corners.
• Preserved ray-traced model shadows when enhanced ground replaces scenery, and corrected emissive-surface shadow handling.
• Restored runtime-selected sprite materials, including enemy fire trails.
• Ground-material overrides, including manually selected lava, no longer replace classified distant planets and starfields. Enhanced skies remain independently selectable.
• Stopped native star/planet colours from being extruded downward as solid floor blocks after an atlas wrap.
• Extended symmetric scanline-tunnel ceiling/floor diagonals into widescreen margins instead of stretching edge pixels into horizontal bars. The native 256-column view is preserved; incompatible decorated tunnels keep their existing rendering path.
• Improved CPU layer-compositing performance while preserving material and coverage information.
• Kept Metal ray-pipeline preparation off the macOS UI thread, with responsive loading feedback and cached preparation results.

Platform and packaging updates:

• Fixed PS5 display uncovering after preview-off and loading screens.
• Added complete Vita launcher/LiveArea artwork and improved VPK metadata and package validation.

• Updated application/package versions to 0.0.8.7, including increasing Android and Quest version codes and the Apple and Xbox package build versions.

Known limits:

apps.name: Neechan X
apps.subtitle: A native iOS client for the imageboards 2ch (2ch.org / 2ch.life) and 4chan, written in Swift 6 and SwiftUI for iOS 26, using Apple's Liquid Glass design system for the navigation layer
apps.localizedDescription:
Neechan:

A native iOS client for the imageboards 2ch (2ch.org / 2ch.life) and 4chan, written in Swift 6 and SwiftUI for iOS 26, using Apple's Liquid Glass design system for the navigation layer.

Unofficial and unaffiliated with either site.

What it does:

• Reading — boards as a catalog or page by page, in list, card or grid layout; threads with reply counts, quote popups, a replies window, in-thread search, and your place kept so a thread reopens where you left it. A post or a whole thread can be translated into your language on the device, and 2ch's likes and dislikes are shown and can be cast.

versions.localizedDescription:
The .ipa below is unsigned. There is no signing certificate in this repository and there should not be one, so it cannot be installed by tapping it: use AltStore, Sideloadly, or your own developer account.

Requires iOS 26 or newer, on iPhone or iPad. Installs as Neechan X (pro.neechan.app-dev) and updates 2.5.1, or 2.5.2 build 9, in place.

A post, or a whole thread, can be read in your own language, translated on the device. 2ch's likes and dislikes are shown and can be cast. The text in a picture can be selected and copied, and a picture can be looked up on Yandex, Google Lens, SauceNAO or iqdb. Files can be picked in the gallery grid and saved together, or every file in a thread saved at once. A clip plays slower or faster, steps one picture at a time while paused, and shows a picture of where the scrubber is while it is dragged. About links to the website, the privacy policy, the source and an address to write to.

A link in a post to a video or a picture opens in the app's own viewer, and a file on another host is no longer sent your 2ch session. Some MP4s that played in silence are heard, an AVI renamed to .mp4 plays, and a seek no longer stops a downloading clip with an error or freezes one at its end. A tap in the gallery grid opens the file you tapped, not the one below it. Music from another app stops only while a clip is heard, and carries on when the clip is paused, muted or closed.

Posting to 4chan goes out the way the site's own reply form sends it, from a browser view inside the app. Its new captcha, a few steps of pictures to slide through, is drawn by the app, and the waits between captchas are the ones the site sends.

Threads:

• Likes and dislikes on 2ch. The boards that count them, such as /news/, show each post's likes and dislikes under it, and a tap casts yours. It counts at once, and comes back off with the site's reason if the site refuses it. A vote is writing to the site, so it follows the same switch as posting: where posting is off, the counts are shown and cannot be tapped. The app had the request for this but never made it, and the answer it expected was not the one the site gives, so a vote that counted would have been reported as a failure.

Posting:

• 4chan posts go through the browser engine. 4chan's posting host refused the app's own requests, even with the cookies a web view had earned, so the reply form never got past the browser check. The captcha and the post now go out from a hidden web view on the board's own page, the way 4chan's quick reply sends them. When Cloudflare wants to check the browser first, its check appears inside the captcha box and is answered there.
• 4chan's new captcha. Press Get Captcha, then on each step move the slider until the picture matches what the instructions ask for, and press Next. The instructions show with the picture they ask about, as on the site, and a short note under the captcha says how it works. The slider starts on the instructions, and nothing is picked for you.
• The site's own waits. Get Captcha counts down whatever wait 4chan sends with each captcha, 30 seconds, a minute or five, and "You have to wait a while before doing this again" shows with it rather than as a bare error. A longer wait shows the site's own message. Its link to verify your email, and the one under the captcha, open in the app, so what the page sets counts for the captcha. A captcha is asked for only when you press for it, since each one starts the wait, and closing the form keeps the wait and a captcha you had started.
• A post that may have gone through says so. When a post leaves and no answer comes back, the form says it may have been posted rather than that it failed, so it is not sent twice.

Links:

• A link to a file opens in the viewer. A link straight to a video or a picture, such as 2ch.su/test/src/237957/17847495108690174855.mp4, opened a Safari sheet. Only boards and threads were recognised, and a file is neither. A link to an mp4, webm, mov, mkv, jpg, png, gif, webp or bmp now opens in the viewer, the way a file attached to a post does. This works in the thread, in a quote and in the replies window, and Go to post and Save treat it as part of the post that links to it. A file on any 2ch mirror (2ch.su, 2ch.hk, 2ch.pm, 2ch.life) is fetched from the mirror you have chosen, so a link to a mirror that has gone dark still plays. A file on another host plays from that host. Until you turn on Adult 18+, a file on a board for adults, or on a host other than the imageboard's, still opens in Safari, the same rule the in-app browser follows.

Gallery:

• Text in a picture can be selected. A picture with words in it, a screenshot of a post most often, gets a Live Text button beside Save and Share. Tapped, the words are lifted out of the picture and can be selected, copied, translated or looked up, and a code or a thing Visual Look Up knows can be opened. The long press and the drag that closes the viewer are left to the text while it is lifted out, and come back when it is put away. The button appears only where something was found.
• Look a picture up. Search for this image, in a file's long-press menu in the viewer, the grid and the feed, sends the picture's address to Yandex, Google Lens, SauceNAO or iqdb. A video is looked up by its thumbnail. The page opens in the app's browser or in Safari by the same rule as any other link, and a file from a thread saved on the device is not offered, since no engine can reach it there.
• Save many files at once. Select, in the gallery grid, lets you tick files and save them together, with Select all for whatever the filter is showing. Save all files, in the thread's menu, saves every file in the thread after asking. The capsule counts them, "Saving 3 of 42", one failure does not stop the rest, and the alert at the end says how many did not make it. A save pressed while another was still running used to be dropped without a word; it now waits its turn.
• Cancel stops a conversion. Cancelling a save while a WebM was being turned into an MP4 took the capsule away and left the conversion running to the end of the clip.
• A file on another host is not sent your session. The player sent your 2ch cookies, including a passcode's, with every file it fetched, whatever host the file was on. In a 4chan thread they went to 4chan's file host. Only a file on the mirror you have chosen is sent them now.
• A tap in the grid opens the file you tapped. Tapping a video could open the picture below it. A thumbnail is cropped to its square, but the cropped part still took taps, and later cells lie on top: a tall screenshot took the lower half of the cell above it, and a wide picture the edge of the cell to its left. Each thumbnail now answers only inside its own square, in the grid, in a thread, on a board and in the attachments of a new post.

Media:

• Playback speed. The 1× under the viewer's scrubber picks a speed from half to double. Voices keep their pitch. The speed holds as you page from clip to clip, and the next viewer opens at normal speed. The feed is not affected.
• One picture at a time. While a clip is paused, two buttons beside the speed step one picture back or forward, and holding one keeps stepping. A step from the end of a clip leaves it paused where it is.
• A picture of where the scrubber is. Dragging the scrubber shows the picture at that point, from the keyframe at or before it, with the time under it. It is made only from what is already on the device, so it never competes with the clip for the connection; where the clip has not arrived, the post's own thumbnail stands in.
• A seek while paused shows where it landed. The clock was left at the time asked for, which is nearly always a little before the picture there, and the old picture stayed on screen until the clip was played.
• A seek is not answered with a picture from before it. A piece of the file read just as a seek began was taken for the first piece of the new position. The picture after the seek could be one from where the clip had been, and what came after it was decoded from the start of the clip.
• Music from another app stops only while a clip is heard. Opening a video stopped Spotify, Music or a podcast even when the clip was muted or had no sound at all, and it stayed stopped until the gallery or the feed closed. It now stops only while a clip plays out loud, and carries on when the clip is paused, muted, finished or closed, or when the app goes to the background. After a pause it waits a second, so a swipe in the feed does not start and stop it. The feed starts muted, so music keeps playing until you turn the feed's sound on. A video in another app's picture-in-picture window stops the same way, but usually waits for a tap to carry on. A call, or music started from Control Centre, pauses a clip that was playing out loud. Before, the clip carried on with no sound.
• Sound plays in an MP4 whose AAC only says it is stereo once it starts. HE-AAC v2 often declares just its core in the file's header, 22.05 kHz mono, and turns out to be 44.1 kHz stereo when the first packet is decoded. The player built everything from the header, refused every bit of sound that came out, and said nothing: the picture played and the clip was silent. What is played is now shaped by the first decoded sound, and a refusal is written to the log. Two of the four HE-AAC v2 clips in one /test/ thread were like this.
• An AVI named .mp4 plays. A board checks a file's name, not its bytes, so an old XviD rip renamed to .mp4 is posted and served as an MP4. The app's FFmpeg could not read AVI or decode MPEG-4 Part 2 and the clip failed to open. neechan-ffmpeg 9.0.4, the same FFmpeg n9.0.2, adds both; the file is recognised by its bytes whatever it is called, and its 5.1 AC-3 sound comes out as stereo. Its last picture carries no time of its own and is now shown after the one before it; untimed, the clip never reached its end and the timeline counted on.

• A seek past the last picture finishes the clip instead of freezing it. Dragging to the very end of any clip, or seeking into the missing part of a cut-off upload, found no picture at or after the target, and the player waited for one for as long as anyone watched. The last picture there is is shown and the clip is over. A cut-off file keeps an index for the whole of what it once was -- one in /test/ declares fifty seconds and holds thirteen -- so a seek it sends off the end goes back to the last keyframe read instead.

apps.localizedDescription:
PeonPad does not include Warcraft II. To play, you provide data extracted from your own legally owned copy on a Mac or PC. That game content stays local to your machine and is never part of the PeonPad download.

AI disclosure: PeonPad uses substantial AI assistance for code, tests, documentation, debugging and maintenance. Some support replies and maintenance tasks are automated. There is no audited percentage of AI-generated code. Build, test and device records describe what was checked. This disclosure concerns PeonPad's workflow, not the authorship of its upstream projects.

What is PeonPad?:

PeonPad is an independent Apple-platform Warcraft II port built on the open-source Stratagus engine and Wargus game layer. It runs engine code directly on iPadOS; it does not run a Windows executable, emulate x86, or stream a game from another computer.

versions.localizedDescription:
PeonPad 0.1.0 Preview 1 is the first public unsigned IPA build.

Important:

• The IPA is unsigned. It must be signed with your own Apple account or a sideloading service you trust before installation.
• The IPA contains no Warcraft II data, Aleona data, installer, MPQ, save, provisioning profile, or signing credential.
• You must own Warcraft II and separately extract a complete data.Wargus folder on a computer.
• After installing, copy that folder to On My iPad > PeonPad > data.Wargus through Files or Finder, then relaunch PeonPad.
• iPadOS 16 or later is required.

What changed:

• Added a data-free iOS distribution build, strict app audit, and deterministic IPA packager.

• Kept embedded game data behind an explicit private-development build mode.

Validation:

• The app and IPA audits rejected prohibited game/private/signing content and local build paths.
• Two independently packaged clean-clone IPAs were byte-identical.
• A physical M2 iPad Pro passed in-place install, missing-data messaging, byte-verified user-data transfer, title/menu launch, and preference-value preservation.

These are accepted, documented behaviours, not regressions in this build:

• Sustained heavy load lowers 117HD resolution. Under thermal pressure the 117HD renderer steps its scene-resolution scale down and restores it on cooldown — by design, to keep the frame rate up.
• JIT attach (iOS only). iOS requires re-attaching the debugger (StikDebug) per launch to enable JIT. That is an OS constraint, not a bug.

apps.name: OwLens
apps.subtitle: 🦉 OwLens is a professional-grade iOS cinema camera app designed for filmmakers and creators who demand uncompromising image fidelity and true control over video capture
apps.localizedDescription:
OwLens:

🦉 OwLens is a professional-grade iOS cinema camera app designed for filmmakers and creators who demand uncompromising image fidelity and true control over video capture. It bypasses Apple's standard image signal processor (ISP), capturing uncompressed 14-bit RAW Bayer sensor data at full sensor resolution ($4032 \times 3024$, 12.2 MP) and encoding it directly into 10-bit HEVC Log in real time.

Key Highlights & Architecture:

• True 14-Bit Bayer RAW Capture: Bypasses Apple's ISP noise reduction, computational edge sharpening, and adaptive tone mapping. Preserves 100% of native sensor photons directly from camera hardware.
• Zero Decimation / Full Megapixels: Full $4032 \times 3024$ native Bayer data is maintained throughout capture and debayering without spatial pixel binning or CFA decimation for 4K video recording.
• Ultra-Fast Metal Compute Pipeline:.

versions.localizedDescription:
🎬 Perfect A/V Lip-Sync & Strict 24.000 CFR Cinema Timeline:

• Time-Quantized Constant Frame Rate (CFR): Frame timestamps are mathematically locked to the 24.000 FPS grid based on hardware optical capture time. Missing or delayed frames no longer cause video to drift behind audio.
• Hold-Frame Slot Filling: Any missed CFR slots under load are automatically populated with the previous frame (up to 4 frames max), ensuring the output container remains 100.000% pure 24.000 CFR without VFR jitter in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.
• Microsecond A/V Synchronization: Audio presentation timestamps are anchored to optical exposure start, and monotonic buffer advance eliminates audio packet overlap across long recordings (zero drift on 5+ minute takes).
• Zero Tail Freeze: Container termination (writer.endSession(atSourceTime: videoEndTime)) cleanly cuts audio and metadata tracks exactly at the final video frame boundary.

⚡ Zero-Stall Capture Pipelining & Frame Preservation:

• Decoupled DMA Blit Queue: Bayer frame copy now runs on a private, dedicated Metal blit queue completely decoupled from the compute pipeline. Eliminates thread stalling on AVFoundation photo delivery.
• Optimized Prepared Settings: Initial prepared photo settings expanded to 24, with throttled replenishment checking every 16 frames to eliminate mediaserverd IPC overhead and burst stalls.
• Expanded Buffer Cushions: bayerBufferPool minimum count and RawFrameBuffer capacity expanded to 32 frames (1.33s buffer cushion) to absorb transient disk I/O and thermal transitions.
• Hardened Sequencer Watchdog: Out-of-order frame delivery and timeout recovery hardened to discard stale frames and prevent orphaned keys from stalling the sequencer.

🌟 Maximum Dynamic Range & Highlight Roll-off:

• Log Headroom Shoulder: Mapped linear sensor input [0, 1] through LogCurve.defaultRMax to unlock full scene reflectance headroom in S-Log3 and Apple Log 2 without highlight clipping.
• Active Defect Pixel Correction (DPC): Adaptive 4-element median filter cleans hot/stuck pixels during recording for pristine master files.
• Hardware ProRes Detection: Dynamic runtime probing for Apple ProRes hardware encoder capability (available on A15 Bionic and newer / iPhone 13 Pro+), with informative UI guidance on unsupported hardware.

📦 Sideloading:

Download OwLens.ipa attached below and install via Sideloadly, AltStore, or TrollStore.
