apps.localizedDescription:
A health app for your wearables. No subscription, no fees, private by default.

As featured in Hackaday and Adafruit.

Devices:

Supported: WHOOP 4.0, 5.0, MG.

Being built: Oura Ring, Garmin, Pebble, Colmi, Ultrahuman, Mi Band and more.

Support:

OpenStrap has no company, no subscription and no paywall behind it. If it's useful to you, a tip helps keep it going.

Bitcoin.

EVM (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon).

Guides:

• Development: build and run from source.
• iOS installation.
• iOS sideload.
• iOS Shortcuts.
• Apple Watch setup.
• AI coach.
• Tasker integration.
• Buzz meanings.
• Writing a device adapter.

Disclaimer:

OpenStrap is independent and not affiliated with or endorsed by WHOOP, Oura, Garmin or any device maker. Product names are trademarks of their owners and are used only to describe compatibility.

versions.localizedDescription:
New look:

• Four tabs: Today, Sleep, Activity, Health.
• One name per score, and every trend tells you how today compares with your usual range.
• Heart-rate zones are labelled rows with their bpm ranges.
• Profile opens from your avatar on every tab. Detailed charts moved to an Advanced screen.

Report an issue:

• Your health database is included only if you switch it on. "Share locally" builds the same file and lets you share it yourself; nothing is uploaded.
• You can delete a ticket any time from My reports. Reports are deleted automatically after 30 days (14 if they include your database).

Scores:

• Recovery is calibrated to your own normal range and combines HRV with resting heart rate.
• Every screen shows the same recovery number, and it's only locked in after a full night.
• When recovery isn't scored, the app tells you why.
• Nightly HRV is more accurate, and the HRV sent to Apple Health now matches what Apple Watch reports.
• Strain is measured against your own resting level.
• A day's strain is never lower than a workout on that day, and days with no detected sleep still get a strain.
• Naps and broken sleeps under 3 hours no longer push resting heart rate up.
• WHOOP 5: nightly skin temperature compared with your usual, in °C.

Your data, more of it:

• History from older WHOOP 4 firmware that was stored but never read now gets decoded, so some people get missing days back.
• New users see "Recovery starts in N nights" while their baseline builds, with resting HR, steps and sleep from night one.

New:

• Nutrition: search past foods, meal times, edit entries, today's protein.
• Heart rate: zoomable day chart and minute-by-minute export.
• Imported workouts are scored with your band's heart rate.
• Activity review, a better weightlifting exercise picker, and padel, skateboarding and push-ups.
• Alarms: next alarm on Home, a note when it fired, more reliable on WHOOP 5.
• 12/24-hour clock setting.
• Android: back up to a folder you choose.
• iOS: Shortcuts to sync the band and get today's numbers, background sync on iOS 27, and a warning that deleting the app unpairs your bands.
• Steps: wearing-location setting, and the app shows when the band counted the steps.
• WHOOP 5 battery pack charge.
• Blood oxygen imported from WHOOP data in Health.
• AI Coach works with OpenAI tool calling; Tailscale addresses count as local.
• Russian translation and improved German.
• Other wearables (Beta, off by default): Oura, Garmin, Pebble, Colmi, Ultrahuman and Mi Band can pair. Turn on "Use this device for scores" on the device page to try them.

Fixes:

• Sync button works again; fewer drops and hangs during sync.
• Sleep corrections now stick, and the app checks the saved night matches your edit.
• Fewer wrong sleep guesses from heart rate alone, and naps no longer double-counted on old days.
• Sleep: nights end at the right time, edits across midnight and daylight-saving changes stick, and last night waits until the band has synced past your wake.
• Health: no duplicates or accidental wipes, heart rate keeps reaching Apple Health, Health Connect workouts work both ways.
• Illness and temperature alerts use the newest night, with honest wording.
• WHOOP 4 nights where skin temperature just follows the room no longer trigger illness alerts.
• One "band charging" card a day, and old workout suggestions clear after 7 days.
• Android back button moves between tabs again.
• iPhone now keeps a sync log, so problem reports include what the app was doing.
• Dozens of smaller fixes to dates, daylight saving, water, workouts and notifications.

OpenStrap Edge is now licensed under AGPL-3.0.

• chore(ios): extension versions 0.10.3 (72) to match pubspec.

• fix(ios): write the sync log on iPhone; confirm ticket ID copy.

• Study fixes: recover archived v12 data, first-weeks countdown, corrections that stick, scoring and noise fixes (v113).

privacy.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: OpenStrap connects to your WHOOP band over Bluetooth to sync your health data.
privacy.NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription: OpenStrap connects to your WHOOP band over Bluetooth to sync your health data.
privacy.NSCameraUsageDescription: OpenStrap uses the camera to read the barcode on a food packet, so logging a meal does not mean typing its nutrition panel out by hand. It reads the barcode digits and nothing else — no photo is taken, kept, or sent anywhere.
privacy.NSHealthShareUsageDescription: OpenStrap reads your height, weight, date of birth and sex to set up your profile; your resting heart rate so it has a starting baseline; any blood pressure, blood glucose or body temperature readings, so a device that is cleared to measure those can sit beside your own data with that device's name on it — never blended into an OpenStrap number; and your workouts and their routes, so a run recorded by another app can be listed and drawn on a map here, named with the app that recorded it and never counted as one OpenStrap measured. It also reads back its own recent samples so it never writes duplicates.
privacy.NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription: OpenStrap writes your sleep, resting heart rate, HRV, respiratory rate, energy and workouts into Apple Health.
privacy.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: OpenStrap never needs always-on location and does not ask for it. It records your route only while a run, ride or walk is actively running — including when your screen is locked — and stops as soon as you finish. Your route stays on this device and is never uploaded.
privacy.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: OpenStrap records your route during a run, ride or walk so you can see it, colored by heart-rate zone, when the workout ends. Recording continues while your screen is locked or you switch apps, but only while a workout is running — it stops the moment you finish. Your route stays on this device and is never uploaded.
privacy.NSMotionUsageDescription: OpenStrap counts your daily steps from this iPhone's own motion chip, because a band on your wrist cannot tell walking from stirring a pot, and the phone in your pocket can. It reads step counts only — never your location or anything else the motion chip records — and only the last few days of them. Your steps stay on this device and are never uploaded.
privacy.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: OpenStrap does not access your photo library. This permission is linked by a dependency but unused — importing your own exported WHOOP data uses the Files app, not Photos.

apps.subtitle: Play Banjo-Kazooie on your iPhone and Apple Vision Pro — the full adventure with the
apps.localizedDescription:
Lighthouse for iPhone & Apple Vision Pro:

Play Banjo-Kazooie on your iPhone and Apple Vision Pro — the full adventure with the Lighthouse enhancements menu, the randomizer, online co-op, game controllers and a tunable touch layout, and on Vision Pro a stereoscopic 3D mode that puts Spiral Mountain on a world-locked panel floating in your room with real depth.

Built on Lighthouse (Harbour Masters' native Banjo-Kazooie port) and libultraship, rendering natively on Metal — no translation layer. 100% vibe coded with lots of passion and attention to detail.

Banjo-Kazooie on Apple Vision Pro — a freely resizable window floating in your room, rendering at true 4K, with the on-screen touch layout. The same build also runs in stereoscopic 3D.

versions.localizedDescription:
A fix for the repeating "Outdated ROM Archives" popup, smoother game timing and touch controls, and an iOS 27 rebuild.

If you are upgrading from 1.0.x.

• "Outdated ROM Archives" popup fixed: archives made by 1.0.x showed this popup at every launch, and pressing OK went straight into the game without re-extracting anything. You will now see the popup once: confirm the prompts and the app re-extracts bk.o2r from the ROM in your Lighthouse folder (about half a minute), then later launches are silent. Your old archive is set aside and only removed once the new one checks out. If your ROM is no longer in the Lighthouse folder, the file picker opens so you can choose it again. Saves are untouched. Archives already made by 1.1.0 are current and launch without the popup.

iPhone & iPad.

• Game keeps real time: when a frame runs late, the game now skips an in-between frame instead of slowing down, so movement and music no longer drift into slow motion.
• Lighter touch controls: the on-screen stick no longer redraws the whole overlay as you move it, cutting the per-frame work the touch layer costs.
• Launch-crash fix: if your settings had the renderer set to OpenGL (which this app does not include), the game crashed at launch. It now falls back to Metal and repairs the setting by itself.
• Built with the iOS 27 SDK: launches correctly on iOS 27 and stays landscape, including after returning from Home or Control Center.

Apple Vision Pro.

• The archive-popup fix, the launch-crash fix, the real-time timing (2D mode) and the lighter touch overlay apply here too. Verified on the visionOS simulator; this build was not tested in the headset, and the 3D mode is unchanged from 1.1.0.

This public build does not include the developer console.

Built on Lighthouse 1.1.0 "Hatteras Alfa". Bring your own Banjo-Kazooie ROM (.z64, US v1.0, US v1.1, Japan or PAL); the app extracts it on device and ships no game content.

Or install the IPA below manually through SideStore/AltStore (iPhone can also use Sideloadly).

Requirements:

• iPhone on iOS 15+, or Apple Vision Pro (visionOS 2+).

apps.name: S5LBox
apps.subtitle: Classic iPhone OS
apps.localizedDescription:
S5LBox:

Classic iPhone OS. On your iPhone.

Slide to unlock. Open an old favorite. Make it yours again.

S5LBox brings the iPhone 3G and its original iPhone OS 3.1.3 to your iPhone. It's the real operating system, running inside an app—not a theme or a recreation. Your iPhone doesn't need to be jailbroken.

What you can do:

• Rediscover the classics. Explore the familiar Home screen, built-in apps, and compatible apps from the early days of iPhone.

• Bring your apps. Import .ipa files directly or put them in S5LBox's IPAs folder in Files. Choose what to install, one app at a time, without closing the running machine.

versions.localizedDescription:
Classic iPhone OS. On your iPhone.

The first public release of S5LBox: the iPhone 3G's iPhone OS 3.1.3 running inside an iOS app. This release is experimental; compatibility and performance are still being improved.

Firmware and first-run setup:

• Native first-run setup with progress, cancellation, errors and retry paths.

• Import an existing IPSW as an alternative. Selection is handled immediately, without reopening Settings or choosing the file a second time.
• Keep firmware details and manual overrides in Advanced settings. Skip setup once firmware is configured. No Apple firmware is bundled.

Machines, storage and controls:

• Create multiple independent machines, with long-press actions to rename, duplicate or delete them.
• Save and resume running sessions, or shut down for a fresh boot. Keep machine files accessible through the Files app.
• Use an 8 GiB virtual disk for new machines by default, with 2 and 4 GiB alternatives under Advanced. Sparse storage avoids allocating the full capacity immediately; guest data and saved sessions still use real storage.
• Modern emulator toolbar and a separate device-controls sheet for Home, sleep/wake, silent mode, volume, pause, restart and Save & close.
• Separate app settings from running-machine settings; keep the legacy interface available in Advanced.
• Pause in the background by default. Provide Force Power Off for guests that cannot complete an ordinary shutdown, including during boot.
• Use guest shutdown confirmation before restarting a running machine. Forced power-off remains an unclean stop and can lose unsaved work.

Guest apps and jailbreak:

• A Files-visible IPAs folder and in-app import, with individual app selection and real IPA icons, including supported legacy optimized PNG artwork.
• Install apps while the guest is running through virtual USB, pairing, AFC and the guest's installation_proxy service—not by editing its live disk.
• Installation progress, cancellation, guest verification errors and per-machine pairing identities.
• Guided guest jailbreak with Cydia, centered preparation progress and automatic entry into the machine afterward.
• First-boot setup performs a respring. The completion notice explains that Cydia may appear afterward and Packages may need a guest reboot.
• Packages helper setup is included with jailbreak by default, with an Advanced opt-out and a setup path for existing jailbroken machines.

Built-in Packages:

• Native package browsing, categories, search, sources, installed packages and available updates.

• Install, update and remove packages using the running guest's own dpkg and maintainer scripts. Unsupported dependency plans are refused rather than silently applied.
• Handle supported package finish requests for respring or reboot after changes, with progress and connection-recovery feedback.
• First-use helper setup and first-boot waiting are integrated into Packages; missing setup is not treated as a successful connection.

Emulation, networking and audio:

• ARMv6 guest execution with a no-JIT shipping path; no host jailbreak or JIT activation is required to run the emulator.
• Experimental MBX graphics enabled by default for new machines, with the existing software-rendering configuration retained for machines that use it.

• Experimental audio playback and microphone input, guest digital volume/mute, host audio-session handling and saved audio-device state.
• Microphone access enabled by default subject to iOS permission, with an Advanced opt-out. Declining permission does not block setup or boot.

Reliability fixes included in 1.0.0:

• Fix virtual USB reconnection after Save & close for both Packages and live IPA installation. Wake a sleeping guest for pending service work, and detect controller resets instead of mistaking cleared interrupts for a completed handshake.

• Improve jailbreak/helper first-boot recovery, stale filesystem metadata handling and protection of referenced disk blocks during supported stopped maintenance operations.

• Fix firmware picker/import state handling, setup progress presentation, retained setup state and the separation of everyday and Advanced controls.
• Include regression coverage for USB transport, installation, storage, firmware preparation, input, audio and package operations.

Compatibility and known limitations:

• Host requirement: an arm64 iOS device running iOS 13 or later. Physical-device validation has focused on iPhone 6s Plus with iOS 15.8.5; it does not establish identical behavior on every supported host version or device.

• Apps and tweaks must support this guest. Copy-protected IPAs cannot be installed; some otherwise compatible apps require AppSync inside the guest.
• Graphics, audio, input latency and performance remain experimental. Not all hardware, apps, tweaks, media formats or audio routes are supported, and original-device animation speed is not guaranteed.
• Packages is not a complete replacement for every Cydia/APT dependency plan. Unsupported plans may require Cydia. Guest scripts and initial jailbreak configuration can still take time; first boot may need a respring or reboot.
• Back up important machine data before experimenting. An interrupted installation can have an uncertain outcome; reconnecting does not undo it.

Apple firmware, machine disks and test-device data are not part of the release assets.

Opaline:

A lightweight, native YouTube client for iOS 12+. No ads, no tracking, no dependencies.

Opaline was released as YTLite until August. It was renamed to avoid confusion with an unrelated tweak of the same name and is not related to it.

Screenshots follow your GitHub theme — the app supports both light and dark mode.

Why:

When Google dropped support for the official YouTube app on older devices, there was no way to watch videos properly. Browsers capped quality at 360p — and even that barely ran. Opaline was born to restore what was lost: high-quality playback on hardware that still works fine, just ignored by Google — a focused, lightweight client that does one thing well.

apps.localizedDescription:
Onside TV:

A clean IPTV app for iPhone with a sports score center built in. It used to be called Nebulo, same app with a new name.

Check the scores, tap a game, and it finds the channel that's showing it on your own IPTV service.

Heads up: Onside TV doesn't come with any channels. You need your own subscription from an IPTV provider.

Sports:

• Live scores, schedules and standings for the NFL, college football, NBA, WNBA, college basketball, MLB, NHL, soccer from all over, F1, golf, tennis, MMA and more.
• Favorite your teams, leagues, drivers and golfers so their next game or live score shows up on the home screen.
• Team, league and driver pages with schedules, results, standings, rosters and stats.

versions.localizedDescription:
Nebulo is now Onside TV!:

Same app, new name, and the biggest update so far.

Read this before you install:

• You need iOS 26 or newer. If your phone is on an older version, stay on Nebulo V2.3 for now.
• Onside TV installs as a new app next to Nebulo. You'll have to log in again, and your favorites and settings from Nebulo won't carry over. Once you're set up you can delete Nebulo.
• There's just one IPA this time, no backup version.

What's New:

• New look: Liquid Glass all through the app, a new home screen with big channel cards and a full screen hero at the top.
• Way bigger sports section: Game cards with lineups, stats, momentum, shot maps, win probability and box scores, plus standings, team pages and schedules.
• Favorite teams: Follow your teams, leagues, drivers and golfers and see their next game or live score on the home screen.
• Live Activities: Follow the score from your Lock Screen and Dynamic Island.
• Smarter game search: Tap a game and the app checks your TV guide for both teams around the start time, then plays the right channel or shows you the best matches.
• New search: Live games, recently watched channels and your categories all in one place.
• Recordings: Stop, delete or jump to the live channel right from the recordings section, and recordings now show their own guide info.
• Connection warning: If your provider only gives you one connection, the app warns you before watching something else would cut off a recording.

Fixes:

• If your login is wrong the app now tells you, instead of dropping you on an empty home screen. The guide also loads right away the first time you log in.
• Streams don't keep playing sound anymore after you close them and lock your phone.
• Smoother scrolling and less heat.
• Show pictures on the home screen only appear when they actually match the show.

Under the Hood:

• Update checks still come from GitHub, so you'll get a heads up in Settings when a new version is out.

Jailbroken:

Trying to use non-ellekit tweak runtimes will likely break functionality. Ideally always use the pre-patched ipa when sideloading.

• Either add the altsource to your on-device sideloading tool:.

Live reload (HMR):

When working on the JavaScript client you can have the app reload automatically whenever you rebuild the bundle, instead of relaunching by hand.

• Run the client's dev server (bun scripts/dev in the client repo). It serves the bundle and a Server-Sent Events stream at /__hot.
• In Unbound's settings, set:.

• loader.update.url to your dev server's bundle URL, e.g. http://:3000/unbound.bundle
• loader.update.hmr to true.

loader.update.hmr is off by default, so this never runs for normal users. The HMR endpoint is derived from loader.update.url's origin — no separate setting needed.

Solea is a player, just as a web browser is for web pages. It provides, sells and recommends no content and no subscription: it only plays the sources you add yourself, and you must have the right to watch them.

This repository hosts the releases of Solea (downloads and release notes). The source code is private.

Download:

• Windows – Solea--Setup.exe (installer) or Solea--windows.zip (portable).
• iPhone, iPad – with SideStore: see below.

iPhone and iPad with SideStore:

Solea installs on iPhone and iPad with SideStore, for free, with your own Apple Account. You need a computer once (about 10 minutes); after that, updates arrive on the iPhone. Step-by-step guide: solea.tv/en/install-iphone.

versions.localizedDescription:
Solea 1.0:

The first final version of Solea. It brings together everything from the test versions 0.9.1 to 0.9.7, plus a lot of work since: a new TV interface, Jellyfin, Trakt and Discord, a Sports space, much better casting, and a safer Solea account.

Update required for Solea accounts: your Solea account now only accepts version 1.0 or newer. Older versions ask you to update. On Android and Windows the update installs from the app; on iPhone and iPad, update with SideStore.

A new TV interface:

• New home screen: a large picture of the title you select, "Continue watching" right below, and doors to Live TV, Movies, Series, Anime and Sports.
• Search, Settings and your profile are round buttons at the top of the home screen.
• New search: channels, series and movies in rows, your recent searches, and movies listed before channels when their title starts with what you typed.
• Voice search listens inside Solea and types as you speak, with a mic that pulses with your voice. The remote's search or mic key opens it directly (boxes with a mic remote).
• Movies, Series and Anime in rows: New, your Trakt lists, Favorites, Top rated, then every category with "See all".
• Long-press OK anywhere for options: favorite, Trakt list, move, guide, replay, remove from "Continue watching".
• Settings in clear categories (Subscription, Solea account, Catalog, Services…), each with a short summary.
• Remote control: the PIN code pad can be used in full, and ▲ ▼ stay in the Settings page.
• Create or sign in to a Solea account from the TV shows the QR code screen: type on your phone instead of the remote.

Phones and computers:

• Redesigned movie and series pages on phones: Play right under the title, choices on one sliding line, expandable synopsis.
• Swipe right to leave a page, home carousel under your finger, a daily selection from the most popular titles, and the video goes under the camera notch in the player.
• Computers: the Play button responds again when the choices take two lines.

Player:

• Easier to read on bright pictures: darker shade behind the controls, and play / ±10 s on dark circles on phones.
• New Audio and subtitles panel: one line per track with clear labels (VO, forced, SDH, 5.1…), subtitles found online as an "Online" track, and an Appearance panel with a sample subtitle.
• Forced subtitles in the audio language turn on by themselves.
• On phones, a tap hides the controls without pausing.

Subtitles:

• More subtitles found online: when OpenSubtitles has nothing in your language or its daily limit is reached, Solea also looks on SubDL, SubSource and Addic7ed (series). The source is shown when they load.
• Subtitles made for your exact file are picked first when they exist.

• Sync in one press: press when you hear the first line and Solea shifts the whole file. Skip a line the author added, go back to the start, or fine-tune by 0.1 s. Your setting is remembered for that file, and it works while casting too, from the remote.

Live TV:

• Program guide in a grid: channels by hour, a small live preview of the selected channel, and live or replay in one press.
• Picture format per channel (whole picture, fill, 16:9, 4:3), remembered for each channel.
• Favorite channels in your own order: long-press OK, then Move. The order follows you to your other devices.
• Current program, end time and progress on each channel, taken from the full guide when needed.
• Smoother motion on Android TV boxes and Fire TV: the screen switches to 50 Hz for 25/50 fps channels (Settings › Playback).
• Frozen picture: Solea notices it even when the sound keeps going, reconnects, tries another format, then a lower quality, and explains when nothing works.

Subscriptions:

• Several subscriptions: keep several Xtream accounts or M3U playlists and switch between them without typing your details again. Each keeps its own catalog, and they follow you with your Solea account.
• Backup servers: up to 5 other addresses from your provider. If the main one stops responding, Solea switches on its own and comes back later.
• Options per subscription: a name, the User-Agent (only if your provider asks for one), and a backup program guide (XMLTV) for channels your provider's guide leaves empty.
• Backup to a file (Settings › Solea account): save your subscriptions, profiles, progress, favorites and settings, and restore them on any device. The file contains your passwords: keep it private.
• Your catalog is no longer emptied when the provider sends back an empty list.

Sports:

• A Sports space (turn it on in Settings › Catalog): matches and live events for the next days, taken from your sports channels' guide and grouped by event with the channels showing them. One press to watch.
• Live scores, team names and logos, filters by sport, a featured match, and rows for Now, Soon and each day.
• Replays are recognized as such, duplicates are merged, and pre-match and post-match shows go to Magazines.
• On computers and phones too.

Anime:

• Skip intro, recap and credits on more anime episodes, with a new source used when the usual ones have nothing.

Jellyfin:

• Add your Jellyfin server in Settings › Services: your movies, series and anime show up in their own rows, and Jellyfin versions appear on movie and series pages.
• Backup when your provider is busy: Solea tries your provider a few times, then plays the same title from your server.
• Casting from Jellyfin: the server prepares the video for the Chromecast, your phone relays nothing.
• Solea shows up with its real name in Jellyfin's dashboard, and episodes are recognized even when Jellyfin missed their number.

Trakt:

• Connect your Trakt account (Settings › Services) with a code on trakt.tv, or a button that opens the page with the code filled in on phones.
• What you finish is marked as watched, and your progress in each series is sent by itself.
• Your watchlist and personal lists in Movies and Series, and a Watchlist button on each page.
• No more random sign-outs.

Your services follow your account:

• Trakt, Jellyfin, OpenSubtitles and your TMDB key follow your Solea account: connect them once, and every device signed in to your account gets them. Disconnecting one in Settings removes it everywhere.

Casting:

• Solea's own Chromecast screen: Solea colours, loading and pause screens with the title, synopsis and time left, clear messages when a video can't be played.
• Next episode: a card with a countdown during the end credits, keeping your voices and subtitles. Skip intro and recap from the Solea remote, or automatically.
• Much faster: changing language or subtitles, or moving to another episode, takes a few seconds without restarting the TV app.
• Smoother playback when the sound is converted by your phone: one connection to your provider per title, conversion all the way to the end, and online subtitles that stay in sync after a pause.
• Sound: Dolby is sent as is when the TV or amplifier can play it; otherwise Solea converts it and picks a 1080p version in the same language. No more 4K HDR sent to a screen that can't show it.
• Subtitles from the file itself when it has them in your language, complete subtitles rather than forced ones for original versions, and your subtitle style from Settings.
• Live channels: logo, current and next program on screen, and Dolby sound converted so it plays.
• Android TVs with Solea installed open Solea itself, which plays the file as is.
• AirPlay from iPhone and iPad to an Apple TV or an AirPlay TV, and DLNA TVs get subtitles too.
• Pick the TV again to get the remote back after closing Solea. Only TVs show up as receivers.
• Next episode with your phone locked, on iPhone too.

Connect a TV from your phone:

• Scan the TV's QR code with your phone's camera: Solea opens and connects the TV in one tap, to your Solea account and your subscription, encrypted for the TV alone.
• Verification code: the TV and your phone show the same short code; only connect if they match.
• On iPhone, the solea.tv/pair page has an "Open in Solea" button; without Solea on the phone, the page works as before.

More devices:

• Small Android boxes and TVs always open in landscape, full screen, and no longer stay on a white screen at launch.
• Lighter Android app: about 38 MB instead of 90 MB, with a new decoder for DTS, TrueHD and Dolby sound.
• "Continue watching" on the Android TV home screen.
• Samsung TVs: a new app that opens on recent models.
• iPhone and iPad: install with SideStore, guide on solea.tv.

Updates:

• Updates from the app on Android now install properly. The remote shows which button is selected, and permission to install apps is asked first.
• Settings › About › Beta versions: also get test versions as updates, on this device only.

Your Solea account:

• Forgot your password? Change it from any device still signed in to your account: nothing is lost.
• Stronger protection: changing the password or deleting the account needs a device that holds your encryption key, unused sign-ins expire after 90 days, and too many wrong passwords only block the place they come from.
• Devices on the same network only accept each other: your progress, favorites and playback can't be read or controlled by other devices on your Wi-Fi.
• Jellyfin servers on the internet are reached over HTTPS.

Help:

• Short announcements can appear at the top of the home screen.

Downloads:

• Android box, Android TV, Fire TV, Android phones and tablets: Solea-1.0.0-android.apk.
• Windows: Solea-1.0.0-Setup.exe (installer) or Solea-1.0.0-windows.zip (portable).
• iPhone, iPad: with SideStore, see solea.tv/en/install-iphone.

apps.name: MeloNX
apps.subtitle: A Nintendo Switch Emulator based on Ryujinx for iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
We do not support piracy, It is forbidden to request copyrighted content.

Do I need a Switch to use this emulator?:

MeloNX emulator is capable of running many homebrew applications, and can be a crucial tool in the development and debugging of homebrew applications and games. To play commercial games, you will need access to a Switch compatible with custom firmware (CFW), which will enable you to dump your system firmware, keys and legally purchased games.

How can I dump my firmware/games/keys?:

First, you need to hack your Nintendo Switch, which you can learn how to do here: https://nh-server.github.io/switch-guide/.

Info:

• A Paid Developer account or TrollStore may be needed for specific devices (Read about Entitlements below).
• MeloNX REQUIRES JIT and CANNOT run without it.

apps.name: Sweet Lyrics
apps.subtitle: Word-by-word synced Spotify lyrics on iPhone, with Apple Music–style animations. Unofficial SwiftUI port of the Spicy Lyrics Spicetify extension
apps.localizedDescription:
Sweet Lyrics for iOS:

Word-by-word lyrics for whatever you're playing on Spotify, in an Apple Music style player on your iPhone or iPad.

It's an unofficial iOS version of Spicy Lyrics, the popular Spicetify extension for Spotify on desktop. Made by sppq (GitHub), tested by nie4ick.

Heads up: it works, but it's still early. You can use it every day, but expect some bugs and settings that change between versions. If something breaks, please.

What it can do:

• Choose Spotify or Apple Music (the iOS Music system player); optional crossfade / AutoMix lyric transitions.
• Lyrics that follow the singer word by word, with the same smooth animations as the desktop extension. In duets each singer gets their own side, backing vocals sit under the main line, and instrumental breaks show three bouncing dots.

versions.localizedDescription: • README: sharper iPad clip, iPad and TV side by side.

apps.name: colon3
apps.subtitle: iOS music player with Soulseek support
apps.localizedDescription:
colon3 (:3):

A native Soulseek client and music player for iOS. Search the Soulseek network, download straight to the phone, and play from a local library. No server or desktop client in between.

• Library: albums and loose songs in a 2-column grid, A–Z side scrubber, Songs, Artists and Playlists views, favourites, multi-select, and import from Files or other apps.
• Playlists: your own (reorder, rename, .m3u8 import/export), plus Favorite Songs and Most Played.

• Player: Apple Music-style full screen with synced lyrics (a .lrc next to the song, else LRCLIB), queue editing, shuffle and repeat, playback speed, AirPlay, and the Liquid Glass mini player on iOS 26+.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

• Import from Apple Music: the same for playlists in the Music app on your iPhone.
• Playback speed: a speed button in Now Playing opens a bar from 0.5× to 2× that snaps to common speeds. Pitch stays natural, and the speed is remembered.

Fixed:

• Software Update: Install Update now opens the install page and starts the iOS install prompt straight away, instead of trying an in-app install that iOS blocks.

apps.name: q2repro
apps.subtitle: Quake II for iPhone & Apple Vision Pro — full campaign, re-release content, and a stereoscopic 3D mode. Built on q2repro
apps.localizedDescription:
Quake II (q2repro) for iPhone & Apple Vision Pro:

Play Quake II on your iPhone and Apple Vision Pro — the full campaign, both mission packs, the 2023 re-release content, Action Quake II, and a stereoscopic 3D mode on Vision Pro that puts the game on a floating screen in your room with real depth. Or go all the way in with VR mode — step inside the level, aim with your hands, and play the whole campaign room-scale.

Built on q2repro (Paril's Q2PRO fork with Quake II re-release support), rendering natively on Metal via ANGLE. 100% vibe coded with lots of passion and attention to detail.

versions.localizedDescription:
visionOS VR (immersive 3D):

• Hand tracking, aim reticle and wheel cursor for the immersive mode.
• Per-eye lighting fixes: the "wall dark in one eye" bug (partial UBO update on the Metal backend) and stale dynamic-light bits.
• Layer-rate pacing and a GPU frame timer; Render Quality defaults to 1.5.
• VR settings sheet: HUD Size / Height / Spread (defaults 1.20 / -0.20 / 1.4), Menu Panel Size, FPS counter.
• Boot config and HUD scale overlay; ffmpeg zero-size packet fix for cinematics.

Build:

• Clean-clone bootstrap fixes: libcurl script on stock bash 3.2, q2proto submodule now initialised.
• Public builds compile out the dev remote console and fault-injection commands.

IPAs: q2repro-1.1.0-iOS.ipa, q2repro-1.1.0-visionOS.ipa (dev-signed; install via SideStore/AltStore or your own signing).

apps.name: Stratagus
apps.subtitle: Warcraft II (Wargus) on iOS, running the Stratagus
apps.localizedDescription:
Stratagus for iOS:

Warcraft II (Wargus) on iOS, running the Stratagus engine. Single-player and local-network multiplayer are playable: touch + gesture controls, on-screen keyboard, and saves visible in the Files app.

Bring your own Warcraft II: Battle.net Edition files — the app ships no game data. On first launch you get an import screen: put the files somewhere the Files app can reach (iCloud Drive, On My iPhone, or a USB drive), tap Import, and pick a folder containing either:

• Already-extracted data — a folder holding Install.mpq and the Support/ folder (e.g. extracted earlier on a PC). This skips the unpack step.

versions.localizedDescription:
Warcraft II (Wargus) on iOS — single-player and local-network multiplayer.

Install: sideload the .ipa with SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, or TrollStore. Bring your own Warcraft II data (GOG/CD) — import it on first launch. See more, including touch controls and multiplayer details in the README.

Note: LAN auto-discovery requires signing with a PAID Apple Developer account (the multicast entitlement). Free account sideloads can still play multiplayer — use "Add server" in Join Local Game to enter the host's IP manually.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Wargus uses your local network to host and find nearby multiplayer games.

apps.name: KartPad
apps.subtitle: Mario Kart Wii and Retro Rewind, native for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and Android
apps.localizedDescription:
KartPad:

KartPad builds on WiiCompiled, the original Mario Kart Wii static recompilation project created by patchzyy. WiiCompiled provides the foundational translator and runtime; KartPad maintains the Apple and Android integration, native controls, game chooser, game-data management, packaging, and releases. The projects are independently maintained.

Bring your own game data. KartPad requires a legally obtained supported PAL RMCP01 revision 0 Mario Kart Wii image. tvOS remains experimental.

AI disclosure: KartPad uses substantial AI assistance for code, tests, documentation, debugging and maintenance. Some support replies and maintenance tasks are automated. There is no audited percentage of AI-generated code. Build, test and device records describe what was checked. This disclosure concerns KartPad's workflow, not the authorship of its upstream projects.

Get KartPad:

KartPad is free. On Android, download it from the.

versions.localizedDescription:
KartPad 0.8.3 (build 265) supports Retro Rewind 6.13.3.

Changed:

• iPhone and iPad: the game chooser shows Update needed for an older installed Retro Rewind pack instead of Ready to play; Set Up Game then updates it in the app.
• Runtime: every platform gains the double-precision fused floating-point operations the new Retro Rewind code uses. Without them the game code could not be built.

Checked and remaining limits:

Android emulator: the signed release app installed over 0.8.2 with all 6,082 app files unchanged. The in-app installer replaced Retro Rewind 6.13.1 with 6.13.3 from the official download. Retro Rewind and Original both reached races that were driven past the first minute with no crash markers; the existing license loaded, and Retro WFC signed in ("Welcome to Retro WFC").

iPhone 14: the private 0.8.3 build installed in place over 0.8.2 after a verified backup; saves, licenses and settings were unchanged, and the chooser showed Update needed for the phone's older Retro Rewind pack. Gameplay on the iPhone was not driven in this check.

Mac: PadMint's clean player check (Apple Python 3.9, empty PadMint folder) built 0.8.3 with the new setup step; the packaged app passed its audit and deep signature check.

Not checked: online races on 6.13.3, physical Android phones, iPhone gameplay, and performance. No FPS change is claimed.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: KartPad connects to your selected private Wii server and other players on your local network.

apps.name: Super Smash Flash 2
apps.subtitle: Unofficial Super Smash Flash 2 iPhone and iPad port with offline Ruffle runtime, customizable touch controls and gamepad support
apps.localizedDescription:
Super Smash Flash 2 for iOS:

An unofficial iPhone and iPad port of Super Smash Flash 2 v1.3.1.2 (Portable), running its original Flash game through Ruffle inside a native iOS app. The game and runtime are bundled for offline play, with a matching touch control deck, controller support, and a customizable layout.

If you want to support me and remain up-to-date about this and other projects, you can in different ways:

Ko-Fi: https://ko-fi.com/dev_zer0

YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@develop_erZ

Features:

• A touch control deck styled around SSF2: an eight-direction D-pad, jump, attack, special, shield, grab, taunt, pause, and Start / OK.
• Simultaneous touch inputs, diagonal movement, touch feedback, and adjustable control size and opacity.
• Customizable touch layouts: move, resize, and hide controls, with separate layouts for portrait and landscape.

versions.localizedDescription:
Adds the missing game-input bindings and dedicated C-stick controls.

• KEYS and controller action menus now include C-Up, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, Jump 2, Shield 2 and Dash. Key bindings may also be left unassigned.
• The right stick defaults to the four C actions, using T / F / G / H for up / left / down / right. A diagonal tilt selects one C direction. Old unassigned right-stick defaults migrate once; existing custom action and key mappings remain.
• Adds an adjustable stick dead zone with threshold hysteresis and optional left-stick-strength walk/dash control. Light tilt sends movement; above 75% horizontal tilt adds Dash. This provides two speed levels rather than continuous analog movement.

Set up C-stick attacks:

In the game's Options → Controls → P1, bind C-Up = T, C-Left = F, C-Down = G, C-Right = H. These slots initially show n/a and must be assigned in the game too. Select each slot and tilt the corresponding right-stick direction to assign it. If your port controller settings previously used Attack on the right stick, change those mappings to the corresponding C actions in CONTROLS → CONTROLLER.

For optional walk/dash, bind the game's Dash to Shift, disable Auto-Dash and D-Tap Dash, then enable Left-stick strength controls walk / dash in the port. To assign an n/a slot on iPhone, map a controller button to that action, select the slot in the game, and press that button.

The portable Flash movie disables its desktop controller initialization. The iOS port still uses a GameController-to-keyboard bridge, so the in-game device list remains Keyboard. Native XInput and continuous analog movement are not enabled by this update.

Download SuperSmashFlash2-1.1.9-unsigned.ipa, sign it and install it. Keep the same signing identity and bundle identifier (com.devz.supersmashflash2) to retain your data.

apps.name: Robo-Boy
apps.subtitle: A web application for controlling ROS 2 robots, tailored for mobile usage
apps.localizedDescription:
Robo-Boy:

Robo-Boy is a web, desktop, iPhone, and Android interface for controlling and visualizing ROS 2 robots. It includes camera streaming, configurable control pads, 3D visualization, native time-series plotting and signal analysis, behavior-tree editing, and custom themes. All interfaces run the same React codebase and connect to a separately installed ROS stack. The mobile packages are lightweight Tauri shells; the desktop can be built either as one of those or as an Electron shell, which is larger but brings its own Chromium and so has WebRTC wherever it runs.

Start With The App:

The shortest route. The app needs only the ROS services, so there is no certificate to create and no proxy to run.

• Start the ROS services on the computer that runs ROS:.

versions.localizedDescription:
Features:

• robot control ownership and observer services, plus camera and assistant launcher fixes (7b10a3b).

apps.name: mLabeler
apps.subtitle: Cross-platform editor for singing voice labels: phonemes, notes, pitch and UTAU oto. Works with DiffSinger datasets, supports automatic labeling. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS

versions.localizedDescription: Quick labelling: the built-in MCFL model (13 languages) right in the app, no toolkit, on computers (Windows 7 included) and phones; language picker next to the button. Boundary refinement now uses the built-in model, no toolkit; removed from auto-labeling. Auto-labeling: multilingual WFL-ASR models (several languages in one song), model authors, filter by model kind, Whisper recognition errors shown in the window. Auto-labeling model comparison: PER, boundary errors, speed, charts; without phonemes, with the labels' phonemes or both; aligners via Whisper + G2P. Unsure phoneme check with percent and threshold (off by default); a manual edit clears the mark. Sound editing: spectrogram brush with a soft edge. Dataset summary: phoneme chart. Settings: all sections expanded, Expand all / Collapse all. Phones: scale button on by default, pinch no longer grabs boundaries.

privacy.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: mLabeler records samples for voicebanks and datasets.

apps.name: DSH Tether
apps.subtitle: Mobile client for the DeepSeek Harness — use the dsh on your dev machine from your Android or iOS phone, remotely across networks, peer-to-peer over iroh with no server to set up (falls back to a relay that only sees ciphertext)
apps.localizedDescription:
DSH Tether carries the DeepSeek Harness web interface to your phone over a direct peer-to-peer connection. The agent keeps running on the machine your code lives on, and the phone gets DSH's own full interface — conversations, tool calls, approvals and settings, not a reimplementation of them. Pair once with a 6-digit code; after that the two ends find each other whatever network they are on.

When there is no machine around, the same app can run DSH on the phone itself (Android) — see Local mode.

The case it solves:

You are not on your machine's network, and you do not want a server in the middle.

An extremely fast seed finder for Shattered Pixel Dungeon, written in Rust — with native apps for Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows.

apps.localizedDescription:
Raw data capture ·.

First launch on macOS. NOOP is not notarized by Apple — notarization needs a paid Apple Developer ID tied to a real identity, which doesn't fit an anonymous, free project. The app is sandboxed and ad-hoc code-signed, and the full source is here to inspect. Because it isn't notarized, macOS Gatekeeper blocks it on first open (you may see "damaged" or "unverified developer" — that's the download quarantine flag, not real damage). To open it, do one of these once:

• Terminal (most reliable): drag NOOP.app to Applications, then run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/NOOP.app and open NOOP normally.

versions.localizedDescription:
Rolling latest testing build — refreshed in place, so this tag is always the newest. NOOP main + ryanbr's open PRs + vetted community PRs, built with the NOOP Staging identity. Android and macOS install beside the official app; the iOS ipa carries the production bundle id, so it replaces an installed official app and uses its data. Filenames carry the base app version (v12.1.0).

• Android (debug) — NOOP-android-debug-v12.1.0.apk — debuggable build. com.noop.whoop.debug.
• macOS — NOOP-macos-v12.1.0.zip — unzip, then right-click → Open (ad-hoc signed, not notarized; Gatekeeper warns once). If it says "damaged", run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/NOOP.app.
• iOS — NOOP-ios-unsigned-v12.1.0.ipa — sideload via AltStore / Sideloadly (re-signs on-device). Replaces an installed official app (production bundle id, shared data), so back up first if you have one. Embedded watch app stripped, widget extension retained for Home/Lock-Screen widgets and Live Activities.

Base app version 12.1.0 · built 2026-10-15 · 8e4b0c1.

apps.localizedDescription:
Ozen (the word means "ear") turns what the people around you say into large, steady captions on your phone, as they speak. It was built for one grandmother with hearing loss, who found every existing transcription app either unreliable with external microphones or too shallow to trust.

• Captions that hold still. Words settle in place instead of jumping around, and a name shows who is talking.
• Private by design. No account and no company server: nothing leaves the phone unless you choose to send it.
• Alerts she won't miss. The doorbell, a smoke alarm or her own name makes the phone buzz, even in a pocket; alarms flash the whole screen.
• Talk back. Type a reply and the phone says it out loud, or shows it in huge letters.

apps.name: Shalielie
apps.subtitle: This is a personal repo for porting new Photographic Styles in iPhone to older model below 15
apps.localizedDescription:
Photographic Style Port:

Current version: v0.7.0.

This is an experimental tool that takes a HEIC from an iPhone older than the iPhone 16 (iPhone 15, 14, 13 … — any model whose photos match a supported tile layout) and adds the metadata an iPhone 16/17 photo carries, so that Apple Photos offers the Photographic Styles palette on it (风格 in Chinese; Apple calls the palette 调色板).

Since v0.5 it also adds the iOS 27 Texture/Grain controls (质感/颗粒) that Apple introduced with the iPhone 18 Pro. Ported photos get them as part of the port; native iPhone 16/17 photos get only these controls, and their existing image data stays byte-identical.

versions.localizedDescription:
The first public build of Shalielie (瞎咧咧), the iPhone app version of Photographic Style Port. It adds iPhone 16/17 Photographic Styles (and iOS 27 Texture & Grain) to photos from older iPhones, right on the phone.

Pre-release. Unsigned IPA for sideloading (Sideloadly, AltStore), which signs it with your own Apple ID. Keep originals.

What's in it:

• Library, Albums, Backup Bin and Settings tabs. Add a style to photos in your library, saved as new photos or replacing the original (the original goes to the Backup Bin first and can be restored).
• Live Photos keep their motion. The app gives the video the style tracks and timed metadata Photos' editor needs on iOS 27, so a styled Live Photo opens in Edit with Style, Texture and Grain, and the video changes with the style.
• Import HEIC (and MOV) Files… from the Files app; a HEIC that already has a style is saved as is, with its video.
• Shortcuts action "Add Photographic Style".

Credits:

Live Photo support is (#7): on-device video styling with VideoToolbox, the iOS 27 video template, and the import fix for styled photos without Texture & Grain. Thank you!

Tested:

• iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0: Live Photos from an iPhone 13 imported from Files; Photos' editor opens them, Style and Texture present, video restyled (@lzh20025).
• iPhone 15 Pro, iOS 27.0.1: still photos, save as new and replace.
• Not yet tested on a phone: picking a Live Photo in the library, Replace mode for Live Photos, the Shortcuts action on Live Photos, Texture added to iPhone 16/17 Live Photos.
